grades.justification: COUNTS. Rules: 108 MUST/SHOULD bullets in total. 68 are correct, 12 are implemented differently (#13 seek bar, #16 queue placement, #20/#24 top bar, #21 bar reveal, #26 popover anchor, #33 right-click menu, #41 sidebar position, #48 Playback tab, #50 overlay vs push, #66 music placeholder, #90 Settings window), 25 are partial, 2 are missing (#30 click-outside/Esc/animation to close the popover, #77 launch to Home) and 1 is a stub (#57 Edit Audio Tracks). Screens: 72 in total. 42 are done, 29 are partial (S01 S04 S05 S08 S09 S11 S13 S14 S15 S16 S17 S20 S21 S22 S29 S30 S31 S35 S40 S43 S48 S51 S52 S53 S57 S61 S62 S66 S68), 0 are missing and 1 is a stub (S27 OpenSubtitles). GRADES. Completeness 66: almost every surface exists and is wired to the engine. But the launch flow, the popover dismissal and several MUST details are absent or stubbed. Fidelity 55: the gallery mostly looks right, but the real window differs in the core player chrome. The top bar renders as two rows, video seek bars become waveforms, panels push the video instead of floating over it, the popover sits vertically centered, the right-click menu is plain native, and the volume OSD is duplicated. Code quality 62: there is a clean protocol/model split, display-link playhead and tests. But gallery-only specimens hide runtime divergence, there are no panel transitions, seeks are not coalesced, preferences are dead or transient, views contain literal sizes, and ScrollView hacks break layout.

doneWell: The ⋯ app menu content matches Figma menu.png row for row, including the final order (Open File(s) … Convert, Open Recent, divider, Profile (Movies), Keyboard Shortcuts, Customize Player, Settings, About), two-tone icons and dim shortcuts (S07 is REVIEW with only tiny deltas). Keep PlayerMenus.swift MXRAppMenuView.
Music now-playing (S34) is faithful: blurred enlarged backdrop, 738 pt cover with glow, 'title - artist', ±15 s buttons, waveform with a 4 pt thumb, and a separate music control-bar layout.
Volume cone: the Figma vector paths, nonlinear fill (100% at 63 of 88 pt), boost to 200% and sRGB gradient are reproduced exactly (all C.VolumeCone/* variants).
Per-show presets work as intended. Choosing or creating a preset assigns it to the show or folder, and it is applied automatically when the next episode starts (AppModel.swift:184-198, 354-355).
Track popover content: Embedded / External / Output Device with refresh, orange ✓, picking does not close, Show Preferences opens the matching sidebar tab, and the bar icon fills orange while open.

Settings is catalog-driven across 13 categories with App/Media/System groups, an inline Advanced Options bar, a click-to-open ⓘ popover, dependent rows disabled through enabledWhen, plain-word dropdowns, and live theme and accent changes.
Customize Player: tile grid, drag-in and drag-out, Save becomes primary on change, Cancel reverts, and the two-row alternate layout model (S67). Only the edit-mode bar rendering (CMP-13) is wrong.
Continue-watching toast: centred above the bar, bold time, orange Continue, ✕, the seek bar previews the resume span, and a 5 s timeout.

Library: compact rail with Home…Recent, pins and +, breadcrumb collapsing to '…', Unwatched/Watched First sorts, watched dimming with a progress line, now-playing orange with ▶, drag from library to queue, and a draggable mini player with corner snap and queue expansion.
Bookmarks and Chapters tabs: chapter number in orange, clicking seeks, one-shortcut bookmark without a dialog. The OSD shows the action plus 'Pressed X'.

Native platform behaviour is respected in many places: NSOpenPanel, engine dialogs as NSAlert sheets, a menu bar mirror including Hide UI, PiP and media keys, and a CADisplayLink that refreshes only the playhead.
Unsupported engine features are mostly labelled rather than faking success (reverse playback, OpenSubtitles), although that sometimes hides designed controls entirely.

findings.title: Every local video gets a waveform 'tick-mark' seek bar instead of the thick solid bar (Show Waveform defaults ON and applies to video)
findings.designEvidence: VIDEO_BREAKDOWN §02 MUST: the seek bar is thick (black track, dark accent fill, orange capsule playhead) – Player-6.png 247:445, Controls 1908:7387. §09 MUST: the waveform appears only 'when Show Waveform on Seekbar is on' (music view, 12m56.6). Key frame 07-sidebar__playback-tab-full-toggles__09m17.5s shows 'Show Waveform on Seekbar' OFF by default.
findings.actual: InterfaceModel.swift:161 sets `showWaveform = true`. MXRSeekBar draws WaveformShape whenever samples exist (PlayerControls.swift:326-341) and switches to the 4 pt music playhead (:327). The bridge analyses the audio track of any AVAsset, including MP4 video (module/bridge/MXRAudioServices.m:273-288). So every local video shows dense vertical bars; Codex's own gallery render S13.Player/osd shows this over a video. The toggle that would turn it off is buried in an invented 'Display' expander (SettingsSidebar.swift:123-124) and is not persisted.
findings.fix: Default showWaveform to false. Draw the waveform only when the user enabled it, and by default only for audio-only media. Keep the 8 pt video playhead for video. Put the toggle back as row 2 of the Playback tab and persist it (preset or profile).
findings.verifyNote:
Confirmed.
- InterfaceModel.swift:161 sets showWaveform = true.
- MXRAudioServices.m:135 advertises supportsWaveform = YES, and readWaveform (:265-288) decodes the first audio track of any local AVAsset, MP4 included.
- Key frame 09m17.5 shows the toggle OFF.
- The gallery hid the bug: AppGallery.swift:73 and PlayerGallery.swift:36-72 force showWaveform=false for video. S13.Player/osd, which does not force it, renders the tick-mark bar over the cat video.
- Extra cost: every media change decodes the whole audio track through AVAssetReader, which breaks the 'as fast as stock VLC' goal.
- CODEX_STATUS claims waveforms only for audio files. That is false.

findings.title: Real window shows two rows: an empty titlebar strip with the traffic lights, then the 40 pt top bar with the cone indented by an unused 76 pt reserve
findings.designEvidence: §03 MUST: one thin top row. §03 SHOULD (macOS): native traffic lights inside a full-size-content title bar. D007/D019: a single shared 40 pt top bar. Player-6.png: cone at x=16 in the single row.
findings.actual: MXRAppController.swift:64-79 creates a .fullSizeContentView window with a transparent titlebar and NSHostingView. Nothing in Sources calls .ignoresSafeArea() or sets safeAreaRegions, so SwiftUI insets all content below the 28 pt titlebar safe area. Meanwhile the ShapeStyle background (MXRAppView.swift:119 `.background(Theme.Color.bgA1)`) bleeds into that strip, which then reads as a separate title row. MXRTopBar also prepends a 76 pt clear spacer for traffic lights (PlayerBars.swift:18, PlayerMetrics.swift:38) in a row that no longer contains them, so the cone is indented. The traffic lights are never re-centred in the 40 pt bar. The gallery hides all of this because it renders with reservesTrafficLights=false and no titlebar.
findings.fix: Apply .ignoresSafeArea() to the root scene (or hostingView.safeAreaRegions = []). Vertically centre the standard window buttons in the 40 pt bar (reposition them in windowDidResize, or use an empty NSToolbar with .unifiedCompact). Keep the 76 pt reserve only in that same row. Check the result in the real window, not the gallery.
findings.verifyNote:
Confirmed, and it matches C3.
- Nothing in Sources calls ignoresSafeArea or sets safeAreaRegions. The NSHostingView in the fullSizeContentView window therefore lays the scene out below the ~28 pt titlebar safe area.
- ShapeStyle backgrounds bleed into that strip. The strip takes the colour of whichever root background touches the top edge: bgA3 at MXRPlayerView PlayerView.swift:83, or bgA1 at MXRAppView.swift:115 (not :119).
- The 76 pt reserve (PlayerBars.swift:18) also stays in native fullscreen, where there are no traffic lights, so the cone is indented there too.
- The strip and traffic lights also stay in Hide UI (S06), where the design shows the video only.
- The gallery hides all of this because MXRAppView is created without reservesTrafficLights.

findings.title: Track popover floats vertically centred mid-right, has no enter/exit animation, and cannot be closed by clicking outside (a click pauses the video instead)
findings.designEvidence: §04 MUST: the popover is 'anchored at the bottom right above the bar'. Native key frame 04-track-popover__subtitles-tab-external-tracks-native__06m21.7s: the popover's bottom edge sits about 20 pt above the control bar. §04 SHOULD: clicking outside or pressing Esc closes it; a short fade or slide is fine.
findings.actual: MXRAppView.swift:52 and :84 use `.overlay(alignment: .trailing)`, which centres the panel vertically. The S14.App/subtitle-tracks render puts it at y≈271–795 of 1080; the design has it at about 485–1005. No panel has any .transition or .animation (grep finds none in Panels/ or MXRAppView). The ⋯ menu, by contrast, opens as an animated NSPopover (PlayerBars.swift:212-213), so the two behave inconsistently. Esc only works through `.onExitCommand` (TrackPopover.swift:19), which needs focus inside the panel. A click on the video runs the default 'playPause' click action (MXRAppController.swift:205-209, MXRNativePreferences.swift:54), so it pauses playback instead of dismissing the panel. The only way to close is re-clicking the bar icon.
findings.fix: Use .bottomTrailing alignment with bottom padding = panelInset above the control bar. Give all right panels a short opacity+move(edge:.bottom) transition that respects Reduce Motion. While a popover is open, add a transparent click-catcher over the video that closes it and swallows the click. Route Esc to closeRightPanel in the key monitor before shortcuts run.
findings.verifyNote:
Confirmed.
- MXRAppView.swift:52/84 use .overlay(alignment: .trailing). The S14.App render puts the popover at y≈271–795. Key frame 06m21.7 has it at ≈485–1005, about 20 pt above the bar.
- No panel has a transition. Esc works only through .onExitCommand (TrackPopover.swift:19).
- A click on the video runs the default click-action 'playPause' (MXRNativePreferences.swift:54, MXRAppController.swift:205-209), so clicking outside pauses instead of closing.
- This is the root cause of C2 and of half of C4.

findings.title: Queue and settings sidebar push and shrink the video into a separate gutter column ('window inside a window') instead of floating over the video
findings.designEvidence: §07 SHOULD: the sidebar overlays the right side of the video and does not push or shrink it. §02 MUST: a floating queue panel at the right of the video. Design principle 5 (never leave the video). Native frames 08-library__queue-panel-native__09m30.1s and 13-bookmarks-chapters-osd__chapters-tab-native__15m16.7s show the panel inside a full-width video frame. §07 MUST: same width and position as the popover.
findings.actual: MXRAppView.swift:93-98 (`if reservesPanelSpace`) puts MXRRightPanelView in an HStack beside the video canvas, at up to 48% of the window width (panelWidth, :182-183), with its own bgA1 gutter and insets. The video is cut at x≈1490 and re-centred (S22.App/queue and S20.App/subtitle-settings renders), so the panel looks like a nested window. In a 1320 pt window it takes 400 pt plus gutters. The track popover overlays while the queue and sidebar push, so the three panels are not in the same position. The invented 'Expand Settings' group in the Playback tab adds to the window-in-window look.
findings.fix: Overlay the sidebar and queue on the video's trailing edge inside the video frame, full height between the bars, with panelInset – the same overlay as the popover. Never shrink the video; at small widths let the panel cover more of it.
findings.verifyNote:
Confirmed against Figma.
- The Queue frame 463:831 is a child of Controls 491:1781 at (1500,-966). It sits over the full-width Frame 312 video and does not reserve a column.
- MXRAppView.swift:93-98 puts the queue and sidebar in an HStack gutter. The S20.App and S22.App renders show the video frame cut at x≈1490, with the panel in its own bgA1 column.
- Show Preferences switches from the overlaid popover to the pushing sidebar, so the video jumps.
- This is the root cause of C5.

findings.title: Scrubbing issues one engine seek per mouse event (no coalescing), so the picture lands only every few seconds and the elapsed label does not follow the drag
findings.designEvidence: §02 MUST: 'While dragging, the elapsed label follows'. Thumbnail preview while seeking (03m29.3). The thick seek bar is meant to be easy to scrub.
findings.actual: Every DragGesture.onChanged (PlayerControls.swift:363-364 → seek(at:) :434-440) calls player.seek(toPosition:, .fast), which runs vlc_player_SeekByPos/Time synchronously per event (MXRServicesBridge.m:626-628). VLC flushes and restarts decoding for each one, so a frame only appears when the pointer pauses. Each event also triggers a seek-preview thumbnail request (preview(at:) :439) that competes with the decoder. MXRTimeLabel shows app.clock.displayTime, the engine time (:84), so the label lags and jumps instead of following the pointer.
findings.fix: Throttle seeks: keep one in flight and send the latest target when the timer's on_seek completion arrives, or at most every ~100 ms. Show dragPosition in the elapsed label during the drag. Debounce thumbnail requests. Do the precise seek only on release.
findings.verifyNote:
Confirmed.
- Each DragGesture.onChanged in PlayerControls.swift:363-364 calls seek(at:) and then player.seek(toPosition:.fast). That goes straight to vlc_player_SeekByPos, at MXRServicesBridge.m:631-634 (cited lines are slightly off), with no coalescing anywhere.
- preview(at:) also requests a new thumbnail on every event.
- MXRTimeLabel uses app.clock.displayTime (PlayerControls.swift:83), not dragPosition.
- VLC's own Qt SeekSlider throttles seeks with a timer for this reason.
- This is the root cause of C6.

findings.title: Two volume indicators: VLC's own vout OSD 'Volume: N%' (top-right, VLC font) plus the cone tooltip, updating out of sync
findings.designEvidence: Figma audio value.png 2245:9805: a single volume chip above the cone. Principle 6: one place per function. §13: on-screen feedback is the designed in-app OSD.
findings.actual: setVolume calls vlc_player_aout_SetVolume (MXRServicesBridge.m:601-603). The core 'volume' callback (src/player/aout.c:94) then calls vlc_player_osd_Volume (src/player/osd.c:156-172), which draws 'Volume: %ld%%' into the video on every change. Separately, MXRVolumeTooltip (PlayerControls.swift:253-266) shows the model value after the asynchronous bridge round trip. The result is two indicators in two places with different timing.
findings.fix: Without touching the engine, set the inherited 'osd' variable to false on the player/vouts and route all feedback through MXRPlayerOSD, which already supports text plus pressed key. Have the tooltip show the local drag value immediately.
findings.verifyNote:
Confirmed engine path: setVolume → vlc_player_aout_SetVolume → the aout 'volume' callback (src/player/aout.c:94) → vlc_player_osd_Volume → 'Volume: %ld%%' drawn top-right in the vout. That drawing is gated by var 'osd' (video_text.c:99).
- The fix is fine, but it is wider than volume: no engine OSD text ever reaches the designed OSD. See MISS-01.
- This explains C7.

findings.title: Volume chip shows a square, accent-coloured outline after click or drag (system focus ring)
findings.designEvidence: audio value.png 2245:9805: a borderless translucent chip with an outside shadow. No element in the design has a focus outline.
findings.actual: MXRVolumeCone applies `.focusable()` (PlayerControls.swift:179), as do the seek bar (:413) and the customisation tiles (MXRCustomizationView.swift palette). On macOS 14+ a click or drag focuses the view, and AppKit draws a rectangular focus ring in the user's accent colour (purplish with a purple accent) around the cone and tooltip area. Secondary suspect: the hairline left by the PlayerOutsideShadow destinationOut mask edge plus the .hudWindow NSVisualEffectView behind the rounded tint (MXRBackdropSurface).
findings.fix: Add .focusEffectDisabled() to the cone and seek bar but keep their onKeyPress handling, and draw a design-consistent indicator only for keyboard focus. Confirm in the real window.
findings.verifyNote:
Plausible, not proven.
- .focusable() is on the cone (PlayerControls.swift:179) and the seek bar (:413), and .focusEffectDisabled() is used nowhere.
- On macOS 14+ a clicked focusable view draws a rectangular focus ring in the system accent colour, which fits 'purplish square outline'.
- But the seek bar has the same modifier and the owner reported no ring there. The gallery C.VolumeTooltip render is clean. The secondary suspect is still possible: the NSVisualEffectView inside MXRBackdropSurface may not be clipped by SwiftUI clipShape.
- The fixer must reproduce this in the real window before choosing the fix.

findings.title: Launch shows a blank cone 'Open a media file' screen; the full-window library on Home is never the start screen, and the 'Start in compact mode' setting is ignored
findings.designEvidence: §11 MUST: 'When there is nothing to resume, launching VLC opens the full-window library on Home, never a blank cone screen'. Player-5.png 6261:15078. Principle 8 and the 13m57 narration ('Home replaces the start screen').
findings.actual: InterfaceModel.swift:143 defaults to `library = .hidden`, and nothing selects .full or .home at startup; showFullLibrary is reachable only by command. PlayerView.swift:147-154 renders the cone and 'Open a media file' button. AppModel+Preferences.swift:47-49 `startsInCompactMode` (option macosx-redesign-compact-start, Settings › Interface) is never read anywhere, so that toggle does nothing.
findings.fix: At startup with an empty queue and no resume prompt, set library = .full and select .home. Read startsInCompactMode to choose between the compact and full library.
findings.verifyNote:
Confirmed.
- library defaults to .hidden (InterfaceModel.swift:143), and nothing sets .full at startup.
- startsInCompactMode (AppModel+Preferences.swift:47-49) is never read.
- The option text in MXRAppOptions.inc:16 ('Opens with the library hidden and only the player visible') and Figma Settings–Interface 3046:10057 ('Start in compact mode' OFF) both imply that the default start is the full library on Home.
- PlayerView.swift:147-154 draws the cone and 'Open a media file' instead.

findings.title: Right-click menu on the video is a plain native text menu; the Figma-styled version exists only as a gallery specimen
findings.designEvidence: §05 MUST: the context menu is 'cleaned up and restyled' – rows with a two-tone icon, a dim right-aligned shortcut and submenu chevrons. Figma right-click menu.png 6065:13616; frame 05-menus__right-click-menu-cleaned__05m23.0s.
findings.actual: PlayerView.swift:64 `.contextMenu { MXRVideoContextMenuContent() }` produces NSMenu rows with no icons and no shortcut column (PlayerMenus.swift:187-216). MXRVideoContextMenuView (PlayerMenus.swift:70-105) matches Figma but is used only by the gallery entry S09.ContextMenu. The visual check passes while users never see it.
findings.fix: Give the native NSMenuItems the two-tone template images and keyEquivalent display (keeping native keyboard behaviour), or present the Figma view in a borderless panel at the click point with arrow-key navigation.
findings.verifyNote:
Confirmed.
- PlayerMenus.swift:68-69 says MXRVideoContextMenuView is a gallery specimen. The real right-click menu is MXRVideoContextMenuContent: native rows with no icons and no shortcut column.
- Checkmarks are faked by appending the text " ✓" to titles (PlayerMenus.swift:225, 233, 237, 287, 311, 313) instead of setting the native menu-item state.
- Shortcuts are not shown either, against principle 14.

findings.title: Playback tab differs from the design: Reverse removed, Waveform and Metadata hidden in an invented 'Expand Settings' group, Metadata is a button, no slider ticks, nothing persisted
findings.designEvidence: Key frame 09m17.5 (corrections #1): Show Subtitle Timeline, Show Waveform, Show Metadata, Reverse (all toggles, OFF), then Sleep Timer, Audio Visualizer, Speed. Figma 5187:24308: Subtitle Timeline, Statistics, Reverse, Sleep Timer, Visualizer, Speed with tick marks, and no expander.
findings.actual: SettingsSidebar.swift:101-127: Reverse is deleted (comment cites D014) instead of shown disabled with ⓘ. Show Waveform and Show Metadata are inside PanelExpand('Display'), and Show Metadata is a plain-text Button that opens a sheet. Statistics prints unstyled caption rows (:128-135). The speed slider has no tick marks (compare the S17 render with the Figma crop). The preset footer is hidden on this tab (:33). The toggles live in transient InterfaceModel state and reset on relaunch.
findings.fix: Restore the designed rows, order and toggles. Show Reverse disabled with an explanation. Make Metadata a toggle that shows a metadata overlay. Add slider ticks. Persist the toggles. Remove the invented expander.
findings.verifyNote:
Confirmed against Figma 5187:24308.
- Figma has Subtitle Timeline, Statistics, Reverse, Sleep Timer, Visualizer, and Speed with tick marks. Key frame 09m17.5 adds Waveform and Metadata.
- The S17 render has no Reverse row and no slider ticks, and adds an 'Expand Settings' group.
- The toggles are transient InterfaceModel state.
- Correction: hiding the preset footer on the Playback tab matches Figma, since the Playback crop has no footer. Drop that sub-claim.

findings.title: Top and bottom bars reveal and hide together, with a 0.5 s delay, instead of independently and immediately
findings.designEvidence: §03 MUST: bars show and hide independently – pointer near the top reveals only the top bar (03m51.0), near the bottom only the control bar (03m53.0) – and hide right after the pointer leaves. Corrections #5.
findings.actual: PlayerView.swift:30-31 and :96-106 feed `nearTop || nearBottom` into the single flag interface.areBarsVisible, which drives both bars. The hide delay defaults to 0.5 s (AppModel+Preferences.swift:14). The windowed default 'In fullscreen only' matches Figma Settings – Interface (node 3055:10792), so keep that.
findings.fix: Keep separate topBarVisible and bottomBarVisible states driven by their own hover zones. Hide at the 'Hide after' value with a 0 default and a 120–150 ms fade.
findings.verifyNote:
The joint reveal is confirmed: nearTop || nearBottom feeds one flag (PlayerView.swift:96-106).
Correct the fix, though:
- Figma Settings–Interface 3046:10057 shows the 'Hide after' slider at about 0.5 s, so the 0.5 s default (AppModel+Preferences.swift:14) is designed. Keep it.
- Separate only the top and bottom visibility states.

findings.title: External Tracks '+' opens a raw file picker; the Add Subtitles dialog is behind the pencil
findings.designEvidence: §04 MUST: '+ opens the Add Subtitles dialog (section 06)'. §06: 'Add (+) in the subtitles popover opens a dialog' with scope and source – the batch flow is the point of the feature.
findings.actual: TrackPopover.swift:62-63: the pencil calls present(.addSubtitles(.file,.computer)), while + calls ui.request(.addSubtitleFile), a bare NSOpenPanel. Folder and playlist matching is therefore hidden behind the edit icon.
findings.fix: Make + open Add Subtitles, defaulting to a folder scope when the media has a folder. Use the pencil to edit or remove external tracks.
findings.verifyNote:
Confirmed.
- At TrackPopover.swift:62-63, the pencil opens Add Subtitles and + calls ui.request(.addSubtitleFile). That opens a plain NSOpenPanel (MXRNativePresentations.swift:77-90).
- The §04 MUST is explicit that + opens Add Subtitles.

findings.title: In Customize mode the seek bar collapses to about 50 pt and overlaps the duration label, and items are outlined one by one instead of as groups
findings.designEvidence: Player - customize.png 2107:5604: the time + seek + duration group shares one dashed outline across the free width. §15 MUST: groups share one outline.
findings.actual: PlayerBars.swift:60-62 wraps each control row in ScrollView(.horizontal) while customising. That proposes unlimited width, so PlayerRowLayout gives the seek bar only its minimum (the play button's width). In the S66.App/customization render the seek bar is a stub overlapping '00:25:40', the right cluster shifts left, and each control has its own outline.
findings.fix: Drop the ScrollView and lay out at the real width. Draw one dashed outline per group (transport, time/seek/duration, volume, track buttons, queue).
findings.verifyNote:
Confirmed in the S66.App render.
- The seek bar is a stub at x≈255–290 overlapping '00:25:40', and the right cluster is pulled left.
- The top bar's fullscreen button lands at x≈1335 instead of the right edge.
- Figma 2107:5604 gives time+seek+duration one outline and speaker+cone one outline.
- Cause: the ScrollView(.horizontal) at PlayerBars.swift:60-62.
- The empty extra bottom row in that render comes from the gallery inserting a row, not from the app.

findings.title: Windows-style Ctrl shortcuts on macOS: menus show 'Ctrl + O', Settings is ⌃P (no ⌘,), Hide UI is ⌃\, Bookmark is ⌃B, and onboarding teaches Ctrl keys
findings.designEvidence: §05 SHOULD (macOS): map Ctrl to ⌘ in displayed shortcuts; Hide UI is ⌘\. §13: ⌘B on macOS. §14 SHOULD: Settings opens with ⌘,. §15 SHOULD: the onboarding shortcuts screen shows ⌘-based keys. PHILOSOPHY: native manners.
findings.actual: ShortcutValues.swift:186-202 binds the defaults Ctrl+O/F/N/D/C/V/R/S/P, Ctrl+\ and Ctrl+B. The app menu shows them (S07 render: 'Ctrl + O'). The native menu bar copies the bindings (MXRNativeMenus.swift:181), so File/Settings use ⌃ keys, and Ctrl+C/V are taken by Open Capture and Open from Clipboard.
findings.fix: Use macOS defaults: ⌘O, ⇧⌘O (folder), ⌘N (network), ⌘, (Settings), ⌘\ (Hide UI), ⌘B and so on. Render them with ⌘ glyphs in the menus, Keyboard Shortcuts and onboarding.
findings.verifyNote:
Confirmed. ShortcutValues.swift:186-202 defines the Ctrl bindings, MXRNativeMenus.swift:181 copies them into the menu bar, and there is no ⌘, anywhere. The S07 render shows 'Ctrl + O'.
One correction: ⌃C and ⌃V do not collide with macOS Copy/Paste, which are ⌘C and ⌘V. When mapping to ⌘, keep ⌘C and ⌘V for Copy/Paste and give Open Capture and Open from Clipboard other keys.

findings.title: Pressing Play with an empty queue leaves a sticky error card in the video, 'The play queue is empty or cannot start', with a native bordered 'Retry Playback' button that retries the same failing call
findings.designEvidence: Not a designed state. Principle 2 (quiet by default). §11: the empty state is Home. §10 OPEN: reuse Figma dialog components rather than native ones.
findings.actual: MXRServicesBridge.m:599 turns the failed vlc_playlist_Start into an error. It is stored as player.errorMessage and shown persistently in the video surface (PlayerView.swift:156-162) with `.buttonStyle(.bordered)`. The 'Retry Playback' button just calls play() again.
findings.fix: Disable Play, or open Home or the file panel, when the queue is empty. Show transient OSD text instead of a sticky card. Use Figma buttons for real playback errors and clear the error when new media loads.
findings.verifyNote:
Confirmed, but the root cause is wider than MXRServicesBridge.m:599.
- VLCPlayerBackend.send (VLCPlayerBackend.swift:139-147) stores ANY failed player command in commandError.
- PlayerModel exposes that as errorMessage, and PlayerView.swift:156-162 shows it as a sticky card with 'Retry Playback' calling play(). See MISS-03.
- Play is not disabled for an empty queue.
- The card is drawn in the same ZStack as the cone and 'Open a media file' button.

findings.title: Library header on Home says '0 items' above Continue Watching items; the compact Home also adds sections the design does not have
findings.designEvidence: Player-5.png: the header count reflects the library. Compact Home (key frame 11-playlists-home__home-compact-panel__13m47.2s) has only Continue Watching and Listen Again.
findings.actual: LibraryModel.swift:155 and :175 set totalCount = backend.mediaCount, the indexed media-library count, on Home. Continue Watching comes from history (MXRLibraryServices.m:294-295), so with no indexed folders the header shows '0 items' next to visible items. The compact Home renders extra sections – Frequently Visited Folders, Frequently Visited Playlists and Frequently Listened Artists (S28 render) – where the design shows only Continue Watching and Listen Again in the compact panel.
findings.fix: On Home, hide the count or count the entries shown. Limit the compact Home to the designed sections.
findings.verifyNote:
Partly refuted, so downgraded to minor.
- Figma compact Home 1106:5633 (sidebar.png) does include Frequently Visited Folders, Frequently Visited Playlists and Frequently Listened Artists. The 'extra sections' sub-claim is wrong.
- Figma's header says '110 items', the library total, so using backend.mediaCount (LibraryModel.swift:155/175) matches the design.
- The remaining bug is the edge case: with an empty media library, '0 items' sits above history-based Continue Watching items. Hide the count on Home when it is 0, or count the shown entries.

findings.title: Subtitle timeline mode in the real bar lacks the '*' window range labels and before/after-playhead cue dimming

findings.title: Subtitle 'Pixels' size mode and the invented 'Position' row are offered in the sidebar but rejected by the bridge; Settings marks the same features unavailable

findings.title: In-window 'Profile ›' and 'Open Recent ›' submenus are unstyled popovers; the Figma profile submenu appears only as a sheet from the menu bar

findings.title: Settings and every dialog are window-attached sheets, not centred modals or a separate Settings window, and dialogs are shrunk with scaleEffect on small screens
findings.designEvidence: §06 MUST: Add Subtitles is 'centered over the player' (06m02.5). §14 MUST: Settings is a large centred window; SHOULD: a separate window opened with ⌘,. §15 SHOULD: onboarding is a first-run window.
findings.actual: All AppSheet cases use `.sheet(item:)` (MXRAppView.swift:124), so they attach below the title bar and block the player. Settings, Keyboard Shortcuts and Onboarding are sheets. When the screen is smaller than the preferred size, other dialogs are scaled down as bitmaps with `.scaleEffect(scale)` (MXRAppView.swift:205-216), giving blurry, undersized text instead of a reflowed layout.

Confirmed, but downgraded to minor.

findings.title: ⋯ app menu and library menus appear inside system NSPopover bubbles with arrows; the queue sort menu is plain text with no ✓

findings.title: A library row has two different file menus: ⋯ shows the Figma list, right-click shows another native list

findings.title: 'Add to Playlist' is missing from the player's right-click › Playlist submenu

findings.title: In fullscreen, opening a panel or the library switches the scene from overlay bars to stacked bars, so the video jumps
findings.designEvidence: §03 MUST: in fullscreen the bars overlay the video and the video must not jump.

In fullscreen, opening any panel, including the subtitle popover used to switch tracks, swaps MXRPlayerView (overlay bars) for the VStack composition at MXRAppView.swift:39-102. The video shrinks by both bar heights, and the bars become pinned. That breaks a §03 MUST in a common action.

findings.title: OpenSubtitles source is hidden or replaced by an 'unavailable' message
findings.designEvidence: §06: source dropdown From Computer / From OpenSubtitles / From Link…. Add Subtitles to Playlist/Folder-3.png 1919:9278. OPEN: needs an API-key product decision.

findings.title: Missing artwork uses an orange note on a grey placeholder instead of the designed generic music art
findings.designEvidence: §09 SHOULD: with no cover art, use the generic music art (green note on dark green, as in the Home 'Listen Again' cards, Player-5.png).
findings.actual: MXRMediaArtwork falls back to MXRIcon(.music, tint: accentMain) on thumbPlaceholder (PlayerView.swift:295), so music without art shows a different glyph in the now-playing view.

findings.title: Gallery specimens and gallery-only parameters let visual checks pass while the shipped window differs
findings.designEvidence: WORKFLOW/AGENTS: every UI change is checked against its Figma render before it is called done. The owner complaint 'looks right at first glance but behaves differently'.
findings.actual: MXRVideoContextMenuView (S09) and MXRProfilesView (S68) are rendered by the gallery but never shown where users open those menus. The gallery renders MXRAppView with reservesTrafficLights=false and no titlebar, which hides CMP-02. Panels are checked standalone (S14.Tracks, S22.Queue) rather than in their real placement, which hides CMP-03 and CMP-04. Codex's PASS/REVIEW counts therefore say little about the app.
findings.fix: Have the gallery compose exactly what MXRAppController composes, including a simulated titlebar and traffic-light reserve. Delete specimen-only views or make the app use them. Add App-level gallery states for open panels and menus.
findings.verifyNote:
Confirmed, with nuance.
- App-level panel scenes do exist (S14.App, S20.App, S22.App). They have no Figma node, so they are never diffed.
- App scenes force showWaveform = (scenario == .music) (AppGallery.swift:73) and build MXRAppView without reservesTrafficLights or onPictureInPicture. So CMP-01, CMP-02 and MISS-04 cannot appear in any render.
- S13 fakes the OSD pairing (MISS-01). MXRVideoContextMenuView is labelled a gallery specimen.

findings.title: Literal sizes in views and transient (non-persisted) UI preferences
findings.designEvidence: AGENTS hard rule: 'No literal colors or sizes in views'. Principle 9: remember the user's context.
findings.actual: SettingsSidebar.swift:14, 53, 60, 64, 172, 176, 197 and 199 (80, 32, 24, 56, 180×38, 50) and EffectsSidebars.swift:14, 18, 109, 209, 213 and 223 (48, 40, 37, 68×32, 52) hard-code sizes, with about 50 literal frames across MXRUI. showWaveform, showSubtitleTimeline, showStatistics and timeDisplay live in InterfaceModel and are lost on relaunch or profile switch.
findings.fix: Move the sizes into Theme tokens. Persist the Playback-tab toggles and time display in the profile or preset stores.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed. The literals carry Figma-node comments, so this is token hygiene, not wrong values. The toggles and timeDisplay are not persisted (InterfaceModel.swift:157-161).

findings.title: The designed two-line OSD never shows the action in the real app: VLC draws the action in the video, and the in-app OSD shows only 'Pressed X'
findings.designEvidence: VIDEO_BREAKDOWN §13 MUST: the OSD shows the action, e.g. 'Crop: 2.35:1', then 'Pressed C'. Key frame 13-bookmarks-chapters-osd__osd-shows-pressed-key__15m27.1s. Principle 14 ('the OSD names the pressed key').
findings.actual:
- VLCOSDBackend (VLCServiceBackends.swift:232) forwards text only when the bridge publishes an 'osd' service snapshot. Nothing in module/bridge produces one; grep finds no producer.
- Engine feedback (volume, rate, crop, aspect, track switches, seek) is drawn by VLC core into the vout through src/player/osd.c (vouts_osd_Message), top-right, in VLC's font. This is the 'Volume: 48%' in C7.
- OSDModel.keyPressed (ServiceModels.swift:204-210) calls show(nil, pressedKey:), so MXRPlayerOSD (PlayerView.swift:208-223) shows only 'Pressed C', at top-left.
- The action and the key end up in two places with two fonts.
- The S13.Player/osd gallery state fakes the pairing with app.osd.show("Crop: 2.35:1", pressedKey: "C") (PlayerGallery.swift:105).
findings.fix:
1. Disable engine OSD for the interface's player without touching the engine: var_Create plus var_SetBool(player, "osd", false) in the bridge. Vouts inherit 'osd' from the player. Keep the user's 'Show feedback for shortcuts' as the UI-side flag.
2. Produce the action text in the UI. Either give each AppCommand or shortcut handler an OSD label ('Volume 48 %', 'Speed 1.5×', 'Crop 2.35:1', 'Subtitles: English'), or have the bridge forward vlc_player listener events (volume, rate, track selection, vout aspect/crop vars) to the 'osd' service.
3. Show both lines through OSDModel.show(text, pressedKey:).
4. Remove the faked gallery pairing.

findings.title: Subtitles matched to a folder or playlist in Add Subtitles are stored in the media library but never loaded when those episodes play
findings.designEvidence: §06 MUST: after Save the files appear under External Tracks, and the mapping persists for that folder or playlist. Narration at 6:00: 'add subtitles to entire folders … have it saved for all future episodes'. Frame 06m21.7.
findings.fix:
1. When building playlist inputs for library media, fetch the media's p_files of type VLC_ML_FILE_TYPE_SUBTITLE (and AUDIO).
2. Attach them before vlc_playlist_Insert, either with input_item_AddSlave(item, SLAVE_TYPE_SPU, SLAVE_PRIORITY_USER) or with an ':input-slave=' option. Select the mapped subtitle by default.
3. Add a bridge smoke test: attach a subtitle to media B, play B, and expect the subtitle in External Tracks.

findings.title: Changing Subtitle Font or Outline Color while watching fails and leaves a sticky 'Retry Playback' error card on the video
findings.designEvidence: §07 problem → decision: subtitle font, size, outline and position are adjustable while watching. §07 MUST, Appearance: Font, Text Color, Outline Color, and so on. Principle 2 (quiet by default).
findings.actual:
- MXREffectsServices.m:185-191 rejects any change to fontFamily, bold, textOpacity, outlineColor, shadow, shadowColor or shadowDistance while a vout exists ('requires reopening the media').
- VLCPlayerBackend.send (VLCPlayerBackend.swift:139-147) stores every failed player command in commandError. PlayerModel exposes it as errorMessage, and PlayerView.swift:156-162 shows it as a persistent card in the middle of the video with a native bordered 'Retry Playback' button that calls play().
- So editing a designed sidebar row mid-episode puts an unrelated playback-error card over the picture, and it stays until some later command succeeds.
- The same plumbing produces the 'play queue is empty' card in CMP-15.
findings.fix:
1. Separate command failures from playback errors. Show command failures as transient OSD text or an inline message on the row. Use errorMessage only for input or decoder errors.
2. For renderer-bound style values, apply the change by re-creating the text renderer: update the freetype-* variables, then re-select the current SPU track. If that is not possible, mark the row 'applies from the next file' with ⓘ instead of throwing.

findings.title: A PiP button is forced into the real top bar and cannot be removed through Customize; no gallery render shows it
findings.designEvidence: §03: the final frames keep fullscreen in the top bar, and PiP is a Customize tile (Player-6.png 247:445). §15 MUST: dragging an element out of a bar removes it. D007 (provisional) allows a Figma-styled PiP button.
findings.actual:
- PlayerBars.swift:28-31 appends a PiP button to the top bar whenever the host passes onPictureInPicture and the layout lacks .pictureInPicture. MXRAppController.swift:73-78 passes it whenever PiP is available.
- So removing PiP in Customize has no effect: the button is re-injected outside the layout model.
- The gallery never passes the closure, so no Figma check sees the shipped top bar.
findings.fix: If D007 keeps PiP, add .pictureInPicture to the default top layout. Render only what the layout contains, so Customize can remove it. Pass a stub onPictureInPicture in the App gallery scenes so renders match the shipped bar.

findings.title: A pasted IPTV .m3u link is saved as one stream entry, not expanded into a playlist of channels
findings.designEvidence: §10 MUST: saving adds the stream, or the expanded m3u playlist, to the Network category. The IPTV demo: pasting a public .m3u link turns it into an automatic playlist of channels (12m20–13m15).
findings.actual: saveNetworkURLs (MXRLibraryServices.m:181-200) creates one vlc_ml_new_stream per pasted URL. The .m3u becomes a single media entry in the collection. Channels appear only in the play queue after VLC's playlist demuxer expands it at play time. The Network category never shows the channel list.
findings.fix: Before saving a playlist URL, preparse it (vlc_preparser or input_item parse with sub-items). Store each sub-item as a stream inside the named network playlist, and keep the source URL for refresh.

refuted.note:
Refuted as stated.
- The 6:00 narration ('manually select the correct subtitle files for every episode and have it saved for all future episodes') means you never redo the work on later viewings. It is not about rules for files added later.
- Attaching per item in the media library (VLC_ML_MEDIA_ADD_EXTERNAL_MRL) is a valid way to persist that.
- The real defect is that those attachments are never applied at playback. See MISS-02.

Refuted. Figma 'Video - Essential.png' (536:1855) and the S18 crop (498:2965) show plain Expand/Collapse cards with sliders and no preview thumbnails, and the breakdown lists 'video filter preview thumbnails' as OPEN. This is not a deviation from the design.

grades.justification: Completeness 68: nearly every designed control and tab is built and wired to VLC: 3 track tabs, output devices, 4 sidebar tabs, presets, EQ and filters, queue, bookmarks, chapters, subtitle timeline. Still missing: the '+ opens Add Subtitles' entry point, timeline range labels in the product, speed-slider ticks, per-preset ⋯ menus, the styled right-click menu and submenus, and all dismissal and motion behavior. Fidelity 45: isolated components match Figma closely in the gallery. In the real window they are composed wrong: the popover is centered vertically, the sidebar and queue push the video into a separate column, menus and dropdowns are NSPopovers with arrows or plain native menus, and nothing animates. Code quality 50: MXRAppView switches between 3 different view trees depending on panel/library state, which blocks transitions and resizes the video in fullscreen. Several gallery entries (S09, S68, S21) render specimens the product never shows, so their PASS results mean nothing. Esc handling is attached where it can never fire, and many literal sizes sit in views despite the AGENTS rule.

doneWell: Isolated panel components are close to Figma (verified side by side): track popover Video/Audio/Subtitles (400x524, 50 pt BG/B2 tab strip with 2 pt accent underline, 60 pt section headers, 32 pt rows with 12 pt gaps, 72 pt footer with a 32 pt 'Show Preferences'), and the 4-tab sidebar (Playback/Video/Audio/Subtitles in the final order) including Defaults, Synchronization, Appearance, Filters and the preset footer. Do not restyle these; fix only how they are positioned and presented.
The Chapters and Bookmarks tabs match Figma 6321:14045 and 6320:13784 almost pixel for pixel. The queue tab header shows a correct computed total ('4 items - 1h 34m').

InterfaceModel's state logic is sound and should be kept: one exclusive rightPanel; the last sidebar and queue tabs are remembered; 'Show Preferences' opens the matching sidebar tab; clicking the other track icon switches tabs; picking a track does not close the popover (the 'menus keep closing' complaint); bar icons go active (filled orange subtitles and gear) while their panel is open; bars stay pinned while a panel is open.
The audio output device list is wired to VLC with event-driven reload plus a refresh button. Selection does not close the popover.
Numeric settings follow the 'typed value + slider' rule; delay sliders are bipolar with the fill running from 0 (PanelSlider center:), and the -10 s / 0 s / +10 s labels are present.

EQ presets map to the Figma two-tone eq-* curve icons. 'Open Advanced Settings' opens the Settings window on the matching category. The Stereo-test availability explanation follows the 'show availability, don't fake success' policy.
⋯ menu content and row geometry match Figma menu.png (375 pt, 48 pt rows, two-tone icons, BG/A2 hover); only its presentation is wrong.
The subtitle timeline renders cues in media time with delay applied, nudges in 50 ms steps, and pauses its TimelineView when bars are hidden (good for CPU budget).

findings.title: Track popover is vertically centered on the right edge instead of anchored 20 pt above the control bar
findings.designEvidence: Figma Controls set 491:1780, variants subtitles 491:2216, audio 496:2495, video 498:2674: popup 491:2243 is 400x524 at x=1500, y=-544 relative to the bar. Its right edge is 20 pt from the window and its bottom 20 pt above the bar (metrics.json sidePanels.placement rightInset 20, gapAboveControlBar 20). Video 06m21.7 (native frame) shows the card sitting bottom-right just above the bar. VIDEO_BREAKDOWN §04 MUST: 'anchored at the bottom right above the bar'. spec-part1 §04: y≈485–1005.
findings.actual: MXRAppView.swift:53 and :85 attach the popover with `.overlay(alignment: .trailing)` and only `.padding(.trailing, panelInset)`, so it is centered vertically in the video area. The 1920x1080 render of S14.App/subtitle-tracks puts the card at y≈271–795 instead of 482–1006, floating mid-right exactly as the owner reports. The same code is duplicated in both branches (lines 52–60 and 84–92).
findings.fix: Use `.overlay(alignment: .bottomTrailing)` and pad both trailing and bottom with Theme.Metric.SidePanels.placement (20/20) inside the area between the bars. Keep the height at min(524, available). Factor the duplicated overlay into one helper.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed. MXRAppView.swift:52 and :84 use .overlay(alignment: .trailing) with only trailing padding. The S14.App/subtitle-tracks render puts the card at y≈271–795. Figma `node 491:2216` places popup 491:2243 400x524 at (1500,-544), so its bottom is 20 pt above the bar and its right edge 20 pt from the window (metrics.json sidePanels.placement 20/20). Video frame 06m21.7 shows the card bottom-right, flush above the bar. Owner complaint C2 is fully explained. The fix as written is correct. Bonus: anchoring to the bottom also keeps the card correct with a two-row control bar.

findings.title: Settings sidebar and queue panel push and shrink the video into a separate docked column instead of floating over it
findings.designEvidence: Figma Controls variants playback 2238:9432, video settings 498:2937, audio settings 536:1059, subtitle settings 763:1958 and queue 491:1781: panel 400x946 at x=1500, y=-966, i.e. over the 1920-wide video area with 20 pt insets (metrics.json: 946 = 1080-40-54-2x20). VIDEO_BREAKDOWN §07 SHOULD: 'The sidebar overlays the right side of the video, as in every frame. It does not push or shrink the video.' spec-part2 §13: 'overlays in every frame'. Video 15m16.7 (native) shows the chapters panel inside the video frame with the video continuing behind it. Principle 5: 'Panels overlay the side of the video'.
findings.actual: MXRAppView.swift:93-98 lays out `HStack { playerCanvas; MXRRightPanelView() }` whenever `reservesPanelSpace` (lines 169-174, .sidebar/.queue). In S20.App/subtitle-settings and S22.App/queue the rounded video frame ends at x=1490. A 10 pt bgA3 gutter follows, then the panel in its own chrome column with its own 20 pt insets. That is the 'small window inside another window' look. The 95% tint plus hudWindow backdrop (PanelControls.swift:52) has only flat chrome behind it. Clicking 'Show Preferences' turns an overlay popover into this pushed layout, so the video jumps sideways with no transition.
findings.fix: Overlay the sidebar and queue on the video canvas: `.overlay(alignment: .topTrailing)`, 20 pt top, right and bottom insets between the bars, width min(400, available), and leave the video frame untouched. If a push mode is ever wanted for small windows, make it an explicit DECISIONS entry and an opt-in preference, not the default.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed. The S20.App and S22.App renders end the rounded video frame at x≈1490, followed by a bgA3 gutter and the panel in its own column. Figma 491:1781 and 763:1958 put the 400x946 panel at (1500,-966), inside the 1920-wide video area. Breakdown §07 SHOULD and Principle 5 both say panels overlay the video. Frames 09m30.1 and 15m16.7 show the video frame border running behind the panel to x≈1912. D019 only lets panels shrink to give the video room; it does not authorize pushing the video. It is also inconsistent: the compact library overlays the video (MXRAppView.swift:78-83) while the right panel pushes it (93-98). With both open, the video is overlaid on the left and pushed on the right. This is root cause #1 of C5.

findings.title: Opening any right panel swaps the whole window into a different view tree; in fullscreen the video resizes and nothing can animate
findings.designEvidence: VIDEO_BREAKDOWN §03 MUST: 'The bars overlay the video in fullscreen. The video must not jump when they appear.' Panels are floating overlays (P1/P2), and spec-part1 §04 suggests a 150 ms fade/slide, which needs a stable hierarchy.
findings.actual: MXRAppView.body (lines 37-103) picks one of 3 compositions. With no panel open it shows MXRPlayerView, a ZStack with overlaid bars. Any rightPanel switches to a VStack { topBar; HStack{canvas,panel}; controlBar } where the bars are layout rows, and the compact library adds a third variant. In fullscreen, MXRPlayerView sets the bar padding to 0, but the VStack branch still reserves 40+54 pt even at the fullscreen chrome opacity. So opening the audio popover shrinks the fullscreen video by 94 pt, and the sidebar takes about 420 pt more width. Each switch also rebuilds MXRPlayerView (@State hover tasks reset) and re-parents the retained video host. A panel set while library == .full is never shown at all (that branch has no MXRRightPanelView), so menu-bar 'Toggle Queue' silently does nothing there.
findings.fix: Use one stable composition: ZStack { fixed video canvas; top/bottom bars as overlays (or reserved space only when windowed and pinned); library overlay leading; right-panel overlay trailing }. Never change which branch the video lives in. Drive panel changes with withAnimation and `.transition` (see P4).
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed. body has 3 different view trees (37-103). In fullscreen, MXRPlayerView pads 0 (PlayerView.swift:62-63), but the panel branch's VStack keeps topBar and controlBar as layout rows. barsVisible is forced true when rightPanel != nil (MXRAppView.swift:135-136), so the video shrinks by 40+54 pt when any popover opens. In the library == .full branch (67-73) MXRRightPanelView is never mounted, so Toggle Queue, Show Subtitle Tracks and similar commands silently set state there. The panel then appears later, when the user leaves the full library. MXRVideoHostView is one retained NSView, re-parented on every branch switch. This structure is also why P4's transitions cannot be added cleanly.

findings.title: No open/close motion for popovers or sidebars, while the ⋯ menu animates only because it is an NSPopover; motion is inconsistent
findings.designEvidence: spec-part1 §04 open question: 'fade plus 6–8px upward slide, about 150ms'. VIDEO_BREAKDOWN §04 SHOULD: 'A short fade/slide is fine'. PHILOSOPHY §2.3: honor prefers-reduced-motion. Bars already use MXRPlayerMetrics.revealDuration 0.13.
findings.actual: No .transition or withAnimation exists for rightPanel anywhere: a grep over MXRUI finds only the bar reveal and the toast. InterfaceModel.toggle/selectTab (InterfaceModel.swift:176-216) mutate state directly, so the popover and sidebar pop in and out instantly. The ⋯ menu uses `.popover(isPresented:arrowEdge:.bottom)` (PlayerBars.swift:212-213), so it gets AppKit's NSPopover fade and scale plus an arrow. The 2 surfaces look and move differently. PanelExpand (PanelControls.swift:406-431) also inserts content instantly. To answer C2: the design does not show the animation, but the spec expects a subtle one, and it must match across surfaces.
findings.fix: Add a Theme.Motion token (for example panel: easeOut 0.15 s, offset 8 pt). Track popover: opacity + 8 pt move up from the bar. Sidebar/queue: opacity + 12–16 pt move in from the right. ⋯ menu: opacity + 4–8 pt move down from the top bar. Use the same curve everywhere, wrap the InterfaceModel mutations in withAnimation at the call sites, use opacity only when accessibilityReduceMotion is on, and animate the tab underline with matchedGeometryEffect.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed: grepping MXRUI/MXRDesign finds no withAnimation or .transition for rightPanel. The only motion is the bar reveal (PlayerView.swift:113), the toast opacity and the mini player. The ⋯ menu animates only because it is a SwiftUI .popover, i.e. an NSPopover (PlayerBars.swift:212-213). Nuance for C2/C4: the design never shows panel motion. Breakdown §04 calls a short fade/slide 'fine', and spec §04 suggests ~150 ms fade plus a 6–8 pt rise. So this is an inconsistency and polish gap, not a contradiction of the design. Major is still right because users clearly notice the snap next to the animated menu. It depends on fixing P3 first.

findings.title: Bottom popovers cannot be dismissed by Esc or by clicking outside; clicking the video toggles play/pause instead
findings.designEvidence: VIDEO_BREAKDOWN §04 SHOULD: 'Clicking outside or pressing Esc closes the popover.' spec-part1 §04 Behavior says the same. Design principle 2: panels 'go away cleanly'.
findings.actual: (1) The local key monitor (MXRAppController.swift:102-115) runs before the responder chain and routes Esc to shortcuts.handle. VLC binds Esc to key-leave-fullscreen by default (src/libvlc-module.c:2318), so the event is swallowed. The `.onExitCommand { ui.closeRightPanel() }` at TrackPopover.swift:19 only fires when focus is inside the panel, and its rows are non-focusable plain buttons, so it never runs. (2) Clicking the video goes to MXRVideoHostView.mouseDown, then onSingleClick, which defaults to .playPause (MXRNativePreferences.swift:53, MXRAppController.swift:205-211). 'Click outside to close' therefore pauses or resumes playback and leaves the popover open. (3) The only way to close it is to click the same bar icon again. Meanwhile the ⋯ NSPopover closes on both Esc and outside click.
findings.fix: In the key monitor, if interface.rightPanel != nil and the key is Esc, close the panel and consume the event before shortcut routing (leave fullscreen only when no transient UI is open). In onSingleClick, if a track popover is open, close it and consume the click without play/pause. Decide whether the sidebar/queue also close on outside click: recommended no for the sidebar (it is a tool panel) but yes for Esc. Remove the dead onExitCommand or move focus into the panel on open.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed by tracing the code. (1) The local keyDown monitor (MXRAppController.swift:102-115) calls shortcuts.handle before the responder chain. The shortcuts snapshot (MXRServicesBridge.m:544-558) includes VLC's key-leave-fullscreen, which defaults to 'Esc' on macOS (libvlc-module.c:2318). So Esc is consumed even when not fullscreen, and `.onExitCommand` (TrackPopover.swift:19) can never fire. (2) A click on the video reaches MXRVideoHostView.mouseDown, then onSingleClick. That defaults to .playPause (MXRNativePreferences click-action fallback), so 'click outside' pauses or resumes playback and leaves the popover open. The only way to close it is the bar icon. This is the root cause of C4's 'unclear how to close'.

findings.title: ⋯ app menu is wrapped in an NSPopover with an arrow; its submenus are click-to-open, unstyled nested popovers, and the designed Profiles submenu (S68) is only used as a modal sheet
findings.designEvidence: Figma menu.png 6062:13354: 375 pt wide, radius 10, bg blur + menuShadow, no arrow. spec-part1 §05: 'Drops from the ⋯ button, left-aligned just under the top bar.' Figma Profiles submenu 6648:20514 (265 pt, 48 pt rows, two-tone icons, check) appears in Profiles.png next to the menu.
findings.actual: PlayerBars.swift:212-213 presents MXRAppMenuView in `.popover(arrowEdge: .bottom)`. The Figma card sits inside NSPopover chrome: system material behind it, an arrow under the ⋯ button, the menu centered on the 28 pt button rather than left-aligned under the bar, and PlayerOutsideShadow clipped by the popover bounds. There is no arrow-key, type-select or hover-to-open behavior. Submenu rows (PlayerMenus.swift:130-153) open another arrowed NSPopover on click containing a VStack of plain Buttons (12 pt spacing, bgA3, no icons, no hover); the profile check is drawn inside an HStack label. The real S68 view, MXRProfilesView, is reachable only as a modal sheet via .manageProfiles (AppModel.swift:234 → MXRAppView.swift:246), so its gallery PASS (S68.Profiles/movies) validates a presentation users never see as a submenu.
findings.fix: Present the menu as a borderless child panel or overlay anchored at the button's leading edge, 4–6 pt below the top bar, with no arrow. Close it on outside click and Esc, and support up/down/return keys (or build it as an NSMenu with custom row views). Open submenus on hover after a ~200 ms delay to the right edge of the row, and reuse MXRProfilesView (and a matching recent-items view) as the submenu content. Remove the .profiles sheet path or make it a real manager.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed. The menu card itself is accurate: the S07 side-by-side matches menu.png almost pixel for pixel, so keep it. But it is presented through `.popover(arrowEdge: .bottom)`. That adds an arrow and NSPopover chrome, centres the 375 pt menu on a 28 pt button at x≈65 so it hangs off the window's left edge, and clips PlayerOutsideShadow. Submenus (PlayerMenus.swift:130-153) are click-to-open arrowed popovers with plain VStack rows on bgA3. MXRProfilesView, the real S68 view whose doc comment says 'the profile submenu', is used only by the native menu-bar 'Manage Profiles' sheet (AppModel.swift:234, MXRAppView.swift:246). The S68 PASS therefore validates a presentation the ⋯ menu never shows.

findings.title: Right-click menu in the product is a plain native menu (no two-tone icons, no shortcuts, ' ✓' typed into titles); the styled version exists only in the gallery
findings.designEvidence: Figma right-click menu.png 6065:13616: 292 pt, 48 pt rows, two-tone icons, right-aligned dim shortcuts, submenu chevrons, Hide UI. VIDEO_BREAKDOWN §05 MUST: 'cleaned up and restyled'. Transcript 5:00: 'update it with our style'.
findings.actual: The video uses `.contextMenu { MXRVideoContextMenuContent() }` (PlayerView.swift:64, PlayerMenus.swift:188-216). NativePlayerCommand is Button(title) with no image and no .keyboardShortcut. Track and device selection appends ' ✓' to the title text (PlayerMenus.swift:225, 237, 287, 311-313) instead of a menu-item state. The Figma-styled MXRVideoContextMenuView (PlayerMenus.swift:70-105) is described as 'a styled context-menu specimen for the gallery' and is never shown to users, so the S09.ContextMenu check validates dead code. MoreSettings items call toggleSidebar(tab) (line 320), so choosing 'Video' while the Video tab is open closes the sidebar.
findings.fix: Keep native NSMenu behavior but bring the look closer to Figma. Set each item's image to MXRIcon.nsImage(name, tone: .twoTone) and its keyEquivalent/modifier mask from the VLC binding so shortcuts render right-aligned, and use state = .on (or Toggle/Picker in SwiftUI Menu) for selected tracks. Alternatively, present the custom MXRVideoContextMenuView in a borderless panel at the click point. Either way, delete the gallery-only specimen or make the product use it. Make MoreSettings items select the tab, not toggle it.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed. The video uses `.contextMenu { MXRVideoContextMenuContent() }` (PlayerView.swift:64), with Button(title) items: no image, no keyboardShortcut, and ' ✓' appended to titles (PlayerMenus.swift:225, 233, 237, 287, 311, 313). The Figma-styled MXRVideoContextMenuView is explicitly 'a styled context-menu specimen for the gallery' (70) and is only used by the S09 gallery entry (PlayerGallery.swift:89-92). MoreSettings calls toggleSidebar(tab) (320). With that tab already open, InterfaceModel.toggle closes the sidebar instead.

findings.title: External Tracks '+' opens a bare file picker; the Add Subtitles dialog is hidden behind the pencil
findings.designEvidence: VIDEO_BREAKDOWN §04 MUST: 'External Tracks with edit (pencil) and add (+). The + opens the Add Subtitles dialog (section 06).' Transcript 6:00: 'when you click on Add, it opens a dialog with three options of adding subtitles to this file or this folder or this playlist'.
findings.actual: TrackPopover.swift:62 makes the pencil call present(.addSubtitles(scope: .file, source: .computer)), and line 63 makes '+' call request(.addSubtitleFile), a plain NSOpenPanel for one file. Users following the design's main subtitle flow ('+' → folder/playlist matching) never reach section 06.
findings.fix: '+' should present .addSubtitles, defaulting the scope to folder/playlist when the media has one. The pencil should edit the existing external tracks (rename, remove, re-match), or open the dialog prefilled with the current mapping.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed. TrackPopover.swift:62 makes the pencil open .addSubtitles(scope: .file, source: .computer), and :63 makes '+' call request(.addSubtitleFile), a bare NSOpenPanel. Transcript [6:00] says clicking Add opens the 3-scope dialog. Breakdown §04 MUST and spec §04 both say '+ opens the Add Subtitles dialog'. The two buttons are effectively swapped.

findings.title: Sidebar dropdowns and the preset picker open as arrowed NSPopovers with unstyled rows, and the selected check mark is invisible
findings.designEvidence: Figma Dropdown 2372:8300, EQ presets 2372:8487, Audio Visualizer 2372:8639, HDR Options 2372:8733: open list 364x232, r6, 44 pt rows (dropdownOption 2372:8360), the selected row filled with an orange check, dropdownListShadow. Figma Setting Preset 2372:8834 (and video 07m58.9): the list opens upward with '+ New Preset' first, each custom preset prefixed by a '⋯' menu, and the current preset checked on a highlighted row.
findings.actual: PanelDropdown (PanelControls.swift:283-329) uses `.popover(arrowEdge: .bottom)` with an arrow and system material. Rows are HStacks with 8 pt padding (~33 pt), 2 pt spacing, and no hover or selected fill. The selected row draws `MXRIcon(.check)` (line 319), but the default .check variant is an empty frame (MXRIcon.swift doc), so no option ever shows as current. Every dropdown uses the same arrowEdge, so the preset list cannot open upward while the others open downward. The preset list (SettingsSidebar.swift:79-90) puts 'New Custom Preset' last, then flat 'Rename Current Preset' and 'Delete Current Preset' rows; delete runs without confirmation and there are no per-preset ⋯ menus.
findings.fix: Build one MXRDropdownList overlay/child panel from the Figma tokens (Controls.dropdownOpenList, dropdownOption, Effect.dropdownListShadow, presetListShadow) with a direction parameter (down for settings, up for preset). Use MXRIcon(.check, state: .active) for the selected row, and add a hover fill and keyboard navigation. Restructure the preset list as '+ New Preset', presets each with ⋯ (Rename/Delete with confirmation), and the current one checked. Match the selection by id, not title.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed. The PanelDropdown list uses `.popover(arrowEdge: .bottom)` with ~33 pt rows (8 pt padding) and no hover or selected fill. Figma option 2372:8360 is a 360x44 row. The selected row draws `MXRIcon(.check)` (PanelControls.swift:319). MXRIcon's doc (MXRIcon.swift:24-25) says this variant draws nothing, so no current value is ever marked. Selection is matched by title. The preset list (SettingsSidebar.swift:79-90) lists presets first, then 'New Custom Preset', then flat Rename and Delete rows, and Delete has no confirmation. Setting Preset.png shows '+ New Preset' first, '⋯' per custom preset, and the checked Default on a highlighted row. One overstatement: 'cannot open upward' is not strictly true, because AppKit flips the popover when there is no room below. The real defect is the missing Figma list styling. The queue sort popover (QueuePanel.swift:76-85) has the same problems.

findings.title: Subtitle timeline: the product never shows the '*' range labels, and the window stops following playback after any drag or ‹/› press
findings.designEvidence: VIDEO_BREAKDOWN §07 MUST: 'The seek bar becomes a zoomed time window, with the range labels marked *'. Video 07m04.2 (native) shows '00:06:00*' … '00:07:00*'. Figma sub timeline 3744:12361.
findings.actual: PlayerBars.swift:223-225 embeds MXRSubtitleTimelineView(showsRangeLabels: false), and MXRTimeLabel (PlayerControls.swift:83-87) keeps showing elapsed/total. The '*' bounds appear only in the isolated gallery entry S21.Timeline/default. SubtitleTimeline.swift:100 and :116-119 set `viewportStart` on the first drag or page click, and it resets only on a media change (line 56). From then on the window is frozen: progress is clamped (line 68), so the playhead sits at the right edge while time advances and cues stop scrolling.
findings.fix: When timeline mode is on, have the bar's time slots show the window bounds with '*'. Return to follow mode (viewportStart = nil) when the drag ends, after a few seconds of inactivity, or when the playhead leaves the window, and add a way to jump back to the playhead.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed. PlayerBars.swift:223-224 passes showsRangeLabels: false, and MXRTimeLabel keeps showing the elapsed and total time. Video frame 07m04.2 shows '00:06:00*' and '00:07:00*' in those slots. viewportStart is set on drag (SubtitleTimeline.swift:100) and on page (118), and cleared only on media change (56). After that, progress is clamped at 1 (68), so the playhead pins to the right edge and cues stop scrolling. Note: the video's window is 60 s and the Figma window is 50 s; the code uses 50.

findings.title: Playback tab: invented unlabeled 'Expand Settings' row, speed slider without ticks and with misaligned labels, bordered speed field
findings.designEvidence: Figma playback sidebar 5187:24308: Show Subtitle Timeline, Show Statistics, Reverse, Sleep Timer, Audio Visualizer, Speed field 5187:24542 (140x32, fill #090909, no stroke, FG/A3 text). Slider 5187:24546 has 8 ticks (5187:24548, 6 pt, #1A1611) and 26 pt label cells centered on each 0.25 step. Video 09m17.5 shows Show Waveform and Show Metadata as ordinary toggle rows. No expander exists in either source.
findings.actual: SettingsSidebar.swift:121-127 adds PanelExpand(title: 'Display'), whose title appears only in accessibility, so users see a bare 'Expand Settings ›' (as in the owner's screenshot). It hides Show Waveform and a plain-text 'Show Metadata' Button (not a toggle). PanelSlider (PanelControls.swift:359-403) draws no ticks, and its labels are spread with Spacers, so '1' is not under the value-1 handle (S17 side-by-side). The speed field uses the generic 36 pt bordered PanelTextField. Reverse is removed (D014) instead of shown disabled with an explanation like other unsupported items.
findings.fix: Use the Figma row list. If Waveform and Metadata stay, make them normal toggle rows after Show Statistics, in video order. Add `ticks:` to PanelSlider and position labels at value fractions. Add a borderless 32 pt field variant for Speed. Show Reverse disabled with a help tooltip.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed in the S17 side-by-side. The render adds a bare 'Expand Settings ›' row; 'Display' appears only in the accessibility label (PanelControls.swift:427). It omits Reverse, which Figma shows as a toggle. D014 hides it, but the breakdown lists it as MUST, so showing it disabled is better. The slider has no ticks, while Figma 5187:24546 has 7 visible ticks. Its labels are spaced with Spacers, so '1' sits at x≈367 px against the handle at ≈350 px, whereas Figma centres '1' under the handle. The Speed field is bordered, while Figma's is borderless. Show Metadata is a plain-text button, while the video at 09m17.5 shows a toggle row. This partly explains C5.

findings.title: Panel rows, icon buttons, tabs and footer buttons have no hover or pressed feedback (bar buttons do)
findings.designEvidence: Figma Icon Wrapper 177:98 (hover #FFFFFF@6%), Button 500:3063 (footer hover BG/A4), option 2107:5935 (row hover/selected), spec-part1 Appendix B (tab hover #808080, row hover #1C1C1C).
findings.actual: PanelIconButton (PanelControls.swift:126-145), trackRow (TrackPopover.swift:96-105), Show Preferences (TrackPopover.swift:73-80), PanelTabStrip cells (PanelControls.swift:75-95), queue sort and header icons, chapter rows and the Expand row all use .plain with no hover state. MXRPlayerIconButton in the bar does have hover (PlayerControls.swift:25-33), so the panels feel dead next to the bar.
findings.fix: Add shared hover styles from the Figma states (iconHover fill for icon buttons, BG/A4 for footer buttons, BG/A2 rows, brighter tab label on hover) through one ButtonStyle in MXRDesign.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed. PanelIconButton, trackRow, the Show Preferences button, PanelTabStrip cells, chapter rows and PanelExpand all use `.plain` with no hover state. PlayerMenuButtonStyle (PlayerMenus.swift:171-185) already has a working hover row style for the ⋯ menu and could be reused. Figma Icon Wrapper 177:98 and Button 500:3063 define hover states.

findings.title: Queue details: current-row duration is orange with a filled glyph, insertion placeholder differs, bookmark +/− order is reversed
findings.designEvidence: Video 20m21.4: the current row has an outline orange ▷, an orange name and a gray FG/A3 duration, plus a dim '⋯' placeholder row at the insertion point while dragging. Figma bookmarks 6320:13784: header shows − then + (same order as the queue).

Bookmarks header renders + then − (117-120).

findings.verifyNote: Confirmed. In video frame 20m21.4 the current row has an outline orange ▷, an orange name and a gray duration '23:06', plus a dim '•••' placeholder at the insertion point. The S22.App render draws a filled ▶ and an orange duration (QueuePanel.swift:222, 228). Between rows, the drop target is a 2 pt orange line (236), and the orange •••-on-accent marker appears only at the end of the list (198-201). In the S23 side-by-side, the header shows + then −, while Figma 6320:13784 shows − then +.

findings.title: Gallery checks validate specimens and isolated components, not what the product composes
findings.designEvidence: AGENTS.md: 'Every UI change is checked visually against its Figma render before it's called done.' WORKFLOW definition of done.
findings.actual: S09.ContextMenu renders MXRVideoContextMenuView, which is never used in the product (P7). S68 renders a view the product shows as a sheet (P6). S21 renders range labels the product hides (P10). The panels are checked only at 400x524 and 400x946 in isolation. The one composed entry, S14.App/subtitle-tracks, clearly shows the mid-right placement (P1) and S20.App/S22.App show the pushed video (P2), yet both were accepted.
findings.fix: Add composed checks: render MXRAppView at 1920x1080 and crop with `$BIN ref --node 491:2216 / 2238:9432 / 491:1781 --bounds render` to compare popover and panel positions relative to the bar. Remove gallery-only specimens or wire them into the product.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed. S09 renders the gallery-only specimen. S68 validates a view that the ⋯ menu does not use. The S21 entry shows range labels that the product hides. S14.App, S20.App and S22.App visibly show the P1/P2 placement bugs and were still accepted, because they have no figmaNode and so no check is possible. The process gap is real.

findings.title: Literal sizes and ratios in views despite the 'no literal sizes in views' rule; duplicated layout math
findings.designEvidence: AGENTS.md hard rule: 'No literal colors or sizes in views.'
findings.actual: SettingsSidebar.swift:13-14 (height < 400, CGFloat(80)), 53 (32), 60 (24), 172/176 (56), 197 (180x38), 199 (50); PanelControls.swift:79 (>= 360), 259 (34), 265 (22x22), 324 (maxHeight 400), 341 (120/140); EffectsSidebars.swift:14, 18, 109, 213; MXRAppView.swift:179/183 (0.45/0.32/0.48 ratios). The height expression `max(0, h - topBar - controlHeight - panelInset*2)` is repeated 4 times, and PanelDropdown matches the selection by title string.
findings.fix: Move these into PanelMetric/Theme with Figma node references, compute the available panel rect once, and select choices by id.
findings.verifyNote: Spot-checked and all present: SettingsSidebar.swift:13-14 (400/80), 53 (32), 60 (24), 172/176 (56), 197 (180x38), 199 (50); PanelControls.swift:79 (360), 259 (34), 265 (22x22), 324 (400), 341 (120/140); MXRAppView.swift:179/183 (ratios). The panel-height expression appears 4 times in MXRAppView. Pure code hygiene.

findings.title: Panels are not keyboard or VoiceOver friendly
findings.designEvidence: PHILOSOPHY §2.3 (VoiceOver, native manners); principle 14 'Respect keyboard users'.
findings.actual: Opening a popover or sidebar does not move focus or post an accessibility notification. Rows are .plain buttons that are not reachable with arrow keys. There is no Tab/arrow navigation through tracks, and Esc does not work (P5).
findings.fix: On open, focus the selected row (@FocusState with defaultFocus), support .onMoveCommand up/down and Return, mark the container as an accessibility group with a label ('Subtitle tracks'), and post a layout-changed notification.
findings.verifyNote: Plausible and consistent with the code. Nothing moves focus or posts an accessibility notification when a panel opens. Rows are .plain buttons with no arrow-key navigation, and Esc is swallowed (P5). Fixing P5 is a prerequisite.

findings.title: Small-window panel states degrade badly
findings.designEvidence: D019: panels yield space gracefully in smaller windows.
findings.actual: At 180 pt height (S18.Sidebar/minimum) the sidebar shows only 'Defaults' and the preset footer, with a zero-height scroll area. At 307 pt width the queue summary truncates to '4 item…' (S22.Queue/compact) because 5 header icons take priority.
findings.fix: Hide the preset footer below a token threshold so content always gets space, and move the queue header actions into an overflow ⋯ when width is under ~360 pt.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed by rendering. S18.Sidebar/minimum (307x180) shows only the tab icons, a clipped 'Defaults' and the preset footer, with no usable content. S22.Queue/compact truncates the summary to '4 item…' because the 5 header icons win the width.

findings.title: Bookmark creation: Ctrl+B instead of ⌘B, no confirmation feedback, errors swallowed
findings.designEvidence: VIDEO_BREAKDOWN §13 MUST: one shortcut, no dialog ('Ctrl+B; on macOS ⌘B'). OPEN: 'a brief OSD Bookmark added'.
findings.actual: The default binding is key('Ctrl+b') (ShortcutValues.swift:202). BookmarksModel.addAtCurrentTime uses `try?` with no OSD or error reporting (EffectsModels.swift:220-229).
findings.fix: Default to Command+b, show osd.show('Bookmark added · 00:12:34'), and surface failures.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed. app-add-bookmark defaults to key('Ctrl+b') (ShortcutValues.swift:202). addAtCurrentTime uses `try?` with no OSD and no error reporting (EffectsModels.swift:220-229). This is one symptom of a broader issue: every app shortcut defaults to Control, and several collide with engine keys (see M1).

findings.title: ⋯ menu shows Ctrl shortcuts that are non-Mac, and Ctrl+P/N/D and 'l' actually run engine title, chapter and audio-track actions
findings.designEvidence: spec-part1 §05: 'On macOS, map Ctrl to ⌘.' VIDEO_BREAKDOWN §05 SHOULD (macOS): map Ctrl to ⌘ in displayed shortcuts. §13: '⌘B on macOS'. AGENTS.md: native macOS behavior.
findings.actual: All app actions default to Control: Ctrl+O, F, N, D, C, V, R, S, P and B, plus bare 'l' and 'q' (ShortcutValues.swift:185-203). The ⋯ menu prints them as 'Ctrl + O' (spelledString), and the menu bar shows ⌃O. Settings is ⌃P instead of ⌘,. VLC's macOS engine defaults already bind Ctrl+p to title-prev, Ctrl+n to title-next, Ctrl+d to chapter-next and 'l' to audio-track (src/libvlc-module.c:2364, 2382-2385). VLCShortcutsBackend.actions returns engine actions before app actions (VLCServiceBackends.swift:14-25). ShortcutsModel.reload builds a first-wins table (ServiceModels.swift:159-166), and the local key monitor dispatches it and swallows the event before the native menu's key equivalent (MXRAppController.swift:102-115). Result: pressing the advertised 'Ctrl + D' (Open Disc) on a film with chapters jumps to the next chapter. 'Ctrl + P' (Settings) and 'Ctrl + N' (Open Network Stream) trigger title navigation. 'l' cycles the audio track instead of toggling the library.
findings.fix: Use Mac-standard defaults for app actions: ⌘O, ⇧⌘O for Open Folder (⌘F is fullscreen in VLC on macOS), ⌘N, ⌘, for Settings, ⌘B and so on. Render the ⋯ menu shortcuts with ⌘/⌥/⇧/⌃ glyphs. Make the default sets disjoint, and have reload() detect collisions using the existing conflicts(for:) helper; app menu commands should win over engine defaults, or the conflict should be reported. Add a unit test asserting there are no duplicate default bindings across the engine (macOS block) and appActions.

findings.title: ⋯ menu open state is local and does not pin the bars, so the top bar can auto-hide under the open menu during playback
findings.designEvidence: VIDEO_BREAKDOWN §03: bars hide when the pointer leaves. A menu anchored to the bar must keep the bar visible, as panels and sheets already do through pinsControls.
findings.actual: menuOpen is @State inside PlayerControlView (PlayerBars.swift:201, 212-213). pinsControls (PlayerView.swift:36-39) checks rightPanel, library, sheet and customizing, but not open popovers or menus. When the pointer moves into the NSPopover (a separate window), onContinuousHover ends (PlayerView.swift:96-106). The hide task then fades the top bar to opacity 0 with hit testing off while the menu stays anchored to an invisible ⋯ button. The same applies to the overflow and speed Menus. Found by code reading, not reproduced at runtime.
findings.fix: Move transient-menu state into InterfaceModel (for example `activeMenu`), include it in pinsControls and barsVisible, and clear it when the menu closes. That also lets the key monitor close the menu on Esc consistently with P5.

findings.title: Color fields need 2 clicks: the swatch opens a system popover holding a second color well
findings.designEvidence: Figma subtitle Appearance 4046:12374/12377: hex field with a 22 pt swatch. Video 07m47.9: Text/Outline Color are inline fields. One click on a swatch should open the picker.
findings.actual: PanelColorField (PanelControls.swift:261-270) shows an arrowed NSPopover containing `ColorPicker(title, …)`, which is a labelled system color well. The user must click again to reach NSColorPanel, and the extra popover is unstyled system chrome inside the sidebar.
findings.fix: Open NSColorPanel directly from the swatch: a borderless NSColorWell representable, or `ColorPicker(...).labelsHidden()` styled as the 22 pt swatch. Keep the hex field as the typed input.

findings.title: Queue sort control is another unstyled arrowed popover with no current-sort indication
