findings.designEvidence: VIDEO_BREAKDOWN §02/§13: queue header has sort, repeat, shuffle, −, +. Figma menu language (option 2107:5935 48 pt rows; Sorting Options 856:2215: 265 pt, two-tone icons, selected ✓).
findings.actual: QueuePanel.swift:76-85 shows `.popover` with a VStack of plain Text buttons (8 pt padding, gap 2, no icons, no hover, no ✓ on the current key). It looks unlike every Figma menu and unlike the ⋯ menu that sits on the same screen.
findings.fix: Reuse the shared Figma menu-row component (PlayerMenuLabel + PlayerMenuButtonStyle, or the MXRDropdownList proposed in P9) for the sort menu. Mark the active QueueSortKey with MXRIcon(.check, state: .active).

grades.justification: Completeness: every top-bar element, fullscreen, PiP, Hide UI and a native menu bar are present. Missing: independent bar reveal, the auto-hidden windowed state, a drag region, cursor hiding, traffic-light handling and opening on Home at launch. Fidelity: the gallery top bar is nearly pixel-exact against Figma 247:447. The real window is wrong: it has a two-row ~72pt header, the cone is indented ~96pt, the ⋯ menu sits in an NSPopover bubble, the track popover is centred, and video seek bars show waveform ticks. Code quality: the structure and fullscreen bookkeeping are sound. Against that, a time-label token is reused as the traffic-light width, bar-visibility rules are duplicated, composition branches recreate the video host, one preference is never read, and gallery entries override product defaults so checks pass while the app differs.

doneWell: The top-bar left cluster matches Figma 247:447 almost to the pixel in the gallery: 38×28 logo cell, ⋯, sidebar toggle, divider and folder chip with Figma gaps (7 and 10pt), and a title centred on the window rather than the leftover space (PlayerRowLayout). S01.App/default differs only where the Windows controls were deliberately removed and in the seek-head position. Keep these metrics when fixing WT-01.
Hide UI (S06) geometry passes pixel-for-pixel against Figma 3328:11554: 10pt videoArea frame, clip radius 19−10=9, nothing else drawn.
In the MXRPlayerView path, fullscreen removes the frame and padding so the bars overlay the video and it does not jump when they appear (PlayerView.swift:62-63, 166-168).

Reveal uses a short 0.13s ease-out and respects Reduce Motion (PlayerView.swift:113). The auto-hide defaults ('In fullscreen only', ~0.5s) and the sensitivity edge zones follow Figma Settings › Interface.

Native fullscreen bookkeeping is robust: fullscreenRequests and fullscreenTransitions, failed-transition handlers, VLC vout set/unset_fullscreen routed through AppKit toggleFullScreen, plus 'Open fullscreen on' and auxiliary vout windows (MXRAppController.swift:239-351, 401-415).
A single persistent video surface (MXRVideoHostView) is reused by the player, compact and full library, mini player and PiP, including PiP return to the host view.

The native menu bar is built from the same AppCommand registry as the ⋯ and context menus, with live key equivalents, validation, checkmark states, Open Recent with Clear Menu, a Profile submenu, Services and a Window menu (MXRNativeMenus.swift).
The full-library top bar is trimmed to cone and ⋯ with the 'VLC Media Player' title, matching Figma Player-1 and Player-4 (PlayerGeometry.topItems).

Clicks on the video host (single click play/pause or controls after the double-click interval, double-click fullscreen, scroll for volume/seek with natural-direction handling) honour the Controls preferences.

findings.title: Real window has two header rows (traffic-light strip plus 40pt top bar) and the cone is indented ~96pt
findings.designEvidence: Figma Player-6 (247:445): topbar 247:447 is one 1920×40 row at y=0; logo cell 247:449 at x=6, so the cone glyph spans x 13–31. Native key frame 02-control-bar__final-layout-with-track-icons-native__06m24.4s: one 38–40px row with the cone at the window edge. D007 and D019 call for 'a shared 40-point top bar' with native traffic lights. VIDEO_BREAKDOWN §03 SHOULD: traffic lights in a full-size-content title bar, inside the top bar.
findings.actual: MXRAppController.swift:64-68 and :80 create a .titled + .fullSizeContentView window with a transparent titlebar and use an NSHostingView as the contentView. MXRAppView.swift:31 (GeometryReader root) never calls .ignoresSafeArea(), so SwiftUI lays the whole UI out below the titlebar safe area. MXRPlayerView's .background(bgA3) (PlayerView.swift:83) bleeds into that strip, which produces a separate ~28–32pt row that holds only the traffic lights, with the 40pt top bar underneath. On top of that, PlayerBars.swift:18 inserts a 76pt Color.clear before the logo. Its width comes from MXRPlayerMetrics.trafficLightReserve = Theme.Metric.ControlBar.timeLabel.width (PlayerMetrics.swift:38), a time-label token reused as a window metric. The cone therefore starts at x≈96pt with empty space to its left. Codex's own 03-paused-e01.png shows uniform #1B1B1B chrome from y=0 to 72pt (Figma: 41pt) and the cone centred at x≈107pt. The reserve is never removed, so in fullscreen (17-fullscreen-live-video.png) a blank 76pt gap sits before the cone. In Hide UI the strip and the traffic lights stay above the framed video. The gallery never sets reservesTrafficLights or uses a real titled window (PlayerGallery.swift:62-79), so S01 'passes' while the product is wrong.
findings.fix: 1) Add .ignoresSafeArea() at the MXRAppView root so the top bar starts at y=0 under the transparent titlebar. 2) Centre the traffic lights vertically in the 40pt bar: offset the standardWindowButton(.closeButton/.miniaturizeButton/.zoomButton) frames by (40 − titlebar height)/2, and re-apply in windowDidResize, didExitFullScreen and didEndLiveResize. An NSToolbar would take the clicks meant for the SwiftUI buttons underneath, so verify hit-testing whichever approach is used. 3) Replace trafficLightReserve with a value published by the window controller (zoomButton.frame.maxX plus a Figma gap, so the cone follows the lights as in D007). Set it to 0 in fullscreen, in Hide UI and whenever the lights are hidden. 4) Add a snapshot entry that hosts MXRAppView(reservesTrafficLights:true) in a real titled NSWindow so this regression becomes visible.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed. MXRAppController.swift:64-80 creates a .titled + .fullSizeContentView window with an NSHostingView, and there is no ignoresSafeArea anywhere in Sources (grep). PlayerBars.swift:18 inserts the reserve and PlayerMetrics.swift:38 sets trafficLightReserve = ControlBar.timeLabel.width (76). Codex's 02-corrected-narrow-vol-up.png and 18-fullscreen-return-paused.png both show the traffic lights alone in a ~32pt strip above the 40pt bar. In 03-paused-e01.png the video only starts at y≈73pt, against 41pt in Figma. 17-fullscreen-live-video.png shows the empty reserve in front of the cone. Native frames 06m21.7 and 11m57.0 show one ~38px row with the cone at x 13–31. Fix caveat: AppKit re-lays out the standard buttons, so moving their frames has to be re-applied on every titlebar layout. The alternative, an empty NSToolbar with .unifiedCompact, takes hits in the bar. Test both ways.

findings.title: Top and bottom bars reveal and hide together instead of independently
findings.designEvidence: VIDEO_BREAKDOWN §03 MUST: 'Bars show and hide independently. The pointer near the top reveals the top bar only (03m51.0), and near the bottom reveals the control bar only (03m53.0).' Key frames 03-top-bar__hover-top-bar-only__03m51.0s and 03-top-bar__hover-bottom-bar-only__03m53.0s. Transcript 3:30: '…only show them when you hover near them and immediately disappear when you move away'.
findings.actual: InterfaceModel.swift:165 holds a single areBarsVisible Bool. PlayerView.swift:96-106 folds nearTop || nearBottom into one pointerNearControls, and PlayerView.swift:30-34 applies the same barOpacity to MXRTopBar (:68-70) and MXRControlBar (:77-79). Moving toward the title also brings up the transport bar, and the reverse. MXRAppView.swift:132-151 keeps a second, different visibility rule whose .onHover only ever sets areBarsVisible = true and never clears it. Consumers (SubtitleTimeline.swift:48, PlayerControls.swift:388) key off the merged flag.
findings.fix: Model two flags (topBarVisible and controlBarVisible). Drive each from its own zone: top when y ≤ max(40, edge); bottom when y ≥ height − max(controlHeight, edge). Run one hide timer per bar. Pin a bar while the pointer is over it or while its own popup is open: the ⋯ menu pins the top bar; the track popover, sidebar and queue pin the control bar. Move the rule into one model-level function used by both MXRAppView and MXRPlayerView, and delete the duplicate. Have the display link and timeline key off controlBarVisible.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed. One areaBarsVisible flag (InterfaceModel.swift:165). nearTop || nearBottom are merged at PlayerView.swift:101-103, and the same barOpacity is applied to both bars (PlayerView.swift:69,78). The MXRAppView.swift:142/149 onHover handlers only ever set true. The video (03m51.0 and 03m53.0) shows each bar revealed on its own. Related: the ⋯ NSPopover's menuOpen is local @State and is not in pinsControls, so in fullscreen the top bar can fade out under an open menu. The two-flag fix has to include menu pinning.

findings.title: Windowed auto-hide leaves empty 40pt and 54pt chrome bands; the video never expands into the thin-frame state
findings.designEvidence: VIDEO_BREAKDOWN §03 MUST: 'In the bars-hidden state in a window, only the rounded video remains, inside a thin frame of chrome color.' Key frame 03m53.6: the video spans y 42–1027 inside an ~8px frame, and the cat keeps its position when a bar reappears (03m51.0, 03m53.0), so the bars overlay the video. In Figma Player-6 (247:445) the video IMAGE fill spans the whole frame, topbar 247:447 and Controls 491:1928 are drawn over it, and Frame 312 (6586:17371) is a 20pt centred stroke with r=19, giving a 10pt frame.
findings.actual: PlayerView.swift:62-63 pads the video by topBar.height and controlHeight whenever the window is neither fullscreen nor in Hide UI, regardless of bar visibility. With Settings › Interface › Auto-hide = Always, the bars fade to opacity 0 but the bgA3 bands remain. The 'hidden' window looks like an empty top bar plus an empty control bar around the video, with the traffic lights still showing (see WT-04).
findings.fix: When auto-hide applies in a window, use the S06 geometry: the canvas with videoArea.padding 10 on all sides and radius 9, with both bars overlaid in the ZStack. Canvas geometry must not depend on bar visibility. Keep the padded layout only when bars are pinned (auto-hide set to never, or in-fullscreen-only while windowed).
findings.verifyNote: The code claim is correct: PlayerView.swift:62-63 pads by topBar.height and controlHeight whenever the view is not fullscreen and not in Hide UI, whatever the bar visibility. Downgraded because the default Auto-hide mode is .fullscreen (AppModel+Preferences.swift:9), which matches Figma 'Settings - interface' ('In fullscreen only'). Windowed bars are therefore pinned by default, and the empty bands only show for users who pick 'Always'. It still breaks the §03 MUST for that setting.

findings.title: Traffic lights never follow the chrome: they stay visible in Hide UI and when the bars auto-hide
findings.designEvidence: VIDEO_BREAKDOWN §05 MUST: 'Hide UI removes all chrome, leaving only the video.' Figma Player - hide UI (3328:11554) shows only the framed video. D007 makes the traffic lights part of the top bar.
findings.actual: Nothing in Sources/ or module/ touches standardWindowButton (grep finds no matches). In Hide UI, MXRAppView.swift:37-38 renders only playerCanvas, yet AppKit still draws close/minimize/zoom at the top-left: today in the extra strip, and over the video once WT-01 is fixed. The same happens when the bars auto-hide in a window.
findings.fix: In MXRAppController, observe isUIHidden and top-bar visibility and fade the buttons' container with standardWindowButton(.closeButton)?.superview?.animator().alphaValue (0 when hidden, 1 when shown, using the same 0.13s easing). Keep them non-interactive while hidden. Re-apply after leaving fullscreen.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed: nothing references standardWindowButton or the titlebar container. In Hide UI, MXRAppView.swift:37-38 renders only playerCanvas, while AppKit keeps the lights and the safe-area strip above the framed video. 18-fullscreen-return-paused.png shows the lights sitting in that strip. Figma 3328:11554 shows only the framed video.

findings.title: In fullscreen, opening any panel switches the composition: the video shrinks by 94pt and the video host is re-parented
findings.designEvidence: VIDEO_BREAKDOWN §03 MUST: 'The bars overlay the video in fullscreen. The video must not jump when they appear.' Distilled principle 5: 'Panels overlay the side of the video.'
findings.actual: MXRAppView.swift:39-41 uses the overlay MXRPlayerView only when library == .hidden and rightPanel == nil. Any other state goes to the VStack {topBar; canvas; controlBar} branch (MXRAppView.swift:64-101), which stacks the bars instead of overlaying them. In fullscreen, opening the subtitle popover shrinks the video by 40 + 54pt, and closing it grows the video back. Switching if/else branches also destroys MXRPlayerView, losing its hover @State and hide task, and re-parents the NSViewRepresentable video host each time.
findings.fix: Use a single composition: one ZStack with the persistent canvas at a stable position and a stable .id, and the bars, library and panels as overlays. Reserve space for the sidebar or queue only in windowed mode, if at all. The canvas frame must not depend on which panel is open.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed. The overlay MXRPlayerView is used only when library == .hidden and rightPanel == nil (MXRAppView.swift:39-41). Any open panel switches to the VStack{topBar; canvas; controlBar} branch, so in fullscreen the canvas loses 40pt + controlHeight (the fullscreen padding there is 0). MXRNativeVideoView.makeNSView returns the shared host (MXRVideoHost.swift:68-71), so every branch switch removes the vout NSView and re-adds it elsewhere, and MXRPlayerView's hover/hide @State is lost.

findings.title: Track popover is vertically centred on the right edge, has no transition, and has no outside-click or Esc dismissal
findings.designEvidence: spec-part1 §04 geometry from native frame 06m21.67: card at x 1503–1900, y 485–1005, so it is anchored bottom-right ~12px from the edge and ~22px above the bar. VIDEO_BREAKDOWN §04 MUST: 'anchored at the bottom right above the bar'. SHOULD: 'Clicking outside or pressing Esc closes the popover. A short fade/slide is fine.' The spec's open question suggests a fade plus a 6–8px upward slide over ~150ms.
findings.actual: MXRAppView.swift:52 and :84 use .overlay(alignment: .trailing), which centres the card vertically; gallery S14.App/subtitle-tracks shows it at y 271–795 at 1080. The insertion at MXRAppView.swift:53-58 and :85-91 has no .transition or animation, so the card pops in. The only ways to dismiss are re-clicking the bar icon or .onExitCommand (TrackPopover.swift:19). That handler fires only if the panel holds focus, which it does not after a click on a plain bar button, and Esc then falls through to VLC's leave-fullscreen hotkey.
findings.fix: Use alignment .bottomTrailing with bottom and trailing padding of Theme.Metric.panelInset. Add .transition(.opacity.combined(with: .offset(y: 8))) and animate rightPanel changes with easeOut(0.15), respecting reduce motion. Add a transparent full-window catcher behind the popover, or a local mouse-down monitor, that calls closeRightPanel(). In MXRKeyRouting, route Esc to closeRightPanel before VLC hotkeys. Present the ⋯ menu through the same mechanism (WT-07) so every popup opens and closes the same way.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed. .overlay(alignment: .trailing) at MXRAppView.swift:52 and :84 has no transition. My S14.App/subtitle-tracks render puts the card at y≈271–795, vertically centred. Key frame 06m21.7 shows it anchored bottom-right, ~22px above the bar. The only dismissal is .onExitCommand on MXRRightPanelView (TrackPopover.swift:19), which needs focus inside the panel. There is no outside-click catcher.

findings.title: ⋯ app menu is presented as an NSPopover: arrow bubble around an already-styled card, with submenus as side popovers
findings.designEvidence: spec-part1 §05: the menu 'drops from the ⋯ button, left-aligned just under the top bar… Bg #161616, radius about 8px'. Figma menu.png (6062:13354) is a flat card with no arrow. VIDEO_BREAKDOWN §05.
findings.actual: PlayerBars.swift:211-213 uses .popover(isPresented: $menuOpen, arrowEdge: .bottom), which is an NSPopover with its own material bubble, arrow, centring and grow animation. MXRAppMenuView already draws its own MXRBackdropSurface and PlayerOutsideShadow (PlayerMenus.swift:42-43), so the result is a card inside a system bubble, centred on the button rather than left-aligned under the bar. Open Recent and Profile open as further .popover(arrowEdge: .trailing) bubbles (PlayerMenus.swift:142). This is the animation the owner sees on ⋯ but not on the bottom popovers (C4). Gallery S07.AppMenu/default renders the card on its own, so the popover chrome was never compared.
findings.fix: Present the menu with a custom presenter: a borderless child NSPanel or an in-window overlay at (logo cell minX, topBar.maxY + gap), showing only the Figma card, with a 120–150ms fade. Dismiss on outside click, Esc or selection. Cascade submenus to the right like menus, without arrows. Reuse the same presenter for the track popover (WT-06). Alternatively, use NSMenu with custom item views if native keyboard navigation matters more.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed. PlayerBars.swift:213 is .popover(isPresented:arrowEdge:.bottom), while MXRAppMenuView already draws its own MXRBackdropSurface and PlayerOutsideShadow (PlayerMenus.swift:42-43). Submenus open as further popovers (PlayerMenus.swift:142). spec-part1 §05 says 'left-aligned just under the top bar', and Figma 6062:13354 has no arrow. This is the animation asymmetry the owner describes in C4.

findings.title: Launch with nothing to resume shows the blank cone screen instead of Home; the 'Start in compact mode' preference is never read
findings.designEvidence: VIDEO_BREAKDOWN §11 MUST: 'When there is nothing to resume, launching VLC opens the full-window library on Home, never a blank cone screen.' Transcript 13:50: 'Instead of this blank cone, now you come back to VLC and see a full media library ready to continue wherever you left off.' Figma Player-5 (6261:15078). Figma Settings - interface includes a 'Start in compact mode' toggle.
findings.actual: InterfaceModel.library defaults to .hidden, and nothing sets .full or .compact at launch (grep: only the showFullLibrary command). PlayerView.swift:147-154 draws a large cone and an 'Open a media file' button on bgB2. AppModel+Preferences.swift:47-49 defines startsInCompactMode, but nothing reads it, so the Settings toggle has no effect.
findings.fix: In MXRAppController.start, once launchFileOpening has determined there are no files to open, set interface.library = startsInCompactMode ? .compact : .full and select Home. When playback starts from the library, follow the designed flow (mini player or collapse). Keep the 'Open a media file' affordance only as Home's empty state.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed, and upgraded. InterfaceModel.swift:143 defaults library to .hidden. The only writes to .full are the Go Home command and a library button, and nothing in MXRPlugin sets a launch presentation. §11 states as a MUST: 'never a blank cone screen'. The transcript at 13:50 names exactly this, so it contradicts a core design decision on every launch. Fix correction: the option's own help text (module/MXRAppOptions.inc:16, 'Opens with the library hidden and only the player visible') means startsInCompactMode should map to .hidden (player only), not .compact. The default (off) should open .full on Home.

findings.title: Play or Space on an empty queue shows a 'play queue is empty… Retry Playback' card on top of the empty-state prompt
findings.designEvidence: Neither Figma nor the video has this state. PHILOSOPHY §4: never invent a new visual language. Distilled principle 2: quiet by default.
findings.actual: AppModel.swift:203-214: canPerform(.playPause) falls through to the default true. togglePlayPause calls backend.play, vlc_playlist_Start fails, and MXRServicesBridge.m:596-599 returns 'The play queue is empty or cannot start.' as commandError. PlayerView.swift:156-162 then shows a centred card with a system .buttonStyle(.bordered) 'Retry Playback' button, which calls play() and fails again. The card is in the same ZStack as the centred cone and 'Open a media file' button and overlaps it. The error only clears when the media changes (VLCPlayerBackend.swift:156-157). The buffering indicator is also a system ProgressView (PlayerView.swift:155) rather than a Figma element.
findings.fix: Make canPerform(.playPause) return player.media != nil || !queue.items.isEmpty. With an empty queue, Play or Space should open the file panel, as macOS VLC does, or do nothing. Keep the error card for real input failures, build it from Figma dialog and secondary-button components, and make it mutually exclusive with the empty state (if/else, not ZStack).
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed. canPerform falls through to `default: true` (AppModel.swift:212). togglePlayPause calls backend.play() when stopped (PlayerModel.swift:91), and that fails at MXRServicesBridge.m:599. The error card at PlayerView.swift:156-162 uses a system .bordered button and sits in the same ZStack as the empty-state cone. This matches the owner's 'Retry Playback' screenshot.

findings.title: Top bar is not a window drag region, and double-clicking it does not zoom or minimize
findings.designEvidence: VIDEO_BREAKDOWN §03 SHOULD: 'The top bar is the window drag region.' spec-part1 §03 open question says the same. macOS title-bar convention: drag, and double-click per the user's 'AppleActionOnDoubleClick' setting.
findings.actual: There is no isMovableByWindowBackground, mouseDownCanMoveWindow, performDrag or WindowDragGesture anywhere (grep). Today only the separate AppKit titlebar strip from WT-01 can be dragged. Once WT-01 is fixed, at most the ~28pt that overlaps the AppKit titlebar will drag, and the rest of the bar will not. Double-click does nothing.
findings.fix: Put an NSViewRepresentable drag surface behind the top bar's non-interactive areas (spacers and title). It should return mouseDownCanMoveWindow = true or call window.performDrag(with:) on mouseDown, and on clickCount == 2 read UserDefaults 'AppleActionOnDoubleClick' and call performZoom or miniaturize. On macOS 15+, .gesture(WindowDragGesture()) is an alternative. Buttons must stay clickable.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed: no isMovableByWindowBackground, mouseDownCanMoveWindow, performDrag or WindowDragGesture anywhere. One nuance: today the separate AppKit strip still drags and zooms on double-click, so the problem becomes acute once WT-01 is fixed. In Hide UI there will then be no drag region at all, so put the drag surface on the canvas frame as well.

findings.title: Cursor never hides over fullscreen video
findings.designEvidence: VIDEO_BREAKDOWN §03: the UI vanishes when the pointer leaves; spec-part1 §03 leaves cursor auto-hide as an open question. VLC semantics: the core option mouse-hide-timeout (default 1000 ms) hides the pointer over video. macOS players (QuickTime, TV) hide it.
findings.actual: Neither Sources/ nor module/ calls NSCursor.setHiddenUntilMouseMoves or NSCursor.hide (grep). After the bars hide in fullscreen (PlayerView.swift:134-141), the arrow cursor stays over the video indefinitely.
findings.fix: Once both bars are hidden and the pointer is over the canvas (fullscreen, or an auto-hidden window), call NSCursor.setHiddenUntilMouseMoves(true) after the mouse-hide-timeout delay read from VLC. Do not hide it while a menu, popover or sheet is open.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed: there is no NSCursor usage in Sources or module. In VLC 4 on macOS, hiding the cursor is the GUI's job: the stock GUI does it in modules/gui/macosx/windows/video/VLCMainVideoViewController.m and VLCVideoWindowCommon.m, and the vout does not.

findings.title: Native menu bar (S11) uses Control shortcuts (⌃O, ⌃P, ⌃\, ⌃N…) and does not follow standard Mac menu conventions
findings.designEvidence: VIDEO_BREAKDOWN §05 SHOULD (macOS): 'Map Ctrl to ⌘ in displayed shortcuts… Hide UI is ⌘\'. spec-part1 §05: 'On macOS, map Ctrl to ⌘.' PHILOSOPHY §2.3: native manners.
findings.actual: ShortcutValues.swift:186-200 sets the defaults to 'Ctrl+\\', 'Ctrl+o', 'Ctrl+p', 'Ctrl+c', 'Ctrl+v' and so on, and MXRNativeMenus.swift:180-183 maps those to .control. The result is File › Open File(s) ⌃O, Settings ⌃P with no ⌘, and Hide UI ⌃\. ⌘O and ⌘, do nothing. Fullscreen is a checkmarked 'Fullscreen' item in the Video menu (MXRNativeMenus.swift:80, AppCommand.swift:54) rather than View › Enter/Exit Full Screen ⌃⌘F. There is no Help menu, and automatic window tabbing is not disabled, so AppKit can add tab-bar items.
findings.fix: Change app-action defaults to Command: Open ⌘O, Open Folder ⌘⇧O, Network ⌘N, Settings… ⌘, and Hide UI ⌘\, and spell them with ⌘ in the ⋯ menu. Move fullscreen to View as 'Enter Full Screen'/'Exit Full Screen' with ⌃⌘F. Add a Help menu. Set NSWindow.allowsAutomaticWindowTabbing = false. Add the ellipsis to 'Settings…'.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed for the shortcuts. ShortcutValues.swift:186-200 binds Ctrl+o, Ctrl+p, Ctrl+\ and so on, and MXRNativeMenus.swift:180-182 maps them to .control, so ⌘O and ⌘, do nothing. AppCommand.settings is titled 'Settings' with no ellipsis (AppCommand.swift:36). Partly refuted: Video › Fullscreen with VLC's own ⌘F binding is stock VLC-for-Mac semantics, not a defect. The real side effect is that AppKit auto-inserts 'Enter Full Screen' (and the tab-bar items, unless tabbing is disabled) into the existing 'View' menu, which duplicates the fullscreen item.

findings.title: Gallery entries override product defaults, so passing checks do not reflect the shipped window
findings.designEvidence: WORKFLOW and AGENTS: every UI change is checked visually against its Figma render. The check only means something if it renders what users get.
findings.actual: PlayerGallery.swift:62-79 renders a bare MXRPlayerView: no NSWindow titlebar, no reservesTrafficLights and no onPictureInPicture, so PiP, the 76pt reserve and the safe-area bug are never rendered. It forces showWaveform = false (:36, :52, :59, :66, :72) and figmaTitle (:140, :144), which hides the default filename-with-extension title and the waveform seek bar. S05.Player/fullscreen has no hover state, so it cannot show reveal behaviour. 'Canonical S01/S06 pixel-identical' in CODEX_STATUS.md is therefore true of the gallery and false of the app: C3, the waveform ticks and the PiP order all shipped unseen.
findings.fix: Add 'product' entries that use AppModel defaults and MXRAppView(reservesTrafficLights:true, onPictureInPicture:{}), hosted in a real titled NSWindow (or with an equivalent simulated safe area). Add S05 states for top-only and bottom-only reveal. Keep the Figma-matching overrides only in clearly labelled 'figma-fixture' entries.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed. PlayerGallery.swift sets showWaveform=false at :36, :52, :59, :66 and :72, and figmaTitle at :140/:144. S01 and S06 host a bare MXRPlayerView with no titlebar, no reservesTrafficLights and no PiP action. Every shipped defect found here (two rows, the reserve, waveform ticks, raw filename, PiP placement, fullscreen desync) is invisible to the gallery checks.

findings.title: Seek bar draws waveform tick marks over ordinary video by default (cross-area: root cause found while checking the window)
findings.designEvidence: Figma Player-6 and Controls 491:1779: a solid thick bar (black track, dark-accent fill, capsule handle). VIDEO_BREAKDOWN §02 MUST: the seek bar is thick. The waveform belongs to music (§09, Figma Controls music variant 4778:26181) or appears when the user enables Playback › 'Show Waveform on Seekbar'.
findings.actual: InterfaceModel.swift:161 defaults showWaveform to true. PlayerControls.swift:326-339 draws WaveformShape whenever the AVFoundation analysis returns samples, which it does for local MP4/MOV audio tracks, so every local video gets dense ticks. Codex's own 03-paused-e01.png and 17-fullscreen-live-video.png show this, and so does gallery S05.Player/fullscreen. The Figma-compared entries force the flag off (see WT-13).
findings.fix: Make showWaveform default to false for the video layout kind and true for music/audio-only, and persist it per kind. Remove the gallery overrides.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed (cross-area). InterfaceModel.swift:161 has showWaveform = true, and PlayerControls.swift:326-339 draws WaveformShape whenever samples exist. My S05.Player/fullscreen render and Codex's 03, 17 and 18 native screenshots all show ticks over plain video. Figma Controls 491:1779 is a solid bar. The waveform is the music variant 4778:26181, or an opt-in toggle (§07, §09).

findings.title: Focusable bar controls draw the system focus ring (purple accent) inside the chrome (cross-area)
findings.designEvidence: No Figma or video frame shows focus rings on bar controls. Figma control bar 491:1779 has no outline around the seek bar or the volume cone.
findings.actual: PlayerControls.swift:179 (volume cone) and :413 (seek bar) apply .focusable() without .focusEffectDisabled(). After a click, macOS draws its focus ring in the user's accent colour. Codex's own native screenshots show a purple rounded rectangle around the whole seek bar (03-paused-e01.png, 05-final-native-player.png). The same mechanism produces the square purple outline around the volume/'78 %' area in C1.
findings.fix: Add .focusEffectDisabled() to these controls. If keyboard focus must be visible, draw a Figma-consistent indicator only when Full Keyboard Access is on. The arrow-key handling already exists through window-level shortcuts, so the controls may not need to be focusable at all.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed for the seek bar: 03-paused-e01.png and 05-final-native-player.png show a purple accent ring around the whole seek bar. PlayerControls.swift:179 (volume cone) and :413 (seek bar) are .focusable() without .focusEffectDisabled(). The C1 link is plausible but was not directly observed. The '78 %' box is MXRVolumeTooltip, which has no stroke of its own (PlayerControls.swift:253-265). The ring is the system focus ring of the focusable 88×28 cone that the tooltip overlays.

findings.title: With the compact library open, the video loses its 10pt frame and rounded right corners
findings.designEvidence: Figma Player.png (187:328) and Player - Light (2425:13624): the canvas keeps the 10pt right frame and rounded right corners while the compact library overlays its left side. Side-by-side crop: scratchpad/review/window-topbar/corners-S28.png.
findings.actual: MXRAppView.swift:153-155 and :161-166: usesWholeWindowCanvas sets usesVideoFrame = false, so the video runs edge-to-edge to the right window border with square corners (gallery S28.App/compact; native 22-compact-library-retained-video.png). Toggling the library makes the frame appear and disappear, and the vout re-fits each time.
findings.fix: Keep videoInset and videoClipRadius in the compact-library composition, and let the library overlay the left of the framed canvas. Canvas geometry should not change when the library toggles.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed. My S28.App/compact render has the video running to x=1920 with square corners. Figma Player.png (187:328) keeps the ~10pt right frame and the rounded top-right corner. Cause: usesVideoFrame: !usesWholeWindowCanvas (MXRAppView.swift:165).

findings.title: Window title shows the raw filename with extension and underscores
findings.designEvidence: Native key frames 06m24.4 ('The Wand S01E04') and 11m57.0 ('The Wand S01E05', playing The_Wand_S01E05.mp4). spec-part1 §03: 'the media title ("The Wand S01E04")'.
findings.actual: AppModel+Preferences.swift:40-44 returns url.lastPathComponent when 'Show the file name in the title bar' is on (the default). The bar shows 'The_Wand_S01E04.mp4' (S05 render) and 'Test Show S01E02.mp4' (native screenshots). PlayerBars.swift:276-279 truncates in the middle and offers no tooltip.
findings.fix: Prefer the media meta title. For the filename option, use deletingPathExtension and optionally turn underscores and dots into spaces. Add .help(full title) to the centred title.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed, with stronger evidence. In Figma 970:3308 and 970:2703 the top-bar title is 'The Wand S01E04' (970:3317) while the library rows show the raw 'The_Wand_S01E05.mp4'. Native frame 11m57.0 shows 'The Wand S01E05' for The_Wand_S01E05.mp4. Figma Settings keeps 'Show the file name in the title bar' ON by default, so the fix is to clean the filename (drop the extension, turn _ and . into spaces), not to switch to meta only.

findings.title: PiP button is an extra item outside the layout, placed after fullscreen, with the wrong cell size; the canvas is blank while PiP is active
findings.designEvidence: Key frame 03-top-bar__window-controls-pip-fullscreen-option__04m00.7s: PiP sits to the left of maximize and fullscreen, in the same cell as the other window controls (Figma 247:466–469 are 36×24). D015 keeps PiP.
findings.actual: PlayerBars.swift:28-31 appends .pictureInPicture after all layout items, so the right edge reads [fullscreen][PiP]. It is not marked mxrLayoutDraggable, so Customize can neither move nor remove it. It uses the default MXRPlayerIconButton box, ControlBar.iconButton 30×32 (PlayerControls.swift:18), while fullscreen uses windowControlCell 36×24 (PlayerBars.swift:296), and the 32pt height overflows the 28pt content row. The gallery passes no PiP action, so this was never compared. While PiP is active the canvas is an empty black rectangle.
findings.fix: Put .pictureInPicture into PlayerLayout.video and PlayerLayout.music top before .fullscreen (and migrate saved layouts). Give it windowControlCell. Show a 'Playing in Picture in Picture' placeholder in the canvas while PiP is active.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed. PiP is appended after the layout items (PlayerBars.swift:28-31) with no mxrLayoutDraggable, and uses the default 30×32 box. PlayerLayout.video and .music end in .fullscreen (LayoutStore.swift:147, 153). 19-pip-detached.png shows an empty black canvas while PiP is active. The breakdown also says PiP ended up as a Customize tile, so it should at least be a removable layout item.

findings.title: Top-row layout measures items at ideal width: a long folder name pushes fullscreen and PiP outside the window and collapses the title
findings.designEvidence: D019: product windows are resizable and must degrade gracefully. Figma folderChip 247:459 is a compact chip.
findings.actual: PlayerBars.swift:146-171 measures every item with sizeThatFits(.unspecified) and places it at that width. The folder chip's Text is never truncated, so a long folder name makes the fixed width exceed the bounds. The flexible spacers drop to 0 and the trailing fullscreen and PiP buttons are placed past bounds.maxX, beyond reach at the 480pt minimum or with the 76pt reserve. The title width (bounds − 2·max(leading, trailing)) drops to 0.
findings.fix: Cap the folder chip width (e.g. 200pt, truncationMode .middle). In placeSubviews, shrink the chip and then the title before moving the trailing cluster, and anchor the trailing cluster to bounds.maxX.
findings.verifyNote: Plausible from code; not rendered, because the gallery never sets the reserve. placeSubviews measures every item with sizeThatFits(.unspecified) (PlayerBars.swift:146) and places them sequentially with no clamp. The folder chip's Text is never given less than its ideal width, so a long folder name at the 480pt minimum pushes fullscreen and PiP past maxX.

findings.title: Folder chip has no hover or pressed feedback
findings.designEvidence: Transcript 11:30: 'how am I supposed to know I should click on that' — making the chip read as clickable is the stated problem. Figma folderChip 247:459 has radius 6, a hit shape.
findings.actual: PlayerBars.swift:280-292 is a .plain Button with no hover background, unlike MXRPlayerIconButton, which uses iconHover and fg1.
findings.fix: Apply the same iconHover background (radius folderChip.radius) and fg1 tint on hover, plus a pressed state.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed in code (PlayerBars.swift:280-292: a .plain Button with no hover). The design evidence is weak: Figma has no chip hover state, and the 11:30 quote motivates the sidebar icon, not chip hover. It is justified only by PHILOSOPHY §4.1 (reuse the iconHover treatment).

findings.title: Fullscreen top-edge reveal is not coordinated with the macOS menu bar and titlebar reveal (to verify)
findings.designEvidence: VIDEO_BREAKDOWN §03: the top bar exists in fullscreen so the title stays readable ('86.8% look at the top').
findings.actual: No window(_:willUseFullScreenPresentationOptions:) is implemented, and the top bar reveal edge is 64pt (PlayerPreferences.swift:17-23). When the pointer reaches y=0, macOS slides down the menu bar and the transparent titlebar, which likely covers the cone, ⋯ and title that the top bar has just revealed. This was not observed directly; Codex's fullscreen screenshot was taken without the menu bar revealed.
findings.fix: Verify on hardware. If they overlap, offset the top bar by the menu-bar height while the menu bar is shown (watch NSApplication presentation and menu-bar visibility) or return [.fullScreen, .autoHideMenuBar, .autoHideDock, .autoHideToolbar] and test. Hide the traffic-light reserve in fullscreen (WT-01).
findings.verifyNote: Unverified, as the finding itself says. There is no willUseFullScreenPresentationOptions, and fullscreenHoverEdge defaults to 64 (PlayerPreferences.swift:17-23). The overlap of the menu bar and titlebar with the top bar at y=0 is likely but needs a hardware check.

findings.title: Player stays in the fullscreen layout after leaving fullscreen: isFullscreen is never refreshed from vout fullscreen changes
findings.actual: Codex's own 18-fullscreen-return-paused.png shows the window back in windowed mode (traffic lights visible), yet the fullscreen button shows the exit glyph and is 'button (selected) Fullscreen' in 18-fullscreen-return-paused.ax.txt:9. The video canvas is also edge-to-edge with no 10pt frame or radius, the layout PlayerView.swift:62-63/166-168 uses only when app.player.isFullscreen is true. Cause: PlayerModel.isFullscreen comes from VLCPlayerBackend.isFullscreen (VLCPlayerBackend.swift:63), which reads the MXRServicesBridge 'player' snapshot (MXRServicesBridge.m:486). That snapshot is reloaded only on services 'player' notifications, and MXRServicesBridge registers no vlc_player_vout listener (its callback tables at lines 203-213 have no on_fullscreen_changed). The vout fullscreen callback reaches only MXRPlayerBridge.applyFullscreen → session `.fullscreen`, which VLCClockBackend ignores (VLCBackends.swift:88) and only MXRAppController uses to drive the window. While playing, an unrelated event (statistics, state) refreshes it after a lag. While paused it stays wrong indefinitely: frame, bar hiding, opacity and hover rules are all still in fullscreen mode.
findings.fix: Make the UI's fullscreen state follow the real window. Either register vlc_player_vout_AddListener in MXRServicesBridge with on_fullscreen_changed → [self changed:@"player"], or have VLCPlayerBackend reload on session `.fullscreen`. Better still, set model state from windowDidEnterFullScreen/windowDidExitFullScreen in MXRAppController, since layout must match NSWindow.styleMask. Add a test that toggles fullscreen while paused and checks the model.
findings.designEvidence: VIDEO_BREAKDOWN §03 MUST: 'In the bars-hidden state in a window … thin frame … In fullscreen there is no frame'. Figma Player-6 (247:445) gives the windowed canvas its 10pt frame (6586:17371).

findings.title: VLC's own vout OSD (pause/play icons, 'Volume: N%', position text) is drawn on top of the redesign's OSD and volume tooltip (C7, cross-area)
findings.actual: 03-paused-e01.png, 17-cat-placement-dark.png and 18-fullscreen-return-paused.png all show the engine's large white '❚❚' pause icon at the top right of the video. In 18 it appears at the same moment as the redesign's 'Pressed ⌘F' OSD at the top left. The core draws these through vlc_player_osd_Icon/vlc_player_osd_Volume (src/player/osd.c:110-170, player.c:1349, aout.c:94), gated by var_InheritBool(vout, "osd") (video_text.c:99, video_widgets.c:289), and "osd" defaults to true. The redesign reads the same 'osd' option only to enable its own feedback (AppModel+Preferences.swift:69) and never suppresses the engine's. Changing volume therefore shows both the engine's 'Volume: 48%' and the redesign's '48 %' tooltip, each with its own timing.
findings.fix: Without touching the engine, create and set a bool "osd" = false on the object the vouts inherit from (the player or playlist object the bridge owns) when the interface starts. Keep the 'Show feedback for shortcuts' preference driving only MXRPlayerOSD. Extension OSD text goes through vout_OSDText in MXRServicesBridge.m:617 and also depends on that variable, so route it to MXRPlayerOSD instead.
findings.designEvidence: Distilled principle 6: 'One place per function, no duplicates.' §13 MUST: OSD feedback shows the action plus 'Pressed C' (key frame 13-…osd-shows-pressed-key__15m27.1s). No frame in the video or Figma shows VLC's legacy OSD glyphs.

findings.title: Sidebar-toggle active state is an orange outline; Figma and the native video show a gray filled-pane glyph
findings.actual: PlayerBars.swift:268-269 and :318 render .sidebarLeft (69:814) with state .active and highlightsActive true in dark mode, so the toggle turns orange when the library is open (S28.App/compact render; scratchpad sidebar-toggle-cmp.png). Light mode does the opposite (no highlight).
findings.fix: When the library is open, render MXRIcon(.sidebar, state: .active) (87:1041, the filled left pane) in the normal fgA2 tint in both themes, and drop the colorScheme special case.
findings.designEvidence: Figma Player.png (187:328): top-bar instance 247:426 is component 87:1041 'sidebar, state=active', a gray filled pane. Native key frame 08-library__compact-library-plus-queue-native__11m57.0s shows the same gray filled glyph.

findings.title: Dropping files onto the window gives no drop-target feedback
findings.actual: MXRAppView.swift:116-120 uses .dropDestination(for: URL.self) with no isTargeted handler. MXRVideoHost.swift:55-57 draggingEntered only returns .copy. Dragging media over the player shows nothing until it is dropped.
findings.fix: Track isTargeted (and draggingEntered/Exited in MXRVideoHostView) and show a Figma-consistent highlight: an accent inset stroke on the canvas frame plus an 'Add to queue / Play' label, honouring reduce motion.
findings.designEvidence: Distilled principle 13: 'Drag and drop is a first-class input … Every drop target shows where the item will land.' Transcript 2:30: 'Ideally you just drag files into the queue'.

grades.justification: Completeness = architecture conformance (50). Several parts conform: the layering (MXRUI sees only MXRCore/MXRDesign), the protocol-backed mock backend, ARCHITECTURE section 2.3 threading in the ObjC bridge (dispatch_async from callbacks, dispatch_sync only in vout enable, a report queue, joins off main), PlayerModel holding no time, and the build-glue touch budget in section 6. Major rules are broken: section 3.3 (overlays should be sibling hosting views, with no masks or opacity on the video and no blur over playing video), section 8 (CALayer playhead with no SwiftUI body work per tick, and coalescing in the bridge), section 5.7 (cancel and cache thumbnails), section 2.2 (typed bridge API instead of a [String: Any] RPC), and D004/PHILOSOPHY (unmodified engine). Fidelity is 0 because visual fidelity is not part of this area (n/a). Code quality (45): the Swift models, MXRCore and the tests are tidy and Swift 6 clean with almost no force unwraps. The ObjC bridge is a set of stringly god-objects with dense one-line control flow and 42 leftover __has_include guards. The hot paths re-snapshot the entire engine state for every event and every command. Gallery fixtures override product defaults and so hide real bugs.

doneWell: MXRIntf.m and MXRVoutWindow.m follow the stock startup, shutdown and vout-window patterns precisely: dispatch_sync to main only in WindowEnable, size and fullscreen reports on a private serial queue guarded by a lock, surface release deferred to main, MXRCloseIntf leaves NSApp the stock way, and finishShutdown joins every worker off main. Do not regress this.

Player, playlist and aout callbacks copy what they need and dispatch_async to main (never dispatch_sync), and every queued block checks _shutDown. This complies with ARCHITECTURE section 2.3 rules 1, 2, 5 and 7.

PlaybackClock is designed as intended: PlayerModel holds no time, displaySecond changes at most once per second, ticks are scheduled at second boundaries, interpolation follows vlc_player_timer_point semantics, and the display link runs only while playing with the bars visible. Fix the per-frame SwiftUI body work (ARC-08), not the model.

The layering is respected: MXRUI depends only on MXRCore and MXRDesign, the mock backend and gallery are not linked into the plugin, and the gallery plus the mxr-snapshot CLI (render, check, node, find) are excellent infrastructure that only needs a shipping-composition entry.

The upstream build-glue touch budget matches ARCHITECTURE section 6 line for line. configure.m4 validates the Swift toolchain, SDK and architecture, and the Swift library is force-loaded into the plugin with a packaging test.

One persistent video surface is reused across the player, library and mini player (D019) without recreating the vout, and PiP uses the same private PIPViewController path as stock, resolved dynamically.
The dark default theme uses opaque Figma tokens for the bars over video, as section 3.3 requires.
SeekPreviewModel already implements the section 5.7 debounce (80 ms) and quantization (max(2 s, length/300)). Only cancellation and caching are missing.
The Swift code is Swift 6 strict-concurrency clean, @MainActor throughout, with almost no force unwraps or try!.

The paused-seek investigation is rigorous: reproduced on the unmodified core with both avcodec and VideoToolbox, with LLDB frame variables and target-PTS assertions. It is a ready-made upstream bug report; reuse it for the VideoLAN issue (ARC-13).
The adapter tests decode recorded native fixtures, and the race and pagination tests in MXRCore are meaningful.

findings.title: Visual verification checks a mock gallery composition, not the window that ships, so defects pass review ('looks right, behaves differently')
findings.designEvidence: Figma renders/Player-6.png (node 247:445): one 40 pt top bar, cone at the left edge, solid thick seek fill. AGENTS.md hard rule: every UI change is checked against its Figma render. PHILOSOPHY section 2.6 (Verify visually).
findings.actual: `mxr-snapshot render --id S01.Player/default` (scratchpad review/architecture/s01-gallery.png) matches Figma almost exactly. Codex's own native screenshots of the real app show something else: build/logs/codex-final-c5793f73-native-ui/07-seekbar-position-midpoint.png and 24-final-native-player-preview.png have an extra empty titlebar strip of about 28 pt above the top bar, the cone indented by about 76 pt, a seek bar drawn as waveform tick marks on an ordinary MP4, a purple rectangular focus ring around the seek bar and its preview, and VLC's core OSD text 'Next frame' at the top right. Why the gallery cannot see any of this: (1) the gallery renders MXRPlayerView on its own, with no NSWindow, no titlebar safe area and reservesTrafficLights=false. (2) PlayerGallery.swift:36,52,59,66,72 set `app.interface.showWaveform = false` on every video fixture, which hides the product default `showWaveform = true` (InterfaceModel.swift:161). (3) MockServices draws OSD natively, while the VLC backend sends it to the core vout OSD (VLCServiceBackends.swift:233, MXRServicesBridge.m:617), so the two backends behave differently. CODEX_STATUS's own numbers are 13 PASS / 55 REVIEW / 30 FAIL out of 98 comparisons.
findings.fix: (1) Add 'shipping composition' gallery entries that host MXRAppView exactly the way MXRAppController.start() does: a titled NSWindow with fullSizeContentView, reservesTrafficLights: true, and an unmodified InterfaceModel. Compare them against Player-6 and Player - Light. (2) Add a test that fails when a gallery fixture assigns a product-default InterfaceModel or Preferences property, unless it is a declared scenario key. (3) Make a native-app 1920x1080 screenshot of S01/S03/S04 part of the definition of done. (4) Add behaviour contract tests that run the same scenarios (OSD routing, waveform eligibility, empty-queue play) against both MockBackend and the recorded VLC fixtures.
findings.verifyNote: Verified. I rendered S01.App/default (scratchpad review/engineering-verify/s01-app.png) and it matches Player-6.png: no titlebar strip, cone at x≈16. Codex's native captures 07 and 24 (build/logs/codex-final-c5793f73-native-ui) show the extra strip, the cone indented by about 76–80 pt, waveform ticks on an MP4, a purple focus rectangle around the seek bar and its preview, and the core 'Next frame' text. PlayerGallery.swift:36/52/59/66/72 force showWaveform=false against the product default at InterfaceModel.swift:161. MockOSD posts engine text natively, while the real bridge never emits 'osd'. This is the systemic reason all seven owner complaints were invisible to the review loop, so I kept it critical.

findings.title: Every player event and every command rebuilds the whole engine state 2–3 times, synchronously on main
findings.designEvidence: ARCHITECTURE section 8: 'Coalesce high-rate events (buffering, statistics, ML change bursts) in the bridge before hopping to main' and 'Split models so a time tick or buffering value invalidates only its view'. Section 2.3 rule 3: commands must not block. PHILOSOPHY section 2.4: idle CPU within 1% of stock VLC.
findings.actual: MXRServicesBridge.m:184-214 maps every vlc_player callback, including on_statistics_changed (about 1 Hz while playing), on_buffering_changed, rate, tracks and aout volume/mute/device, to `dispatchChange:@"player"`. VLCPlayerBackend.reload() (VLCPlayerBackend.swift:149-163) then calls `snapshot(for:"player")` = playerSnapshot (MXRServicesBridge.m:439-499). Under the player lock, that rebuilds dictionaries for every track, title, chapter, program, statistics and teletext. It also holds the vout and aout to read about 40 effect variables (MXREffectsServices snapshot), enumerates the audio devices and looks up the library cache. The result is diffed with NSDictionary isEqual across 25 field groups, and getters decode Effects/SubtitleStyle through a JSON round trip. Commands make it worse. VLCPlayerBackend.send() calls perform(). The bridge ends every player command with a synchronous `[self changed:@"player"]` (:606, :607, :686), which re-enters reload(). send() then calls reload() again (:139-147), and the engine callback adds a third snapshot afterwards. playerSnapshot also has a side effect: `[self applyPendingVolume]` calls vlc_player_aout_SetVolume from inside a getter (:484). Two separate vlc_player listeners (MXRPlayerBridge and MXRServicesBridge) also keep two sources of truth for player state.
findings.fix: Replace the 'something changed, re-read everything' bus with typed delta events per domain, for example onVolume(float, muted), onTracks(category), onState(state) and onCapabilities(mask), each carrying its payload. Coalesce them in the bridge so there is one main-queue hop per run-loop turn per domain. Commands must never call changed: synchronously; the engine callback is the only notifier. Do not register on_statistics_changed unless the Statistics panel is visible. Read effects only when an effects panel is open. Remove the side effect from playerSnapshot. Merge MXRPlayerBridge and the player part of MXRServicesBridge into one player service that owns one listener.
findings.verifyNote: Downgraded from critical: nobody has measured it. The chain is verified. PLAYER_CB at MXRServicesBridge.m:164-201 covers statistics, rate, tracks and aout; buffering goes through applyBuffering, which calls changed:. The command-path snapshots are performCommand → synchronous [self changed:@"player"] (:606/607/686) → sink → VLCPlayerBackend.reload, then send() calls reload() again (VLCPlayerBackend.swift:139-147). playerSnapshot (:437-499) takes the player lock, reads ~40 effect vars through vout/aout holds, lists aout devices and calls applyPendingVolume. Getters JSON round-trip (VLCServiceTransport.swift:84-86). One correction: play/pause/stop, setMuted, setFullscreen and selectAudioDevice do NOT call changed: synchronously, so 'every command' is overstated. Profile it with Instruments before the redesign. It is a plausible contributor to C6, but not proven.

findings.title: Scrubbing has no scrub session: seeks are unthrottled, the time label follows the engine instead of the pointer, and thumbnail requests pile up
findings.designEvidence: PHILOSOPHY section 3.3: the seek bar is thick and easy to hit, with thumbnails while seeking. VIDEO_BREAKDOWN S03 (thumbnail while seeking). ARCHITECTURE section 5.7: debounce, quantize, cancel the previous request (vlc_preparser_Cancel), LRU cache, never on main.
findings.actual: PlayerControls.swift:362-368 sends `app.player.seek(toPosition:, .fast)` on every DragGesture onChanged with no throttle or completion gating. Each event pays the 2–3 full snapshots described in ARC-02, which stalls main, so the bar and video update in jumps. FAST seeks land on keyframes, so the video only changes once per GOP, which is every few seconds on typical content. The current-time label (MXRTimeLabel, PlayerControls.swift:84) shows PlaybackClock.displaySecond, which is engine time; the drag target lives in private @State inside MXRSeekBar. The preview path has more problems. SeekPreviewModel cancels only the Swift Task (AppearanceAndPreviewModels.swift:99/108). VLCThumbnailBackend uses withCheckedThrowingContinuation with no cancellation handler (VLCServiceBackends.swift:137-151). The bridge never calls vlc_preparser_Cancel; it uses a single thumbnailer thread with an 8 s timeout and software decode (`hw_dec=false`), writes a PNG to /tmp, reads it back and deletes it (MXRThumbnailServices.m:35,49-70). There is no cache. Stale requests therefore queue up and the preview trails the pointer by seconds.
findings.fix: Add a ScrubController to MXRCore. Its begin(target) freezes PlaybackClock to the scrub target so the label and bar follow the pointer. update(target) sends FAST seeks at most every ~100 ms, or only after the previous on_seek(NULL) completion that MXRPlayerBridge currently ignores. end(target) sends one PRECISE seek. Make thumbnails cancellable: keep the vlc_preparser_req handle and call vlc_preparser_Cancel(prev) on each new slot. Use vlc_preparser_req_NewThumbnail (picture_t to CGImage in memory) with hw_dec=true, and an actor LRU per media keyed by quantized slot, prefetching neighbouring slots.
findings.verifyNote: The core finding holds: there is no scrub session, no completion gating and no PRECISE-on-release-only design (a plain click already sends FAST then PRECISE, PlayerControls.swift:363-371), and thumbnails cannot be cancelled. MXRThumbnailServices.m never keeps the req for vlc_preparser_Cancel and uses 1 thread, hw_dec=false and a PNG round trip through /tmp. Two claims are corrected. (1) The engine already coalesces seeks: input_ControlPush reduces same-type controls (src/input/input.c:1550) and postpones seeks up to 125 ms while buffering (:737-748), so seeks do not pile up in the engine; the cost is on main. (2) The time label does follow seek requests: vlc_player_input_SeekByPos calls UpdateTimerSeekState → timer on_seek (src/player/input.c:144) → MXRPlayerBridge cb_timer_seek → clock. SeekPreviewModel already debounces (80 ms) and quantizes, so requests queue up only when the pointer dwells. The 'every few seconds' video update while playing is mostly FAST keyframe granularity, which stock VLC shares. While paused it is the D020 stale-frame bug.

findings.title: Two volume indicators: VLC's core OSD 'Volume: N%' fires on every UI volume change, alongside the native tooltip
findings.designEvidence: Spec S04: the volume cone has its own '100 %' tooltip (Figma C.VolumeTooltip). ARCHITECTURE section 5.8: the core OSD is kept only for hotkey feedback, and the native OSD toast is top-left (S13).
findings.actual: vlc_player_aout_SetVolume sets the aout 'volume' variable. Its callback (src/player/aout.c:89-95) always calls vlc_player_osd_Volume, which draws 'Volume: %ld%%' into the vout OSD channel at the top right. The UI tooltip shows PlayerModel.volume, which is refreshed by a separate snapshot path (_pendingVolume/_acceptedVolume, MXRServicesBridge.m:600-608), so the two numbers are rendered at different moments from different sources. adjustVolume(steps:) adds a step to a model value that can still be stale. `showMessage` also sends the same text to the core OSD (TOP|RIGHT, MXRServicesBridge.m:617) and to the native OSD (VLCServiceBackends.swift:233), which duplicates it. VLCOSDBackend's 'osd' listener is dead because no 'osd' service is ever emitted.
findings.fix: Suppress the core OSD for changes the UI makes itself. vout_OSDText checks `var_InheritBool(vout, "osd")` synchronously (src/video_output/video_text.c:98), so in the bridge: hold all vouts, `var_Create(vout,"osd",VLC_VAR_BOOL)`, set it false, call SetVolume/Mute, then restore it. Alternatively, adopt section 5.8's fully native OSD. Make showMessage native-only. Update PlayerModel.volume from the float payload of on_volume_changed, not from a re-snapshot.
findings.verifyNote: Verified. src/player/aout.c:89-95 calls vlc_player_osd_Volume on every volume var change, which draws 'Volume: N%' TOP|RIGHT (video_text.c:140). This is C7. Corrections: OSDModel.showEngineMessage has no callers, so the showMessage duplication is latent, not live. Both the tooltip and the core OSD read the aout value after the synchronous reload, so 'different sources' is overstated; the visible problem is two indicators with different position, style and lifetime. The volume OSD is one instance of a broader problem: core OSD is left on for every action (see the missed OSD finding). A per-call var toggle is fragile; disable 'osd' once on the player object instead.

findings.title: The seek bar of ordinary videos is drawn as a waveform, and the app decodes the whole soundtrack of every opened video
findings.designEvidence: VIDEO_BREAKDOWN section 09: for audio files the seek bar can become a waveform when 'Show Waveform on Seekbar' is on. Figma Player-6.png: a video uses a solid orange seek fill. The waveform appears only in the music variant (4778:26191).
findings.actual: InterfaceModel.swift:161 defaults `showWaveform = true`. PlayerControls.swift:326 shows the waveform whenever samples exist, without checking isAudioOnly. MXRAudioServices.m:348-366 accepts any local file with an audio track, MP4 and MKV included, and AVAssetReader decodes the entire track to 22 kHz float on every media open. Swift never sends `cancelWaveform` (it appears nowhere in Sources), so stale analyses of long movies block the serial queue. Codex's own native screenshot 07 shows tick marks on 'Test Show S01E01.mp4'. The gallery hides the problem by forcing showWaveform=false (see ARC-01).
findings.fix: Gate on `app.player.isAudioOnly && interface.showWaveform` and never request a waveform for video media. Default the toggle to the design's behaviour (audio only). Wire task cancellation to `cancelWaveform` (withTaskCancellationHandler). Cache peaks on disk, keyed by path, mtime and size.
findings.verifyNote: Verified. PlayerControls.swift:326/335 gate only on samples plus showWaveform, with no isAudioOnly check. The default is true (InterfaceModel.swift:161). MXRAudioServices.m accepts any local file URL, AVAssetReaderAudioMixOutput decodes the whole first audio track at 22050 Hz, and Swift never sends cancelWaveform. Stronger design evidence: key frame 07-sidebar__playback-tab-full-toggles__09m17.5s.jpg shows 'Show Waveform on Seekbar' OFF while a video plays, and VIDEO_BREAKDOWN:449 ties the waveform to music. Correction: there is a 24-entry in-memory cache keyed by path, mtime, size and bins, so re-opening a file in the same session is cached. A new long movie still blocks the serial _waveQueue for later requests, and the per-sample double division in the bin loop is expensive.

findings.title: System focus rings (accent-coloured squares) appear around the volume cone with its '78 %' tooltip and around the seek bar with its preview
findings.designEvidence: Figma C.VolumeTooltip (S04) and C.SeekPreview (S03): rounded surfaces with no outline. No component in Figma has a focus outline.
findings.actual: MXRVolumeCone applies `.focusable()` (PlayerControls.swift:179) and so does MXRSeekBar (:413), after the tooltip/preview `.overlay` and without `.focusEffectDisabled()`. A click gives the view focus, and macOS draws the keyboard-focus ring in the user's accent colour (purple here) around the view's bounds, overlay included. Codex's screenshot 07 shows exactly that purple rectangle enclosing the seek bar and its thumbnail. The same pattern exists at SettingsControls.swift:301, SettingsEqualizerView.swift:68 and MXRCustomizationView.swift:73. A secondary risk: MXRBackdropSurface wraps NSVisualEffectView in SwiftUI clipShape, which does not always round AppKit material layers, so check that square material edges do not show behind the rounded tint.
findings.fix: Add `.focusEffectDisabled()` to the custom controls. Where keyboard access matters, draw a Figma-styled indicator only for keyboard focus (@FocusState plus a NSEvent-driven 'last input was keyboard' flag), or use `.focusable(interactions: .edit)` so clicks do not take focus. Keep the arrow-key handling.
findings.verifyNote: Verified. `.focusable()` sits at PlayerControls.swift:179 (cone, after the tooltip overlay) and :413 (seek bar), plus SettingsEqualizerView:68, SettingsControls:301 and MXRCustomizationView:73. focusEffectDisabled appears nowhere. Native capture 07 shows the accent-coloured rectangle enclosing the seek bar and preview, the same mechanism as C1. A possible secondary 'square edge': PlayerOutsideShadow (PlayerMenus.swift:156-168) masks the shadow to rect+15 pt, but menuShadow is y=8 with radius 7.5, so the shadow is cut by a hard straight edge below the tooltip on bright video. Give the mask padding blur+|y|.

findings.title: The titlebar safe area is not ignored, producing two rows (traffic-light strip plus 40 pt bar), and the cone is pushed right by a borrowed token
findings.designEvidence: Figma Player-6.png: a single 40 pt top bar with the cone at x=0. D007: native traffic lights inside the Figma top bar. D019: a shared 40-point top bar.
findings.actual: MXRAppController.swift:65-80 creates a titled, fullSizeContentView window and sets `contentView = NSHostingView(rootView: scene)`. Nothing in Sources calls ignoresSafeArea or sets safeAreaRegions (grep finds no matches), so SwiftUI lays the whole scene out below the ~28 pt titlebar safe area and the top bar becomes a second row (native screenshots 07 and 24). A fixed reserve is also inserted at the left (PlayerBars.swift:18). `MXRPlayerMetrics.trafficLightReserve = Theme.Metric.ControlBar.timeLabel.width` (PlayerMetrics.swift:38) is an unrelated token reused to satisfy the 'no literal sizes' rule.
findings.fix: Apply `.ignoresSafeArea()` at the root of the hosted scene, or set `NSHostingView.safeAreaRegions = []` on macOS 14+. Vertically centre the traffic lights in the 40 pt bar by repositioning `standardWindowButton(_:).superview` on resize and fullscreen exit, or by using a titlebar accessory of matching height. Replace the borrowed token with a reserve measured from AppKit (zoom button maxX + Figma gap). Only another reviewer can judge whether the cone itself should sit after the traffic lights (D007).
findings.verifyNote: Verified. Nothing in Sources uses ignoresSafeArea or safeAreaRegions, and no code in MXRPlugin touches standardWindowButton. NSHostingView in a fullSizeContentView window therefore insets SwiftUI below the titlebar, giving two rows (C3). trafficLightReserve = ControlBar.timeLabel.width (76; Tokens.swift:738) is token laundering. Per D007, the cone SHOULD sit after the traffic lights, so the reserve is correct once the bar occupies the titlebar row; the defect is the extra row plus traffic lights that are not centred in the 40 pt bar. Addition: reservesTrafficLights is passed as true unconditionally (MXRAppController.swift:77), and the reserve at PlayerBars.swift:18 has no fullscreen check. In fullscreen, where macOS hides the traffic lights, the cone stays indented by 76 pt.

findings.title: The playhead and subtitle timeline re-evaluate full SwiftUI bodies on every display frame
findings.designEvidence: ARCHITECTURE section 8: 'The playhead is a CALayer moved by an NSView.displayLink callback only while the bar is visible and playing. No SwiftUI body re-evaluation on ticks.'
findings.actual: PlayerDisplayLink (PlayerControls.swift:386-391, 474-493) writes @State `position` on every CADisplayLink tick. The whole MXRSeekBar body is rebuilt each time: GeometryReader, ZStack, restore-prompt layers and, when a waveform is shown, two WaveformShape paths of up to 244 rounded rects plus a mask. That is 60–120 times a second for as long as the bars are visible during playback. MXRSubtitleTimelineView (SubtitleTimeline.swift:48-51) uses TimelineView(.animation), which rebuilds every cue segment, four buttons and a gesture per frame. Its body also recomputes all cue segments from the full cue list whenever displaySecond changes.
findings.fix: Use an NSViewRepresentable SeekTrackView with CALayers (track, fill, head) and CAShapeLayer waveform paths cached per size. The display-link callback only sets fill width and head position inside CATransaction.setDisableActions(true). Treat the timeline the same way: a cue layer cached per viewport window, with only the playhead layer moving.
findings.verifyNote: Verified: the display link writes @State position every tick (PlayerControls.swift:387-391) and SubtitleTimeline uses TimelineView(.animation). That breaks ARCHITECTURE §8 (table row at line 1080). Downgraded because the link runs only while the bars are visible during playback (the `active:` condition at :388), and the bars auto-hide. Cheap interim fix: on a 1238 pt bar a 25-minute film moves ~0.8 pt/s, so skip writes unless the head has moved at least 0.5 px.

findings.title: The video lives inside one full-window SwiftUI tree with a mask, bars are hidden with opacity, and live blur sits over playing video
findings.designEvidence: ARCHITECTURE section 3.3: overlays are small sibling hosting views above MXRVideoSurfaceView; never apply opacity < 1, filters or masks to the surface; set isHidden after the fade; no blur, vibrancy or glass over playing video in the default appearance.
findings.actual: MXRAppController.swift:76-80 places the vout NSView as an NSViewRepresentable (MXRVideoHost.swift:69-72) inside a single window-sized NSHostingView. PlayerView.swift:166 applies `.clipShape(.rect(cornerRadius:))` to the ZStack that contains the video, which is a mask over AVSampleBufferDisplayLayer and so an extra compositing pass and EDR risk. Bars are hidden with `.opacity(barOpacity)` (:69, :78), so they stay in the render tree, along with their NSVisualEffectViews where those are used. MXRBackdropSurface (NSVisualEffectView, withinWindow) sits over the video in Light mode and in library/customization chrome (PlayerBars.swift:36-38, 83-85), and also in the volume tooltip, seek preview, menus, the error card (PlayerView.swift:161) and the settings sidebar (SettingsSidebar.swift:66). Dark-mode bars do use opaque tokens, which is good.
findings.fix: Build an AppKit root (MXRPlayerRootView) with the surface plus sibling NSHostingViews for the top bar, control bar, right panel and OSD, as section 3.3 specifies. Draw the rounded video frame as an overlay above the video (an inverse-corner shape in the bar colour) instead of masking the video. Set isHidden=true after the fade completes. Over playing video, use solid tokens and keep materials for static backdrops, or make them an opt-in glass theme (D008).
findings.verifyNote: Downgraded. The divergence from ARCHITECTURE §3.3 is real: one window-sized NSHostingView, clipShape over the vout host at PlayerView.swift:166, and bars hidden by opacity. But no user-visible defect is shown; capture 24 renders the rounded video frame correctly. The blur claim conflicts with Figma: C.VolumeTooltip 2245:9805 and C.SeekPreview 2151:9673 both specify BACKGROUND_BLUR r=50 under a 95% fill, so blur on those surfaces is design-specified. A solid 95% fill would look nearly identical and is a defensible optimisation, not a fidelity fix. The C5 attribution is wrong: C5 is the sidebar's visual composition, which the panels reviewer covers.

findings.title: Pressing play with an empty queue leaves a permanent 'The play queue is empty or cannot start. Retry Playback' card
findings.designEvidence: Figma has no such state. Idle shows the 'Open a media file' affordance (PlayerView.swift:146-152 already draws it). PHILOSOPHY section 2.3 (native manners).
findings.actual: MXRServicesBridge.m:593-599: play/togglePause in STOPPED state calls vlc_playlist_Start and turns its failure (empty queue or invalid index) into an NSError. VLCPlayerBackend.send() stores it as commandError (:139-147), which surfaces as errorMessage. PlayerView.swift:155-161 renders a card whose 'Retry Playback' button calls play() again and fails the same way. The error is cleared only by a media change or a state recovery.
findings.fix: Treat play/toggle on an empty queue as 'open media' (request .openFiles) or as a no-op. Keep validation failures of commands out of PlayerModel.errorMessage, which should come only from on_error_changed. Show transient command failures as an OSD or toast.
findings.verifyNote: Verified: MXRServicesBridge.m:590-599 turns a vlc_playlist_Start failure into an NSError; commandError then becomes errorMessage and the card renders at PlayerView.swift:156-162. Corrections and additions: (1) any later successful player command also clears it (VLCPlayerBackend.swift:142-145), not only a media change or recovery. (2) vlc_player_Start also returns EGENERIC during the stopping race (src/player/player.c:1237-1255), so the message can appear with a non-empty queue. (3) The card shares a ZStack with the 'Open a media file' button (PlayerView.swift:147-162), so both draw on top of each other when media is nil. (4) It uses a stock `.buttonStyle(.bordered)` that is not in Figma. (5) Every validation failure, including the PiP fallback 'Player command setPictureInPicture is unavailable' from PlayerBars.swift:249, lands in the same playback-error card.

findings.title: Every seek while paused shows a stray core 'Next frame' OSD at the top right
findings.designEvidence: S13: OSD feedback is the native toast at the top left. Upstream API: include/vlc_player.h:3355 on_next_frame_status. src/player/input.c:941-953 shows the OSD only when no listener handles the status.
findings.actual: Upstream displays a frame for a seek while paused through the next-frame path: vlc_input_decoder_Flush sets frames_countdown=1 when paused (src/input/decoder.c:2793-2797), then decoder_Notify(frame_next_status, 0) runs. No listener is registered (MXRServicesBridge.m:202-214 has none), so the player draws 'Next frame' through the core OSD. It is visible in Codex's screenshot 07; CODEX_STATUS records it and leaves it unexplained.
findings.fix: Register `.on_next_frame_status` and `.on_prev_frame_status` in the bridge's vlc_player_cbs. That suppresses the OSD and also gives a deterministic 'the frame for the paused seek is on screen' signal, which can end the scrub or thumbnail state from ARC-03.
findings.verifyNote: Verified. The path is decoder.c:2793-2797 (upstream, not from D020) → decoder_Notify(frame_next_status, 0) → vlc_player_input_FrameNextStatus (src/player/input.c:941-953). It draws 'Next frame' only when no listener exists, and MXRServicesBridge's PlayerCallbacks (:202-214) registers none. Registering the listener also suppresses the modal vlc_dialog_display_error for -EBUSY/-EINVAL/-ENOTSUP ('no video found', input.c:925-934), for example when frame-stepping audio. Register on_prev_frame_status too.

findings.title: D020 engine patches (clock.c, decoder.c, es_out.c): the bug is real and also affects stock VLC 4, but the fix should be reverted from the UI branch, quarantined and taken upstream
findings.designEvidence: PHILOSOPHY section 2.1 and D004: the engine is not modified; exceptions must be small, isolated and upstreamable. ARCHITECTURE section 6 lists only build glue. Upstream tracker titles found by search: 'seek on pause no longer updating' (https://code.videolan.org/videolan/vlc/-/issues/25315) and 'Time/position not updated after seek while paused' (https://code.videolan.org/videolan/vlc/-/issues/22456, https://trac.videolan.org/vlc/ticket/22456). Historic upstream work on the same flags: https://mailman.videolan.org/pipermail/vlc-devel/2008-October/052132.html and https://mailman.videolan.org/pipermail/vlc-commits/2015-June/030776.html.
findings.actual: (1) Does stock VLC have the problem? Almost certainly. The stock macOS UI (VLCControlsBarCommon.m:412-440 to VLCPlayerController.m:1200-1221, vlc_player_SeekByTime/SeekByPos FAST or PRECISE) and Qt (player_controller.cpp:1375-1430, vlc_player_SetTime/SetPosition) call the same player API with no paused-specific path. Neither listens to on_next_frame_status, and neither uses vout_NextPicture or NextVideoFrame. Codex reproduced the stale frame on the unmodified core with both avcodec and VideoToolbox, with LLDB evidence (build/codex-paused-seek-evidence-before-core/apple-review.md). vlc_input_decoder_Wait breaks immediately when paused (decoder.c:2957), StopWait clears b_waiting, and the first post-seek picture is then unforced and dropped as late. Upstream API alone cannot fix this. I did not run the stock build/arm64/VLC.app GUI to confirm by eye; it would take two minutes. (2) Is the patch good? The first hunk (decoder.c:1524-1526, force the first picture while paused) and the es_out.c:3726-3729 system_now change are narrow and arguably the right upstream fix. The upstream rebuffering work (ec61ad7474 and be5cd7a749, Sept 2026) already handled only b_rebuffering. The other hunks are a cascade: each fix exposed the next failure. clock.c:397-400 keeps pause_date across reset, and clock.c:680-683 rebases the monotonic fallback. decoder.c:2904-2908 calls Decoder_ChangeOutputPause, and therefore vout_ChangePause, from the input thread while holding the FIFO lock, which breaks decoder.c's own rule that only DecoderThread drives outputs while running. These hunks change A/V-sync semantics in the core's most actively reworked area: frames_countdown was reworked in 7dedecf9e7 (2025-11) and rebuffering landed in Sept 2026. The merge-conflict and regression risk is high, and no upstream reviewer has seen it. AGENTS.md was also edited to drop 'unmodified' (it now reads 'on top of an **VLC engine**').
findings.fix: Recommendation: REVERT the four src/ hunks from claude/polish and restore AGENTS.md wording. (a) Move the hunks, plus tools/test-clock-pause-reset.* and module/tests/paused-seek-*, to a separate branch `engine/paused-seek` (one commit per hunk) and open a VideoLAN issue and MR with the native reproduction. Lead with the decoder first-picture and es_out hunks, and justify clock.c and the ChangePause hunk separately or drop them if upstream fixes the root cause differently. (b) If the owner wants the fix in local builds before upstream accepts it, carry it as an explicit patch file (redesign/patches/) applied by build-native.sh, with a version check that fails loudly after upstream merges. Never as silent edits under src/. (c) Ship the UI-side mitigations regardless: ARC-12 (on_next_frame_status) and the scrub thumbnail as a still image while paused (ARC-03).
findings.verifyNote: Verified. Commit 67d2711555 changes src/clock/clock.c (+10), src/input/decoder.c (+11) and src/input/es_out.c (±6). The ChangePause hunk calls Decoder_ChangeOutputPause from the input thread under the FIFO lock, and the same hunk rewrites decoder.c's ownership comment to permit that. AGENTS.md lost 'unmodified'. Upstream commits ec61ad7474/be5cd7a749 (2026-09-17) and 7dedecf9e7 exist. I did not verify the external tracker URLs. The owner states the engine must stay untouched, so quarantining the patch as a patch series is right. Note: reverting re-exposes the stale-frame-after-paused-seek bug. Land the UI mitigation (thumbnail held as a still while paused, plus ARC-12) in the same change.

findings.title: Stringly-typed bridge boundary: a 3-method [String: Any] RPC, about 234 string-compare dispatches, and keys that Swift reads but ObjC never writes
findings.designEvidence: ARCHITECTURE section 2.2: per-domain protocols, a bridge with Foundation types only, NS_SWIFT_UI_ACTOR sinks. D003: a thin, typed bridge.
findings.actual: MXRBridgeAPI/include/MXRServicesBridge.h exposes only snapshotForService:/performCommand:service:arguments:/request:service:arguments:. The bridge dispatches on strings: MXRServicesBridge.m has 94 isEqual:@ checks, MXRLibraryServices.m 48, MXRMediaServices.m 37 and MXREffectsServices.m 22. Swift parses with silent defaults (VLCServiceTransport.swift extension). Several keys are consumed but never produced: `snapshotURL`, so the .snapshotTaken event never fires; `isPictureInPicture`, so the PiP button never shows as active and setPictureInPicture fails with 'Player command … is unavailable' when onPictureInPicture is nil; plus `external`, `scrambled`, `isMenu` and `fileName`. MXRServicesBridge.m still has 42 `#if __has_include("MXR…Services.h")` guards around its own headers, left over from integrating parallel worktrees.
findings.fix: Move to typed ObjC per-domain services, for example MXRPlayerService with typed methods and an NS_SWIFT_UI_ACTOR delegate carrying typed payloads, and MXRQueueService, MXRSettingsService and so on. Swift then gets compile-time checking. As an interim step, generate one shared key enum for ObjC and Swift and add a contract test that fails when Swift reads a key that no native fixture contains. Delete the __has_include guards.
findings.verifyNote: Verified. Over module/bridge/*.m, grep finds 0 producers for snapshotURL, isPictureInPicture, "external", scrambled, isMenu and fileName. isEqual:@ counts are 94/48/37/22, and MXRServicesBridge.m has 42 __has_include guards. Concrete user-visible consequences: takeSnapshot never gives feedback (.snapshotTaken never fires), and the PiP button never shows as active.

findings.title: Changing one setting re-enumerates every VLC config option at least three times on main
