findings.designEvidence: ARCHITECTURE section 2.3 rule 3: commands do not block main. Section 5.2: settings get/put with live apply.
findings.actual: setConfig ends with a synchronous `[self changed:@"settings"]` (MXRServicesBridge.m:820). That triggers VLCSettingsBackend.reload(): settingsSnapshot runs module_list_get over every option of every module with gettext (:513-546), rebuilds the schema and diffs all values. The VLCShortcutsBackend listener also fires, ShortcutsModel.reload reads `actions`, and that computed property takes a shortcuts snapshot plus another full settings snapshot (VLCServiceBackends.swift:13-27). VLCSettingsBackend.setValue then calls reload() again (:19-23). Settings sliders repeat all of this for every tick.
findings.fix: Build the schema once at startup and on rescanPlugins. Send `valueChanged(name, value)` deltas. Shortcuts should read only key-* and global-key-* options and should not depend on settings events. Never reload synchronously inside a command.
findings.verifyNote: Verified. setConfig → synchronous changed:@"settings" → VLCSettingsBackend.reload (a full module_list_get/module_config_get/gettext walk at MXRServicesBridge.m:513-546 plus rebuildSchema). VLCShortcutsBackend listens to 'settings' too, and ShortcutsModel.reload → backend.actions takes another full settings snapshot (VLCServiceBackends.swift:13-27). setValue then reloads a third time. This is worse than stated: the effects commands (setVideoEffects, setAudioEffects, setSubtitleStyle, setTrackDefaults and others; MXRServicesBridge.m:580-588) emit both 'player' and 'settings'. Every EQ, brightness or subtitle-style slider tick in the right sidebar therefore pays player snapshots plus two full config walks. The C5 link is wrong: C5 is visual.

findings.title: Literal sizes in views, plus 'token laundering' to get around the no-literals rule
findings.designEvidence: AGENTS.md hard rule: 'No literal colors or sizes in views.' Tokens come from redesign/design/tokens through gen-tokens.py.
findings.actual: Literal frames with Figma-node comments: EffectsSidebars.swift:14,18,109,209,213,223 (48/40/37/68x32/52/37), SettingsSidebar.swift:197,199 (180x38, 50), QueuePanel.swift:123,158 (64, 34), PanelControls.swift:265 (22x22), VideoFilterInspector.swift:94 (37). findings.title: The 15 worst code hotspots, with refactor advice
findings.designEvidence: ARCHITECTURE section 2 (layering, thin bridge). PHILOSOPHY section 2.7 (small, explained changes).
findings.actual: 1) module/bridge/MXRServicesBridge.m (955 lines / 65 KB): one god object for player, queue, settings, shortcuts and capabilities; 94 string compares; 42 __has_include guards; getters with side effects; one-line multi-statement methods. 2) Sources/MXRVLCBackend/VLCPlayerBackend.swift: about 40 computed properties that re-parse a dictionary on every read, JSON round trips, and a 1012-character line 160 holding the diff table. 3) VLCServiceTransport.swift plus MXRServicesBridge.h: an untyped RPC. 4) module/bridge/MXRMediaServices.m (915 lines): output, extensions and renderers in one file. 5) module/bridge/MXRDiscoveryServices.m (636 lines). 6) module/bridge/MXREffectsServices.m: 29 lines over 200 characters, nested ternaries, and it includes another module's private `../../../../audio_filter/equalizer_presets.h`. 7) module/bridge/MXRThumbnailServices.m: all control flow on single lines, a temporary PNG file round trip, no cancel. 8) module/bridge/MXRLibraryServices.m (48 string compares). 9) Sources/MXRUI/Player/PlayerControls.swift (494 lines): seek bar, cone, time label and preview in one file, with per-frame body work. 10) Sources/MXRUI/Player/PlayerView.swift: a hover/hide state machine built from Tasks inside a View, plus the error card and the video mask. 11) Sources/MXRUI/Settings/MXRSettingsView.swift (492 lines / 28 KB). 12) Sources/MXRUI/Panels/PanelControls.swift and EffectsSidebars.swift: literal geometry. 13) Sources/MXRCore/App/AppModel.swift (390 lines): wiring, preferences and command routing in one type. 14) Sources/MXRGalleryCatalog/GalleryCatalog.swift (1830 lines / 92 KB), whose fixtures override product defaults. 15) Sources/MXRVLCBackend/VLCServiceBackends.swift: shortcut grouping by substring (group(_:)), the dead 'osd' listener, and thumbnails with no cache or cancel.
findings.fix: For 1-3, split the bridge into typed per-domain ObjC services, one statement per line, with delta events (ARC-02, ARC-14). For 2, decode once into a typed `PlayerSnapshot` struct. For 4-8, apply the same per-domain split and use table-driven maps; replace the private header include by copying the preset table or querying the equalizer module's config choices. For 9, extract ScrubController (MXRCore), an AppKit SeekTrackView and a VolumeCone file with generated paths. For 10, extract ChromeVisibilityController. For 11-12, split per category and move geometry into tokens. For 13, separate AppModel composition from command routing (AppCommand handler). For 14, split per domain and lint that fixtures do not override defaults. For 15, read shortcut groups from vlc_actions metadata or a checked-in table.
findings.verifyNote: The figures check out: VLCPlayerBackend.swift line 160 is 1013 characters, GalleryCatalog.swift is 1830 lines, MXRSettingsView 492, AppModel 390, MXRServicesBridge.m 955, and MXREffectsServices.m has 29 lines over 200 characters. This is a summary of the other findings, not a separate defect.

findings.title: Tests: model and adapter tests are solid; the visual tests are ceremonial and the native tests are not wired up
findings.designEvidence: WORKFLOW definition of done (verify loop). ARCHITECTURE section 8 (measure, don't guess).
findings.actual: Meaningful: MXRCoreTests (clock interpolation, transport, restore prompt, media request races, pagination); MXRVLCBackendTests (decoding of recorded native fixtures, command-error recovery); tools/test-clock-pause-reset.c (13-case clock contract). Ceremonial: GalleryRenderTests.testEveryEntryRenders (:36-50) only asserts the size and that the image is not fully transparent, and testFigmaNodesExistAndMatchEntrySizes checks bounding boxes but no pixels. The native ObjC runtime tests (module/bridge/tests/*.m with *.md instructions) and module/tests/paused-seek-smoke.m are not part of any make target, and their instructions hardcode ../build/arm64. Missing regressions: waveform eligibility (audio only), empty-queue play, no full snapshot per command (count snapshots), seek throttle and scrub label, window composition (top bar at y=0), and a ObjC/Swift key contract.
findings.fix: Wire the native tests into `make check-macosx-redesign`, with paths taken from configure and media fixtures generated by a script. Add the regressions listed above. Have snapshot tests compare with tolerance against Figma crops for the S01/S03/S04 components instead of only 'renders'. Move the engine tests with the patch series (ARC-13).
findings.verifyNote: Verified. testEveryEntryRenders only checks size and that some pixels are opaque. check-macosx-redesign (Makefile.am:61-75) runs only `swift test` plus test-packaging.py. module/bridge/tests/*.md hardcode ../build/arm64, and module/tests/paused-seek-* are not wired up.

findings.title: Documentation bloat, and governance documents edited to fit the work
findings.designEvidence: DECISIONS.md header: short records. AGENTS.md hard rules. PHILOSOPHY section 2.1.
findings.actual: redesign/docs/CODEX_STATUS.md is 313 lines / 31 KB, in Russian unlike every other doc. findings.title: Build evidence (13 GB) and stale worktrees (~3.4 GB): what is safe to delete

findings.actual: ../build is 13 GB. findings.title: Small isolation and touch-budget leaks
findings.designEvidence: ARCHITECTURE section 6 (whole conflict budget) and section 2 (the bridge is the only code that includes vlc headers; additive module).
findings.actual: The build glue is exactly as planned (configure.ac +1, modules/gui/Makefile.am +1, package.mak +5 conditional), which is good. Small leaks remain. MXREffectsServices.m:11 includes another plugin's private header `audio_filter/equalizer_presets.h`. MXRPlatformServices.m includes `../../../macosx/private/PIPSPI.h`, which is acceptable reuse but undocumented in section 4. Makefile.am:54 claims the global `install-data-local:` target inside the shared modules/Makefile, so any upstream module that adds one will break the build. applyConfig (MXRServicesBridge.m around line 786) calls var_Create on aout/vout objects for every setting change without a matching var_Destroy, leaking references. module/tests and tools/test-clock-pause-reset.* compile engine internals (src/clock) from the UI module.
findings.fix: Copy the equalizer presets table or query `equalizer-preset` choices from config. List the PIPSPI reuse in section 4. Use a uniquely named install hook chained through install-data-local only if no other one exists, or install through the plugin's own data rule. Create each var once per object or use var_SetChecked on existing variables. Move the engine tests with ARC-13.
findings.verifyNote: Verified. MXRAudioPreferenceServices.m:10 ALSO includes the private equalizer_presets.h, not only MXREffectsServices.m:11. Makefile.am:54 claims install-data-local; no other modules/ Makefile.am defines it today. var_Create at :775 is refcounted, and the references are freed with the object, so this is churn rather than an unbounded leak.

findings.title: The core VLC OSD is left on for every action, so the S13 two-line OSD is split across opposite corners and legacy VLC text and sliders appear over the redesign
findings.designEvidence: VIDEO_BREAKDOWN §13 MUST (line 584): the OSD shows two lines, the action ('Crop: 2.35:1') and then 'Pressed C'. Key frame 13-bookmarks-chapters-osd__osd-shows-pressed-key__15m27.1s.jpg shows them stacked and left-aligned. Transcript [15:00]: she wishes the message showed the shortcut that was pressed. ARCHITECTURE §5.8 assumes the native line sits 'aligned under the core OSD (top-left)', but core OSD messages are TOP|RIGHT (src/video_output/video_text.c:140).
findings.actual: Nothing sets the 'osd' variable to false: module/ has no '"osd"' reference. So: every seek-bar drag event calls vlc_player_osd_Position (src/player/input.c:152, osd.c:121-152), which draws '00:12:34 / 00:25:40' at the top right, plus VLC's legacy horizontal slider widget in fullscreen. Play and pause draw core icons (player.c:1292/1349). Every tick of the sidebar Speed slider draws 'Speed: %.2fx' (player.c:1430). Tracks, chapters and 'Subtitle slave added' also draw core text. Shortcuts go through key-action (MXRServicesBridge.m:857-861), so the hotkeys module draws the action text at the top right, while OSDModel.keyPressed (AppModel.swift:313-314, ServiceModels.swift:204) draws 'Pressed C' natively at the top left (PlayerView.swift:91-95, MXRPlayerOSD). OSDModel.engineDisplayed never fires because VLCOSDBackend waits for an 'osd' service the bridge never emits (VLCServiceBackends.swift:232). MockOSD posts the engine text natively, so the gallery shows a correct stacked S13 and hides the bug. The Settings rows 'Show feedback for shortcuts' and its duration control only the native half.
findings.fix: At bridge start, call `var_Create(VLC_OBJECT(player), "osd", VLC_VAR_BOOL); var_SetBool(..., false)`. Vouts inherit it through the dummy-vout → player parent chain (input_resource_New(VLC_OBJECT(player)), resource.c:312/424), the engine stays untouched, and 'spu' stays on so subtitles still render. UI-initiated changes then need no OSD, because the control is its own feedback. For hotkeys, generate the action text natively from the resulting model change, or from a table on ShortcutAction (rate, crop, aspect, track, chapter, jump, volume), and show both lines in MXRPlayerOSD. Register on_next/prev_frame_status (ARC-12). Update ARCHITECTURE §5.8 and add a mock/VLC contract test so the backends cannot diverge again. This also resolves C7 (ARC-04).

findings.title: The track popover (C2/C4) is vertically centred mid-right, appears with no transition, and can only be dismissed by its own button
findings.designEvidence: Figma Controls 'Property 1=subtitles' 491:2216: popover 491:2243 (400×524) sits at x=1500, y=-544 relative to the 54 pt bar. Its bottom edge is 20 pt above the bar and its right edge 20 pt from the window edge, i.e. anchored bottom-right above the track buttons. Video key frame 04-track-popover__audio-tab-tracks-output-device__04m42.4s.jpg shows the same placement, directly above the audio, subtitle and gear icons.
findings.actual: MXRAppView.swift:52-59 and :81-89 place MXRRightPanelView with `.overlay(alignment: .trailing)`, which centres it vertically in the canvas. The gallery render of S14.App/subtitle-tracks (scratchpad review/engineering-verify/s14-app.png) puts the popover at y≈270–795 of 1080, a floating mid-right card. rightPanel changes have no .transition or .animation, whereas the '⋯' menu is a native Menu with the system NSMenu animation, hence the inconsistency in C4. Dismissal works only by clicking the toggle button again, or with Esc through `.onExitCommand` (TrackPopover.swift:19), which requires keyboard focus inside the popover. There is no click-outside dismissal.
findings.fix: Use `.overlay(alignment: .bottomTrailing)` with bottom/trailing padding of Theme.Metric.panelInset (20 pt), or anchor the popover to the triggering button with anchorPreference so it tracks the button in customised layouts. Add `.transition(.opacity.combined(with: .offset(y: 8)))` with a tokenised duration that honours accessibilityReduceMotion, animated on rightPanel. Add a transparent click-catcher over the video that calls closeRightPanel, and route Esc through MXRKeyRouting whenever a popover is open.

findings.title: Media-library events are not coalesced, and each one triggers a database count plus full player and queue snapshots on main
findings.designEvidence: ARCHITECTURE §8: 'Coalesce high-rate events (buffering, statistics, ML change bursts) in the bridge before hopping to main.' PHILOSOPHY §2.4: CPU usage close to stock VLC.
findings.actual: LibraryEvent (MXRLibraryServices.m:38-43) calls engineChanged for every vlc_ml event. That runs vlc_ml_count_media on the work queue, then on main clears the whole _mediaCache and emits 'library' (:74-85). MXRServicesBridge changed: (:403) also emits 'player' and 'queue' for every library change, so each ML event costs a full playerSnapshot (ARC-02), a queue snapshot and a library contentChanged reload. Because the cache was cleared, playerSnapshot's cachedMediaForURL starts an async 'media' request, and its completion emits 'player' again (:62-70), adding one more full snapshot per event. A library scan or thumbnail pass produces thousands of MEDIA_ADDED/UPDATED events, which hits the main thread hard while video plays.
findings.fix: Coalesce ML events in the bridge (for example with a 250 ms dispatch_source) so each burst costs one count query and one 'library' emission. Emit 'player' only when the event's media id matches the current item, and 'queue' only when it matches a queued item. Invalidate only the affected cache entries instead of removeAllObjects.

refuted.note: Refuted. This toolchain (Swift 6.4) expands @Observable setters to `guard shouldNotifyObservers(_v, newValue) else { _v = newValue; return }`, with `lhs != rhs` for Equatable (I checked with swiftc -dump-macro-expansions on a scratch file). Assigning `areBarsVisible = true` when it is already true does not invalidate any view. MXRAppView.swift:142/149 use .onHover, which fires only on enter and exit, not per mouse move. The only residue is a stylistic one: the hide timer is a Task inside a View.

grades.justification: Completeness: every screen and all 13 Settings categories exist. Missing or dead parts: the Recording Advanced Options bar, the video dim in Customize mode, a usable Light theme, about 6 settings that do nothing, 15+ rows shipped as 'unavailable', Convert limited to MP4, Stream limited to HTTP. Fidelity: the gallery renders are near pixel-perfect against Figma (Settings, Shortcuts, Add Subtitles, Network, New Playlist, onboarding). But the gallery runs on mock data and hides how the real app behaves. The real app shows raw VLC action ids ('vol-up'), raw values ('-1'), 'unavailable' captions, and system menus and popovers instead of the Figma popup; Customize mode collapses the control bar; Light theme makes headings invisible. These are exactly the 'looks right at first glance, behaves differently' failures. Code quality: the catalog-driven design (D013) and the models are sound. Against that: developer notes leak into UI copy, a layout-value default bug, a fixed-offset onboarding canvas, a scaleEffect hack that shrinks dialogs, two dropdown implementations (neither is the Figma one), sheets nested three deep, and app options that are registered but never read.

doneWell: Settings static fidelity is excellent. All 13 category pages (gallery S48.Settings/*) match the Figma 'Settings - *' renders almost row for row: the window chrome, App/Media/System nav card with the orange filled icon on the selected row, section headings, her square ON/OFF toggle, segmented Theme, 9 accent swatches, the stacked 'Remember last volume / Always starts at' control, color fields with swatch, sliders with scale labels, and the inline 'Advanced Options' bar that expands below with the chevron turning down. Keep these metrics (SettingsMetrics.swift) and SettingsControls' visual code.

Catalog-driven Settings (settings-map.json5, D013) with human-word composites: Repeat Off/All/One, 'When playback finishes', Buffering presets that enable custom ms fields, 'Fetch titles and artwork', and subtitle fuzziness as Off / Any title / Contains title / Title with extra characters / Exact title match. Dependent rows dim to 30% as the spec requires (Library, Network buffering). Changes save live, with debounced persistence.

The Keyboard Shortcuts layout (S64) matches Figma pixel for pixel, including the narrow stacked variant, conflict highlighting and capture isolation, so captured keys don't reach playback (only the over-broad blocking needs fixing, SD-09).

Add Subtitles (S25-S27): all four Figma states match, including the dashed connector, the hover swap icon on the right cell, orange checkmarks and the Cancel/Save styling. SubtitleMatcher auto-matching runs when files load, and a generation token cancels stale target loads.

Open Network Stream and New Playlist match Figma closely. Save stays disabled until the input is valid. The drop zone draws Figma's per-edge dash pattern and accepts dropped files. The disabled-button luminosity treatment is faithful.

Customize Player palette (S66/S67): tile grid, labels, dashed icon boxes, a tile disappearing once placed, Save turning primary only after a change, Cancel reverting, and context-menu and accessibility alternatives to dragging. These are good; only the bars in edit mode are broken (SD-02).

Onboarding (S69-S71) matches all Figma frames: 3 steps, a live mini-player preview that recolors with the 9 accents (AccentPalette's documented HSB derivation produces convincing accents), and keycaps read from live bindings rather than hard-coded.
The profile model (ProfileStore) snapshots and applies all settings per profile, and profile switching is blocked during customization.

findings.title: Real Keyboard Shortcuts dialog lists raw VLC action ids ('vol-up') instead of human action names
findings.designEvidence: Figma Keyboard Shortcuts.png (2437:14832) shows 'Toggle fullscreen', 'Exit fullscreen / close dialog', 'Play / pause'. Spec-part2 section 14 C. PHILOSOPHY principle 9 'Use your words'.
findings.actual: module/bridge/MXRServicesBridge.m:556 sets each engine action's name to its id (@"name":S(names[i])), and Sources/MXRVLCBackend/VLCServiceBackends.swift:17 uses that as the title. Codex's own real-app screenshot ../build/logs/codex-final-native-ui/07-relaunch-engine-shortcut.png shows the row 'vol-up' and the capture sheet titled 'vol-up' (04-nested-shortcut-existing-control.png). Only the 'app-*' actions have human titles. The gallery looks right only because MockServices.swift supplies titles.
findings.fix: Take the title from the key option's text: config_FindConfig("key-"+id)->psz_text, passed through vlc_gettext. Overlay a curated table for the Figma wording (Toggle fullscreen, Exit fullscreen / close dialog, Show playback position and time, ...). Never fall back to the id. Add a test asserting that no visible title matches /^[a-z0-9+-]+$/.
findings.verifyNote: CONFIRMED. MXRServicesBridge.m:556 sets @"name":S(names[i]) and VLCServiceBackends.swift:17 uses it as the title. The real-app screenshots build/logs/codex-final-native-ui/07-relaunch-engine-shortcut.png (row 'vol-up') and 04-nested-shortcut-existing-control.png (capture sheet titled 'vol-up') show the bug. The fix source is correct: src/libvlc-module.c add_key("key-*", ..., *_KEY_TEXT) carries translatable texts such as VOL_UP_KEY_TEXT 'Volume up'. One caveat: some texts are empty, e.g. key-projection-toggle has "" at :2606, so the curated overlay table is required. A related defect has the same root cause. VLCServiceBackends.swift:37-46 groups actions by substrings of the id, so leave-fullscreen, position and intf-show fall into 'Other', and play-pause/stop/next/prev land in 'Basic'. Figma puts Toggle fullscreen / Exit fullscreen / Show position / Show controls in Basic and Play/Stop/Next/Previous in Playback. The curated table should also assign groups.

findings.title: Customize Player edit mode breaks both bars: seek bar collapses to a stub, right-hand groups float mid-bar
findings.designEvidence: Figma Player - customize.png (2107:5604) and video 19m12.4 (key-frame 15-customize-onboarding__customize-edit-mode-native): every bar keeps its real layout, outlined. Full-width seek group; window/fullscreen group at the right edge. The editor must be WYSIWYG.
findings.actual: Two causes. (1) Sources/MXRUI/Player/PlayerBars.swift:61 wraps each bottom row in ScrollView(.horizontal) while customizing. The ScrollView proposes unbounded width, so PlayerRowLayout falls back to its minimum: the seekBar gets playButton width and flexible items get 0. (2) PlayerBars.swift:26 and :118 add a trailing drop target (Color.clear width 8) with no layoutValue. PlayerControlKey.defaultValue is .spacer (line 125), so the target becomes a flexible spacer and takes a third of the free width; in the top bar the fullscreen button lands near x=1335 of 1920. Seen in check render S66_App_customization (render_bottom.png / render_top.png) and in Codex's real-window screenshots codex-final-c5793f73-native-ui/23-cat-dark-customization.png and codex-final-native-ui/25-customization-baseline.png: '00:02:09 [|] 00:25:40' squeezed to about 40 pt.
findings.fix: Drop the horizontal ScrollView in edit mode. If overflow is a concern, use the same ViewThatFits path as normal mode. Give the trailing drop target an explicit .layoutValue(key: PlayerControlKey.self, value: .dropSlot) of zero flexible width, or render it as an overlay instead of a layout child. Add a gallery assertion that seekBar width in edit mode equals its width in normal mode.
findings.verifyNote: CONFIRMED by code and image. PlayerBars.swift:61 wraps the row in ScrollView(.horizontal) while customizing. PlayerRowLayout.sizeThatFits (:130-141) then falls back to its minimum: the seekBar gets playButton width and flexible items get 0. The trailing drop targets at :26 and :118 have no layoutValue, so they default to PlayerControlKey.defaultValue = .spacer (:125), which isFlexible (LayoutStore.swift:76). My S66.App/customization check shows the seek bar as a stub, the right-hand group packed at x≈400-720 of 1920, and the empty rest of the bar. The real screenshot 25-customization-baseline.png shows '00:00:06 [|||]00:01:00' with the ticks overlapping the duration. The editor is not WYSIWYG.

findings.title: Light theme makes section headings, the selected category, dialog headings and shortcut names invisible
findings.designEvidence: VIDEO_BREAKDOWN section 14 MUST: 'Changing the theme or accent recolors the whole UI live' (17m44.0 light frame). Design principle 16: 'Light theme and any of the 9 accents must work for every new component.' tokens/colors.json meta warns that the Light palette is an unverified mapping table, and that Light/FG/1 and FG/2 equal the dark values.
findings.actual: Sources/MXRDesign/Generated/Tokens.swift:275-276 copies light fg1=#EAEAEA and fg2=#C6C6C6 unchanged onto a #E7E7E7 background (contrast about 1.0:1). fgA4 at :280 is #3B3B3B, so placeholders, info icons and the OFF knob are as dark as body text. Results: general-light render (r_S48_Settings_general-light.png) loses 'Appearance/Startup/Diagnostics' and the selected 'General' label. light_S64_KeyboardShortcuts_default.png hides every action name and key, because MXRKeyboardShortcutsView.swift:114 and :129 use fg2. light_S36_NetworkStream_empty.png hides 'Network URL' and 'Playlist Name', and its placeholders look like entered values. App-only tokens (homeCard #171717, volumeBody, thumbPlaceholder, swatchOutline) are identical in both themes.
findings.fix: Record a DECISIONS entry that corrects the Light mapping: fg1 about #161616, fg2 about #2E2E2E, fgA4 a light gray about #9A9A9A for placeholders and disabled text. Give every app-defined token a light value. Add a contrast test (WCAG >= 4.5 for fg1/fg2/fgA1 on bgB1/bgA1 in both themes) and gallery light variants for every dialog.
findings.verifyNote: CONFIRMED. Tokens.swift light fg1=#EAEAEA and fg2=#C6C6C6 sit on bgB1 #E7E7E7. My renders: general-light hides Appearance/Startup/Diagnostics and the selected 'General' label. S64 light hides every action name and key, and the gray search field reads like a disabled control. S36 light hides 'Network URL' and 'Playlist Name'. The default theme is dark (MXRAppOptions.inc:3), which limits exposure. But Light and System are offered in Settings and onboarding, and choosing them makes Keyboard Shortcuts unusable, so critical stands. colors.json:13/514 already flags the Light palette as an unverified mapping.

findings.title: Dropdowns show raw engine values ('-1', blank, '-') when the VLC value isn't in the curated choice list
findings.designEvidence: VIDEO_BREAKDOWN section 14 MUST: 'There are no numeric codes. Use dropdowns of plain options.' Figma Settings - global.png shows Log details = 'Errors only'.
findings.actual: Sources/MXRUI/Settings/MXRSettingsView.swift:396 calls SettingsChoiceMenu(title: settings.selectedChoiceTitle(for: row) ?? settings.string(row)). VLC's default log-verbose is -1 (modules/logger/file.c:243), which is outside the catalog choices [0,1,2]. Codex's real screenshot codex-final-c5793f73-native-ui/18-settings-system-intermediate.png shows 'Log details  -1'. The same path renders sout-x264-preset (default NULL) as a blank dropdown and 'Default optical drive' as '-'.
findings.fix: Map every engine default to a choice. Add [-1, 'Errors only'] (or normalize -1 to 0). For NULL string defaults, add an 'Automatic' choice with value ''. Fallback: show the engine's own choice text, otherwise 'Custom'; never str(value). Add a test that loads real VLC defaults through the catalog and asserts that every dropdown resolves to a title.
findings.verifyNote: CONFIRMED. MXRSettingsView.swift:396 falls back to settings.string(row). logger/file.c:243 defaults log-verbose to -1, and real screenshot 18-settings-system-intermediate.png shows 'Log details  -1'. sout-x264-preset defaults to NULL (codec/x264.c:706) and has no '' choice, so the dropdown is blank. 'Default optical drive' is worse than described: the catalog (settings-map.json5:230) defines ONLY [['', '-']], so it is a one-item dead dropdown. Fix correction: -1 does not mean 'Errors only'. It means 'inherit the global verbosity' (file.c:137-138; VLC labels it 'Default'). Add [-1, 'Default'] rather than mapping -1 to Errors only.

findings.title: Developer notes ('verify', 'verify enum values') show to users in the info popovers
findings.designEvidence: VIDEO_BREAKDOWN section 14 MUST: 'The info icon shows the setting's explanation on click.' PHILOSOPHY principle 9: human-readable explanations.
findings.actual: Sources/MXRCore/Resources/settings-map.json5:48 has info 'Needed for Show Statistics in the player. verify' (General > Advanced > Collect playback statistics). :275 has info 'verify enum values' (Video > Framing > Zoom). :559 has info 'verify' (Performance > Developer > Encoder). Catalog info overrides the engine longtext (SettingsModel.swift:170), so these strings appear verbatim when the icon is clicked.
findings.fix: Move review markers to JSON5 comments or a separate 'review' key. Write real explanations. Add a catalog lint that fails when an info string contains 'verify' or 'TODO'.
findings.verifyNote: CONFIRMED. settings-map.json5:48 reads '... in the player. verify', :275 reads 'verify enum values' and :559 reads 'verify'. SettingsModel.info(for:) (:170-174) prefers catalog info, so these strings are shown verbatim. Downgraded to minor: the text only appears after clicking the info icon on 3 rows, 2 of them inside Advanced. It is still an embarrassing leak and a trivial fix, and the lint idea is good.

findings.title: Settings that silently do nothing, and info popovers that only repeat the label
findings.designEvidence: CODEX_STATUS claims 'unsupported operations show availability rather than acknowledge success'. Principle 9: an info icon on every setting that explains it.
findings.actual: These rows are registered in module/MXRAppOptions.inc and listed in settings-map.json5, but nothing in Sources/ or module/ reads them: 'Interface language' (macosx-redesign-language, line 15, 12 languages; the app has no localizations), 'Cipher preference' (:527), 'Process priority' (:553), 'Allow the app icon to change' (:117), 'Show the file browser inside the open dialog' (:116), and 'Show window decorations' (video-deco, :79), which does nothing for the embedded custom window. Separately, 35 app options register a longtext equal to their label (e.g. 'Cipher preference'/'Cipher preference', 'Vertical position', 'Cast quality'). MXRSettingsView.swift:303 shows an info icon whose popover repeats the title.
findings.fix: Remove the dead rows, wire them up, or mark them unavailable through SettingsAvailability. Write a real explanation for each of the 35 options, or hide the info icon when the info text equals the label. Add a test that every macosx-redesign-* option in the catalog has a consumer.
findings.verifyNote: CONFIRMED, with corrections. The cited line numbers (15, 527, 553, 117, 116, 79) are settings-map.json5 lines, not MXRAppOptions.inc lines; the language option is MXRAppOptions.inc:2. A grep over Sources/ and module/ finds no consumer for macosx-redesign-language, cipher-preference, process-priority, dynamic-icon or open-dialog-browser. The list is incomplete. Also unconsumed: show-errors, developer-mode, minor-warnings, pause-on-interruption, visualization-size and audio-device (see missed finding SD-M3). The 35 options whose longtext equals the label are confirmed by script (theme, accent, remember-window, autohide-delay, ... cast-quality), and real screenshot 18 shows info icons on Theme and Accent color that the Figma lacks. The video-deco claim is plausible but unverified at runtime.

findings.title: 15+ 'unavailable in this build' rows clutter the real Settings, including a dead Skin section that opens the Interface page
findings.designEvidence: Figma Settings - interface.png / privacy / controls / subtitles / recording show clean rows. VIDEO_BREAKDOWN section 14: Settings in human words, no clutter. Skins are a Qt/Windows feature with no macOS meaning.
findings.actual: SettingsAvailability.swift:16-31 together with MXRServicesBridge.m:118 mark these rows unavailable: update-check, custom-skin, skin-file, 4 Last.fm rows, web remote (+port/password), cast discovery, cast quality, and 4 subtitle-style rows. MXRSettingsView.swift:317-323 dims the label to 30% but draws the caption at full fgA1, so the caption is brighter than its own label. Real screenshot codex-final-native-ui/35-interface-pref-baseline.png: the Interface page opens with 'Custom skins are unavailable in this interface' twice, and the disabled 'Use a custom skin' toggle reads ON (default true in MXRAppOptions.inc:10). 'Discover cast devices' is unavailable even though CODEX_STATUS claims renderer discovery works.
findings.fix: Hide rows that cannot work on macOS (Skin section, tray, decorations) through a catalog 'platforms' or 'requires' key. Keep a single disabled state, with the explanation only in the info popover. Never show a disabled toggle as ON. Make the Skin defaults false.
findings.verifyNote: CONFIRMED. SettingsAvailability.swift:16-31 and MXRServicesBridge.m:118 UnsupportedSetting cover 11 app options plus the Last.fm engine options. MXRSettingsView.swift:317-323 dims the label to 30% but draws the caption at full fgA1. Real screenshot 35-interface-pref-baseline.png shows the Interface page opening with two 'Custom skins are unavailable in this interface.' captions brighter than their labels, and a disabled toggle reading ON (MXRAppOptions.inc:10 default true). Screenshot 18 shows the same pattern for 'Check for updates automatically'. Note that the Figma itself shows the Skin section with the toggle ON, so hiding it needs a DECISIONS entry (macOS adaptation).

findings.title: Windows shortcut defaults on macOS: Settings is Control-P (not Command-comma), Open is Control-O, About is Shift-F1; L clashes with VLC's macOS audio-track key
findings.designEvidence: VIDEO_BREAKDOWN section 15 SHOULD (macOS): 'the shortcuts screen shows Command-based keys where VLC for macOS uses them'. Section 14 SHOULD: Settings opens with Command-comma. PHILOSOPHY 2.3 'Native first'. VLC's own macOS defaults (src/libvlc-module.c:2284+): fullscreen Command+f, next/prev Command+Right/Left, volume Command+Up/Down, audio-track 'l', subtitle-track 's'.
findings.actual: Sources/MXRCore/Values/ShortcutValues.swift:186-202 sets app defaults to key('Ctrl+o'), ('Ctrl+p') for Settings, ('Ctrl+c') for Capture, ('Ctrl+v'), ('Shift+F1'), and 'l' for Show/Hide File Browser. MXRNativeMenus.swift:178-180 copies these into the menu bar, so Settings shows Control-P and there is no Command-comma. In VLC's macOS defaults 'l' is audio-track, so L now has two bindings. The onboarding shortcut screen and the in-window menu show these Windows bindings.
findings.fix: Use macOS defaults: Command-O, Command-Shift-O, Command-N for network, Command-comma for Settings, Command-R / Command-Shift-S, an About item without a shortcut; move File Browser off 'l'. Keep the Figma 'Ctrl + O' styling only for display. Run the conflict check against VLC's Apple defaults in tests.
findings.verifyNote: CONFIRMED, with corrected evidence and a stronger failure. Figma Profiles.png/menu.png literally show 'Ctrl + O', 'Ctrl + P' (Settings) and 'Shift + F1' (About), so Codex copied the Windows design. VIDEO_BREAKDOWN §15 SHOULD (macOS) and §14 SHOULD (Command-comma opens Settings) override it. The real conflicts are worse than stated: VLC's Apple defaults (src/libvlc-module.c ~2378-2382) bind Ctrl+p=title-prev, Ctrl+n=title-next and Ctrl+d=chapter-next. The app's Settings (Ctrl+p), Open Network (Ctrl+n) and Open Disc (Ctrl+d) collide with them, and 'l' collides with audio-track. MXRAppController.swift:102-114 resolves the binding to one action, so one of each pair silently loses. Onboarding reads live bindings (MXROnboardingView.swift:297-311), so on first run it shows 'Cycle Audio Track L' next to 'Show / Hide File Browser L'. Fix correction: do not 'keep Ctrl + O for display'; display the macOS glyph form (⌘O), and record a DECISIONS entry.

findings.title: While Keyboard Shortcuts or Onboarding is open, every menu key equivalent is blocked: Command-V, C, A, Z and Q do nothing
findings.designEvidence: PHILOSOPHY 2.3 Native first. Text fields must support paste. Command-Q must always work.
findings.actual: Sources/MXRPlugin/MXRNativeMenus.swift:28-30 passes isCapturing = isCapturingShortcut || sheet == .keyboardShortcuts || sheet == .onboarding into MXRKeyRouting.shouldPerformMenuEquivalent, which returns false for every event (MXRKeyRouting.swift:21-22). The Edit menu delivers paste:/copy:/selectAll: to text fields, so you cannot paste into 'Search Keyboard Shortcuts...' or the onboarding media-folder field, and Command-Q is blocked on the first-run screen. Inconsistent: the same dialog opened from Settings > Controls is a nested sheet with sheet == .settings, where nothing is blocked.
findings.fix: Block menu equivalents only while ShortcutCaptureSheet is recording (isCapturingShortcut). Always allow Edit-menu and Quit equivalents.
findings.verifyNote: CONFIRMED. MXRNativeMenus.swift:26-30 passes isCapturing=true for sheet == .keyboardShortcuts or .onboarding. MXRKeyRouting.shouldPerformMenuEquivalent then returns false (:21-22), and MXRMenuBar.performOnMainActor (:235) skips super. Paste in 'Search Keyboard Shortcuts...' and in the onboarding folder field, plus Command-Q on first run, are therefore blocked. No test covers it. The fix is right: gate only on isCapturingShortcut.

findings.title: No dropdown matches Figma's popup: Settings uses an arrowed system popover, Add Subtitles a plain NSMenu, the Profile submenu a popover of bare buttons
findings.designEvidence: Figma sub filename.png and Dropdown.png (2372:8300): popup directly under the field, same width, BG/A1, radius 6, about 46 pt rows, selected row highlighted with an orange check on the right, no arrow (video 17m31.0 key-frame 14-settings__dropdown-human-words). Figma target.png (1959:5325) and origin.png (1963:5465) for Add Subtitles scope/source. Figma Profiles.png (6648:20666) for the Profile submenu: orange check on the LEFT, labels indented, '+ New'.
findings.actual: Settings: SettingsControls.swift:152 uses .popover(arrowEdge: .bottom), giving NSPopover chrome, an arrow and system material, with 32 pt rows (controlInnerHeight), no hover, and no arrow-key navigation. Add Subtitles: DialogMenu.swift:24-32 builds a plain NSMenu, so the system menu font and look apply and the current item gets no check (item.state is never set). In-window menu: PlayerMenus.swift:130-152 (PlayerSubmenuRow) opens a popover of plain Buttons; the Profile list draws HStack{Text; check} with the check after the name and 'New Profile...' as text (PlayerMenus.swift:26-37). The pixel-correct MXRProfilesView (gallery S68 PASS) only appears as a modal sheet through 'Manage Profiles'.
findings.fix: Build one MXRDropdownPopup component: a borderless child NSPanel or a SwiftUI overlay anchored under the field, no arrow, with Figma metrics, hover row, check, keyboard navigation and Esc. Use it for Settings, Add Subtitles, the Shortcuts 'All Fields' filter and the language menu. Render MXRProfilesView as the submenu next to the Profile row.
findings.verifyNote: CONFIRMED. SettingsControls.swift:152 uses .popover(arrowEdge: .bottom) with 32 pt rows and no hover. Figma Dropdown.png shows an arrowless list under the field with taller rows and an orange check on the right. DialogMenu.swift:24-32 builds a plain NSMenu and never sets item.state. PlayerMenus.swift:26-37/130-152 renders the in-window Profile submenu as a click-to-open popover with an arrow, the check AFTER the name, and the text 'New Profile...'. Figma Profiles.png puts the check on the left, indents the labels and uses '+ New'. MXRProfilesView (gallery S68 PASS) already matches and should be reused.

findings.title: Every dialog is a top-attached macOS sheet: no scrim, dialogs nest up to 3 levels, and small screens get a uniformly shrunk dialog
findings.designEvidence: Spec-part2 section 14 A: Settings is a modal centered in the window, with the player behind visibly lightened by a scrim (BG/B2 Transparent). The video shows Add Subtitles centered over the player (06m02.5) and Customize centered (19m12.4). Section 14 SHOULD: Settings is a separate window opened with Command-comma.
findings.actual: MXRAppView.swift:124 presents all AppSheets with .sheet(item:), which attaches to the top edge with no dimming. Settings > Controls > Edit Keyboard Shortcuts opens a sheet on top of the Settings sheet (MXRSettingsView.swift:89), and editing a key opens a third sheet (MXRKeyboardShortcutsView.swift:86). MXRAppView.swift:207-215 scaleEffect()s non-Settings dialogs down when the screen is smaller than the Figma size, so text renders below 14 pt and blurs. It also measures NSScreen.main rather than the window's screen.
findings.fix: Present Settings as its own NSWindow (Command-comma, one instance, remembers its frame), styled per Figma. Present the other dialogs as a centered in-window overlay with a BG/B2-Transparent scrim and a fade/scale-in transition (honor Reduce Motion). Make dialogs lay out responsively (ScrollView body) instead of scaleEffect. Open Keyboard Shortcuts as a peer window or replace the Settings content, not as a nested sheet.
findings.verifyNote: CONFIRMED. MXRAppView.swift:124 presents every dialog with .sheet(item:). :197-216 scaleEffect()s all dialogs except Settings, Shortcuts and Profiles, and measures NSScreen.main. MXRSettingsView.swift:89 and :216 nest Shortcuts as a second sheet, and MXRKeyboardShortcutsView.swift:86 adds a third for capture. Evidence nuance: spec-part2 §14 (line 343) only says the backdrop is 'probably a scrim', and line 494 lists the separate window as OPEN. VIDEO_BREAKDOWN §14 MUST ('large centered window') and SHOULD (separate window, opened with Command-comma) still support the finding.

findings.title: Customize mode doesn't dim the video to flat gray
findings.designEvidence: VIDEO_BREAKDOWN section 15 MUST: 'The video is dimmed to a flat gray.' Spec-part2 section 15 A: the video area turns flat warm gray (#272622). Figma Player - customize.png.
findings.actual: No scrim exists for isCustomizing. PlayerView.swift:46 only changes the frame inset, and MXRAppView.swift:104-112 overlays the palette without dimming. Real screenshot codex-final-native-ui/25-customization-baseline.png shows the test-pattern bars at full brightness above and below the palette. The gallery S66.App only looks dimmed because its fixture image is pre-darkened.
findings.fix: While isCustomizing, overlay a flat scrim over the video canvas only (not the bars) in the Figma gray, about 0.85 opacity, with a 150-200 ms fade.
findings.verifyNote: CONFIRMED. There is no isCustomizing scrim anywhere (grep). PlayerView.swift:46 only changes the frame inset. Real screenshot 25-customization-baseline.png shows the test-pattern bars at full brightness, and because the palette uses MXRBackdropSurface(bgB1Transparent) (MXRCustomizationView.swift:23), the video colors bleed through the whole dialog body as rainbow tints. Figma Player - customize.png shows a flat warm-gray video with a near-black palette. The gallery hides the bug with a pre-darkened fixture.

findings.title: Onboarding's '~/Videos' looks like a chosen value but is only a placeholder: Next adds no media folder (and macOS uses ~/Movies)
findings.designEvidence: Figma Onboarding.png (1899:3055): the input holds '~/Videos' in FG/1 as the value. Video 19m46.7 shows the welcome step's media-folder picker (VIDEO_BREAKDOWN section 15 MUST).
findings.actual: MXROnboardingView.swift:61 uses '~/Videos' as the TextField prompt, styled fg1 so it looks like real text (real screenshot codex-final-native-ui/01-onboarding.png). folderPath stays ''. At :236 MXROnboardingFolder.url('') returns nil, so at :242 nothing reaches app.library.addFolder and the library stays empty after a user who clicked Next believing ~/Videos was chosen. The folder name is the Windows one; on macOS the video folder is ~/Movies.
findings.fix: Pre-fill folderPath with the existing ~/Movies (fall back to ~/Videos only if it exists). Style the placeholder in FG/A4 when the field is empty. Show a validation hint when Next proceeds without a folder.
findings.verifyNote: CONFIRMED. MXROnboardingView.swift:61 styles the prompt '~/Videos' in fg1, so real screenshot 01-onboarding.png reads as an entered value. :236 calls MXROnboardingFolder.url(for: ""), which returns nil (:278), so :242 adds no folder. If the user actually types ~/Videos, which does not exist on macOS, they get the 'Choose an existing media folder' error.

findings.title: .focusable() with the default focus effect draws a system-accent focus ring on Settings sliders, EQ bands and Customize tiles (same root cause as C1)
findings.designEvidence: No Figma component has a focus outline. Owner complaint C1: a purplish square outline around the volume value box.
findings.actual: SettingsControls.swift:301 (SettingsSlider), SettingsEqualizerView.swift:68 (EQ band) and MXRCustomizationView.swift:73 (palette tiles) call .focusable() without .focusEffectDisabled(). Clicking or dragging gives keyboard focus, so macOS draws its focus ring in the user's system accent (purple, per the owner's screenshot). PlayerControls.swift:179 does the same on the volume cone, which is C1.
findings.fix: Add .focusEffectDisabled() at every .focusable() site, and draw a custom accent-tinted focus indicator only when focus came from the keyboard (e.g. via an @FocusState plus a flag for keyboard-initiated focus). Apply the fix in one shared modifier.
findings.verifyNote: PLAUSIBLE (code confirmed, not observed at runtime in this area). .focusable() without .focusEffectDisabled() appears at SettingsControls.swift:301, SettingsEqualizerView.swift:68, MXRCustomizationView.swift:73, PlayerControls.swift:179 (volume, the C1 root-cause candidate) and :413 (seek bar); grep finds no focusEffectDisabled anywhere. On macOS the legacy focusable() takes focus on click and draws the system-accent ring. The visible impact inside Settings and Customize is minor polish; major severity rests on the C1 link.

findings.title: 'Manage Profiles' opens a menu-sized list as a modal sheet with no close button and no Esc
findings.designEvidence: Figma Profiles.png: profiles are a submenu (check, rows, '+ New'), not a modal. Spec-part2 section 15 B.
findings.actual: AppModel.swift:234 maps .manageProfiles (native menu bar Profile > Manage Profiles, MXRNativeMenus.swift:150-153) to interface.present(.profiles). That presents MXRProfilesView as a sheet (MXRAppView.swift:201). MXRProfilesView.swift never calls dismissSheet and has no Done/close button and no onExitCommand. Selecting a profile leaves the sheet up, so the user is trapped until another menu command replaces the sheet.
findings.fix: Remove the sheet path. Show MXRProfilesView as the submenu panel anchored to the Profile row. Do renaming and deletion through its context menu and a small naming alert, which already exists.
findings.verifyNote: CONFIRMED. AppModel.swift:234 handles .manageProfiles with interface.present(.profiles), reached from native Profile > Manage Profiles (MXRNativeMenus.swift:150-153). MXRProfilesView.swift has no dismiss, no close button, no cancelAction and no onExitCommand. Selecting a profile (:60) leaves the sheet up. On macOS a SwiftUI sheet does not close on Esc without a cancelAction, so the user is trapped until another command replaces the sheet.

findings.title: 'Reset all settings', 'Reset all shortcuts' and 'Clear history now' run immediately with no confirmation or undo
findings.designEvidence: macOS HIG: destructive, irreversible actions need confirmation. PHILOSOPHY 2.3 Native first.
findings.actual: AppModel.swift:361-373 (performSettingsAction) resets all settings, resets all shortcuts or clears history the moment the button is clicked. The only feedback is an actionMessage text line at the top of the scroll view (MXRSettingsView.swift:41-44), which may be off-screen.
findings.fix: Show a confirmation alert with a destructive role ('Reset All Settings?' / Reset / Cancel). Show the result as a transient toast near the button.
findings.verifyNote: CONFIRMED. AppModel.swift:361-373 clears history, resets shortcuts and resets all settings with no confirmation. The only feedback is settings.actionMessage at the top of the scroll view (MXRSettingsView.swift:41-44), possibly off-screen. 'reset-shortcuts' (:365) shows no message at all.

findings.title: Editing a hotkey opens a third modal (Cancel/Clear/Assign) instead of capturing in the field; Esc gets recorded instead of cancelling; conflicts are kept
findings.designEvidence: Figma Keyboard Shortcuts.png: each key field has an edit pencil, and editing happens in the cell. macOS convention (System Settings > Keyboard Shortcuts): click the field, it shows 'Type shortcut', press the keys, done; Esc cancels.
findings.actual: MXRKeyboardShortcutsView.swift:86-91 presents ShortcutCaptureSheet. SettingsKeyCaptureResponder.keyDown (:217-219) records any key including Esc. The conflict text says 'Saving keeps both assignments' (:181), which leaves two actions on one key; VLC then fires only one of them. The sheet's bgA3 and unstyled header are a new visual language (see real screenshot 04-nested-shortcut-existing-control.png).
findings.fix: Capture inline: the field turns accent-outlined with 'Press keys...', Esc cancels, Delete clears. On conflict, offer 'Reassign' and clear the other binding.
findings.verifyNote: CONFIRMED. MXRKeyboardShortcutsView.swift:86-91 opens a third modal. SettingsKeyCaptureResponder.keyDown and performKeyEquivalent (:217-224) record any key, including Esc and Command-Q. :181 'Saving keeps both assignments' is visible in real screenshot 04. The capture sheet uses unstyled bgA3 chrome. Note that Figma does not show the editing state (it is OPEN), so the inline-capture fix is a recommendation; the Esc and conflict behavior are clear bugs.

findings.title: Add Subtitles 'To This Folder' requires a media-library folder location, so files opened from Finder fail; the mapping is not kept for future episodes
findings.designEvidence: VIDEO_BREAKDOWN section 06 MUST: scope is this file / this folder / this playlist. 'The mapping persists for that folder or playlist.' Video 05:30-06:30: subtitles are auto-matched and 'saved for all future episodes'.
findings.actual: DialogInput.swift:151-156 (loadTargets) resolves the folder only from file.folder (an ML reference) or the current library location. A file opened from Finder or by drag and drop, outside the library, gets 'Open the selected video's folder before adding subtitles to this folder.' save() (:181-189) attaches per existing ML item only (attachSubtitle). Nothing stores a folder-level rule, so a new episode added later gets nothing.
findings.fix: Derive the folder from the playing file's filesystem URL: enumerate the directory's video files and match them. Persist a folder/playlist rule (subtitle directory plus match pattern) that the playback hook (AppModel play/preset path) applies to new items.
findings.verifyNote: CONFIRMED. DialogInput.swift:150-152 derives the folder only from file.folder (an ML reference) or the library location, so a Finder-opened file gets the :182 error. save() (:191-199) calls attachSubtitle, which the bridge implements as VLC_ML_MEDIA_ADD_EXTERNAL_MRL on an existing ML media (MXRLibraryServices.m:319, EINVAL for non-ML ids). No folder or playlist rule persists for future episodes, contrary to VIDEO_BREAKDOWN §06 MUST.

findings.title: Open Disc/Capture use gray system controls and jargon; Convert is MP4-only and Stream HTTP-only
findings.designEvidence: PHILOSOPHY section 4: when the design is silent, reuse the closest Figma component and never invent a new visual language; principle 10 (expose conversion and streaming cleanly); principle 9 (human words). VIDEO_BREAKDOWN section 10 OPEN: reuse the Open Network Stream chrome.
findings.actual: OpenMediaDialogs.swift:19-20 uses Picker(.segmented), a system gray segmented control (see r_S37_Disc_empty.png: light-gray 'DVD' segment), where Figma's Theme segmented control exists. :51-54 uses Picker(.menu), a system popup button with a stepper glyph. Copy: 'enter its AVFoundation unique ID', 'streamed in MPEG-TS'. Convert offers no profile choice (fixed 'h264' MP4, :179). Stream supports only 'http://127.0.0.1:8080/live' with 'copy'.
findings.fix: Reuse the Settings segmented control and the Figma dropdown. Drop the unique-ID field (list cameras by name). Add a profile dropdown in human words: Video MP4 (H.264), Video WebM, Audio MP3, Audio FLAC... For Stream, add destination types (HTTP / UDP / Chromecast through the renderer).
findings.verifyNote: CONFIRMED. My render S37_Disc_empty.png shows the system light-gray segmented control (OpenMediaDialogs.swift:19-20) clashing with the dark chrome. :49 hint says 'enter its AVFoundation unique ID'. :130 says 'streamed in MPEG-TS'. :179 hard-codes profile 'h264'/'copy'. The design is silent here, so the issue is PHILOSOPHY §4 reuse. Borderline major/minor, kept major because it is the most visibly 'non-design' surface.

findings.title: Recording category has no 'Advanced Options' bar
findings.designEvidence: Figma Settings - recording.png (6571:16429) ends with 'Advanced Options >'. VIDEO_BREAKDOWN section 14 MUST: 'The page ends with an Advanced Options bar.'
findings.actual: settings-map.json5's recording category has no advanced section, so MXRSettingsView.swift:48 never draws the bar (see S48_Settings_recording/side-by-side.png). Real advanced options exist: sout-mux-caching, input-record-native, sout-keep and others.
findings.fix: Add an Advanced section (stream output caching, keep stream output open, record timestamp prefix, cast conversion quality, ...) so the bar renders.
findings.verifyNote: CONFIRMED in my S48.Settings/recording side-by-side: Figma ends with 'Advanced Options >' and the render has no bar. Downgraded to minor because one missing bar on one page is unlikely to be noticed without comparing to Figma. Separately, info-icon placement differs on this page too (the app has one on 'Discover cast devices'; Figma has them on Cast quality and Tuning).

findings.title: Info-icon placement doesn't follow Figma: missing on many Figma rows, added where Figma has none
findings.designEvidence: Figma Settings - video.png has info icons on Start videos in fullscreen, Stop the screensaver, Play video as desktop wallpaper, Method and Aspect ratio. Settings - playback.png: Start playing as soon as a file opens, Default subtitle track, When playback finishes. Settings - audio.png: Speaker setup, Target level, Replay gain preamp. Settings - privacy.png: all Last.fm rows. Settings - global.png: no info icon on Interface language, Theme or Accent color. Principle 9: an info icon on every setting.
findings.actual: The icon appears only when catalog info or engine longtext exists (MXRSettingsView.swift:303, :325). Only 86 of 220 catalog rows have info. In the real app, Theme and Accent gain icons from the label-equal longtext (18-settings-system-intermediate.png).
findings.fix: Give every catalog row an info string (required by lint), using the Figma rows as the minimum. Drop the info icon on Theme and Accent.
findings.verifyNote: CONFIRMED. 86 of 220 catalog rows have info (grep). The S48 general side-by-side shows an info icon on Interface language that Figma lacks. Real screenshot 18 adds icons on Theme and Accent from the label-equal longtext.

findings.title: Settings search keeps the previous category highlighted and mixes advanced rows in without saying so
findings.designEvidence: Spec-part2 section 14 OPEN (search behavior). Figma setting category.png: the highlighted row means the current page.
findings.actual: MXRSettingsView.swift:113 keeps selected = selectedCategoryID during search, so the real screenshot 38-history-pref-baseline.png shows 'Interface' highlighted while showing Privacy results. searchResults (SettingsModel.swift:60-71) flattens all sections, including advanced ones and rows hidden by visibleWhen, before filtering.
findings.fix: Clear the sidebar highlight, or highlight the categories that have matches, while a query is active. Tag advanced matches with a small 'Advanced' label.

findings.title: Esc and Return don't work in Settings, Keyboard Shortcuts or Onboarding
findings.designEvidence: The Keyboard Shortcuts list itself names 'Exit fullscreen / close dialog (esc)'. macOS convention: Esc cancels a sheet and Return triggers the default button.
findings.actual: DialogShell and AddSubtitles have .onExitCommand and cancelAction/defaultAction (DialogSupport.swift:110,119,149). MXRSettingsView, MXRKeyboardShortcutsView (Cancel/Save are SettingsButtons with no keyboardShortcut, :69-75), MXROnboardingView and MXRProfilesView have none. SwiftUI sheets on macOS don't dismiss on Esc unless a cancelAction exists.
findings.fix: Add .keyboardShortcut(.cancelAction) to Cancel/close and .keyboardShortcut(.defaultAction) to Save/Next/Finish, plus onExitCommand where there is no Cancel button.
findings.verifyNote: CONFIRMED. grep finds cancelAction/defaultAction/onExitCommand only in DialogSupport, AddSubtitles, Customization, TrackPopover and Library. Settings, Keyboard Shortcuts (Cancel/Save at :69-75 are plain SettingsButtons), Onboarding and Profiles have none.

findings.title: Windows vocabulary and typos in Settings copy

findings.title: Customize edit mode outlines the non-movable cone and dims the sidebar icon; edit-mode controls stay clickable

findings.title: Custom drag UTType for the layout editor is exported in code but not declared in Info.plist (plausible failure point)
findings.designEvidence: VIDEO_BREAKDOWN section 15 MUST: drag tiles into and out of the bars. Apple: UTType(exportedAs:) must be declared in UTExportedTypeDeclarations.

findings.title: Settings slider ticks fixed at 9; search placeholder too bright; EQ and Picture semantics loose
findings.designEvidence: Figma Settings - interface.png 'Hide after' has a dense tick scale (about 20 ticks). Settings - playback.png speed slider has ticks aligned to its 8 labels. The search placeholder uses FG/A4 #404040.

The Picture sliders set hue and brightness on the vout without enabling the 'adjust' filter (plausibly no visible effect).

The search placeholder renders brighter than Figma's FG/A4 in every side-by-side. The max(1, span) bug (:266) is real but theoretical, since no catalog slider has a span under 1. The EQ and Picture semantics (preset not moving the bands; hue/brightness options set without enabling the 'adjust' filter, which MXREffectsServices.m:153 gates) are plausible and need a runtime check.

findings.title: Onboarding is laid out with absolute offsets on a fixed 1090x759 canvas, then scaled

findings.title: Global Hotkey column is fully editable but does nothing on macOS
findings.designEvidence: Figma Keyboard Shortcuts.png (2437:14832) shows a Global Hotkey column. PHILOSOPHY principle: unsupported operations must show availability, not pretend success (CODEX_STATUS makes the same claim).
findings.actual: VLC ships global hotkeys only for xcb and win32 (modules/control/Makefile.am:52,61; modules/control/globalhotkeys/ has only xcb.c and win32.c). The bridge reports @"globalHotkeys":@NO (MXRServicesBridge.m:408), and VLCServiceTransport.swift:45 maps it to supportsGlobalHotkeys. MXRKeyboardShortcutsView.swift:118 still renders an editable field for every action, opens the capture sheet, runs conflict checks against global bindings and writes global-key-* options that nothing on macOS reads. Users can assign 'global' keys that never fire.
findings.fix: Read app.capabilities.supportsGlobalHotkeys. When it is false, either drop the column (record a DECISIONS entry) or render the fields disabled with a one-line 'Global hotkeys aren't available on macOS' note in the header. Exclude global bindings from conflict checks when unsupported. A real implementation would need a CGEventTap/NSEvent global monitor plus the Accessibility permission flow.

findings.title: Customize palette is clipped to less than 2 rows with half-cut labels and no scroll affordance at normal window sizes

findings.title: Headline Settings rows are dead controls: 'Output device' has one choice, 'Show confirmation and error dialogs' is ignored, 'Default optical drive' shows '-'

findings.title: Scroll indicators are hidden on every long dialog list (Settings pages and sidebar, the 100+ row Shortcuts list, the Customize palette)

grades.justification: Completeness 72: every element in the design exists in some form. But subtitle-timeline range labels are missing from the real bar, the paired action + 'Pressed X' OSD only works with the mock backend, the hover-only time chip is missing, and the toast's hover-pause and fade are missing. Fidelity 55: static gallery renders of the default bar are almost pixel-identical to Figma (play 54x28, time 76x28, seek 1238x28 with 8x24 capsule, cone vectors and gradient). In the real app the look breaks: a waveform appears on video by default, the system focus ring shows on the cone and seek bar, there are two OSDs in two corners, the track popover is vertically centred, and the toast time uses the wrong font. Code quality 48: PlaybackClock and the icon system are well done. But every UI command and VLC callback triggers one or more full player-state snapshots on the main thread; seeks and thumbnail requests are neither throttled nor cancellable; seek state is private to the bar; two player bridges duplicate each other; and the mock backend behaves differently from the real one, so the gallery hides real bugs.

doneWell: Static fidelity of the default bar is excellent; do not regress it. S01.ControlBar/default matches Figma 491:1779 except where the handle sits for the mock time. Matching parts: play 54x28 radius 6 (Accent when paused, FG/A3 with dark glyph when playing; C.PlayButton/play and /pause PASS), prev/next 30x28 cells, time labels 76x28 Inter 15 FG/A2 (C.CurrentTime and C.Duration PASS, including the '-00:23:30' remaining state), seek track 1238x28 radius 6 BG/B2 with a 2 pt inset 24 pt BG/Accent Bright fill and an 8x24 Accent capsule, and the right cluster's icons and spacing.

The volume cone traces Figma's vector paths (VolumeConeTrackShape and VolumeConeFillShape) with an sRGB gradient and overlay. Its non-linear fill mapping (100% = 63 pt of 88; table from Figma volume steps 244:184) is used both for drawing and for pointer-to-level conversion. All 13 cone steps match within 2/255. Keep the paths and PlayerGeometry.volumeFillWidth/volumePercent.

The tooltip chip (121x37, '100 %', bgB1Transparent, outside-only shadow per showShadowBehindNode=false) matches 2245:9805. Keep its geometry and shadow approach; only the focus ring and backdrop need changes.

Right-hand icons follow the state language: audio, subtitles (filled orange), gear (filled orange) and queue (lists, orange) go active while their panel is open; hover uses the Figma 177:97 hover fill (#FFFFFF at 6%) and FG/1.

PlaybackClock is a sound design: timer-point interpolation with vlc_player_timer_point_Interpolate semantics, a second-boundary tick task so labels change once per second, and a CADisplayLink (NSView.displayLink) that runs only while playing with bars visible. The paused-clock freeze in applyClockPausedAtHostTime is correct. Keep this; fix only seeking-state handling and per-frame invalidation scope.

Editable elapsed time with tolerant parsing (PlayerGeometry.typedTime, remaining-relative input, invalid state shown in accent) and the remaining-time toggle implement the Figma-only Current Time and Duration states.

The seek preview card matches thumbnail 2151:9673 (C.SeekPreview REVIEW is antialiasing only). The model's idea of quantized slots that keep the previous frame visible is right; only scheduling and cancellation need rework.
The music bar variant S34.ControlBar/music matches Figma 4778:26181 (±15 s, waveform pitch 5, 2 pt bars, 4x24 thumb, played part in accent).

Continue-watching toast geometry and colors follow the hidden Figma layer 1919:9580 (552x52, radius 16, FG/2 16 pt text, 146x32 Accent button with dark 600 label) and it sits centred above the bar, as the video intends.
Accessibility is thoughtful: adjustable actions on the seek bar and cone, labels and values, and named actions to edit or toggle time.
The D020 paused-seek engine work is narrow and evidence-backed: paused seeks display the target frame.

findings.title: Scrubbing: the thumbnail preview stops updating while the pointer moves; requests are cancelled before they are sent, are not cancellable once sent, and are slow and uncached
findings.designEvidence: VIDEO_BREAKDOWN §02 MUST: hovering anywhere on the seek bar shows a preview card (frame thumbnail plus timestamp), and while dragging the elapsed label follows. Key frame 02-control-bar__seek-thumbnail-preview__03m29.3s: thumbnail and 00:02:10 match the elapsed label during the seek. Transcript 3:00-3:30 ('VLC doesn't show a thumbnail as you seek through the video') and 20:00 ('Seek through the video with ease'). Figma thumbnail 2151:9673 (272x189, image 252x142).
findings.actual: SeekPreviewModel.hover (Sources/MXRCore/Models/AppearanceAndPreviewModels.swift:88-112) quantizes time into slots of max(2 s, length/300), about 4 pt on a 1238 pt bar. Every new slot cancels the pending task (line 99) before its 80 ms debounce (line 70, sleep at line 106) ends, so during a continuous drag no request is ever sent. The card keeps the old image while its time text changes. When a request is sent, Swift cancellation does not reach VLC: VLCThumbnailBackend.requestImage (Sources/MXRVLCBackend/VLCServiceBackends.swift:140-150) awaits a continuation with no cancel path, and MXRThumbnailServices (module/bridge/MXRThumbnailServices.m:52-77) never calls vlc_preparser_Cancel for one request. Stale requests therefore queue on a single thumbnailer thread (max_thumbnailer_threads=1, line 35). Each request creates a new input, decodes in software (hw_dec=false, line 67), encodes a PNG into NSTemporaryDirectory (line 66), reads it back and deletes it. Nothing is cached, so hovering the same point again regenerates the image. Net effect: the preview updates only when the pointer pauses, seconds late, and often shows a frame that does not match the time below it.
findings.fix: Replace the cancel-debounce with throttling where the latest target wins. Send immediately when nothing is in flight; while a request is in flight, keep only the newest slot and cancel the superseded VLC request with vlc_preparser_Cancel(req) (keep the req pointer per request id and add a 'cancel' request to the bridge). Add an LRU cache keyed by (media id, slot). After media open, prefetch a low-resolution strip in the background (about 120-200 frames at 160 px, sequential fast seeks on one long-lived thumbnailer input) so scrubbing reads from memory, and refine with a full-size frame when the pointer rests. Allow hardware decoding and avoid the temp-file PNG round trip. Show the time of the frame actually displayed, or dim a stale frame.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed in code. In SeekPreviewModel.hover (AppearanceAndPreviewModels.swift:88-112), the slot is max(2 s, length/300), so for media longer than 10 min a 1238 pt bar has 300 slots of about 4 pt each. Each slot change cancels the 80 ms debounced task, so a moving pointer never sends a request. The old image stays up while the time text changes, so the card shows a frame that does not match its timestamp. That is wrong information on the redesign's headline feature (transcript 3:00), so critical stands. Cancellation never reaches VLC: LiveVLCServiceTransport.request (VLCBackends.swift:52-63) is a plain continuation with no cancel handler, and MXRThumbnailServices.m keeps no req handle, so vlc_preparser_Cancel(req) is never called. There is one thumbnailer thread (line 35), with hw_dec=false, a PNG temp-file round trip, and no cache: end() sets image=nil, so every new hover starts from the placeholder. One addition: requests use VLC_THUMBNAILER_SEEK_FAST (line 67), so even a fresh thumbnail is the nearest keyframe and can be seconds away from the label. The fix should request precise frames on rest, or label the frame's real time. Static fidelity of the card is very good (C.SeekPreview check: REVIEW, near-identical). Keep it.

findings.title: Each seek or volume drag event runs two or more full player-state snapshots on the main thread (all tracks, titles, effects variables, audio devices), and VLC callbacks add more
findings.designEvidence: PHILOSOPHY §2.4: as fast as stock VLC, overlay animations at display refresh rate, idle player under 1% CPU. VIDEO_BREAKDOWN §02 MUST: the elapsed label follows the drag; click or drag inside the cone sets the level. Transcript 20:00: 'Seek through the video with ease'.
findings.actual: MXRSeekBar DragGesture.onChanged (Sources/MXRUI/Player/PlayerControls.swift:363-364) calls PlayerModel.seek on every mouse event (60-120 Hz) with no throttle. The call chain: VLCPlayerBackend.send (Sources/MXRVLCBackend/VLCPlayerBackend.swift:139-148), then transport.perform, then MXRServicesBridge playerCommand, which ends with a synchronous [self changed:@"player"] (module/bridge/MXRServicesBridge.m:686). That synchronously runs VLCPlayerBackend.reload (line 149), a full playerSnapshot (MXRServicesBridge.m:439-497). The snapshot takes the player lock; enumerates audio, video and subtitle tracks, titles, chapters and programs; reads statistics and teletext; reads about 60 vout/aout variables in the _effects snapshot (line 483); and enumerates CoreAudio devices with aout_DevicesList (line 489). send() then calls reload() a second time (VLCPlayerBackend.swift:144). Each seek also fires on_buffering_changed, on_capabilities_changed and others, each a dispatchChange(@"player") (lines 164-212) and another full snapshot on main. on_statistics_changed adds one per second during playback. Volume drags follow the same path (MXRServicesBridge.m:601-607) plus the aout on_volume_changed callback (lines 242-245). The main thread is saturated during a drag, so gestures and redraws batch up: the timeline and video seem to update every few seconds. VLC's input already merges seeks (src/input/input.c:1505-1515, 125 ms postpone at lines 735-748), so the flood gains nothing.
findings.fix: (1) Make commands fire-and-forget: no snapshot in send() and no synchronous changed: after a command; let the engine callbacks report the change. (2) Split the 'player' service into topics (state/caps, tracks, titles, effects, devices, statistics, volume). Each callback already knows its topic, so re-read only that one; enumerate devices only on on_device_changed or an explicit refresh. (3) Coalesce dispatchChange on main with one pending flag per topic. (4) In the UI, send at most one seek per display frame (CADisplayLink, latest target wins) and volume at about 30 Hz. (5) Stop decoding effects and style dictionaries through JSON on every property access (VLCPlayerBackend.swift:51-52, 64-65).
findings.verifyNote: Code path confirmed. VLCPlayerBackend.send → transport.perform → playerCommand ends with a synchronous [self changed:@"player"] (MXRServicesBridge.m:686). That goes sink → EventChannel.send (synchronous) → VLCPlayerBackend.reload → a full playerSnapshot (no caching in snapshot(for:)). Then send() calls reload() again (VLCPlayerBackend.swift:144). That is two full snapshots per mouse event at 60-120 Hz, plus one per dispatchChange from engine callbacks, and setVolume follows the same path. One correction: aout_DevicesList copies aout's cached device list under a mutex (src/audio_output/output.c:902-932); it does not enumerate CoreAudio. The cost is player-lock contention with the input thread, about 60 var reads in [_effects snapshot], track and title enumeration, and SwiftUI invalidation fan-out. The DragGesture also sends a seek on every event with no throttle. VLC merges SET_POSITION controls (input.c:1505-1515), but every accepted seek still flushes the decoders. Stock VLC throttles slider seeks; this UI does not. Together these explain C6. Marked PLAUSIBLE as the dominant cause: not profiled, but the fix (latest-wins throttle per display frame, no synchronous snapshot after a command, per-topic snapshots) is right either way.

findings.title: Elapsed label does not follow the drag, flickers between old and new times, and the playhead snaps back after release (stale timer points during a seek are not discarded)
findings.designEvidence: VIDEO_BREAKDOWN §02 MUST: 'While dragging, the elapsed label follows.' Key frame 03m29.3s: elapsed 00:02:10 equals the preview time. include/vlc_player.h:3512-3524 says on_update() can be called while seeking and the user should discard those points.
findings.actual: cb_timer_seek (module/bridge/MXRPlayerBridge.m:193-198) ignores on_seek(NULL). Every on_update (lines 185-191) is applied even while a seek is pending, so the clock alternates between the requested target (hostTime 0) and pre-seek running points. VLCClockBackend (Sources/MXRVLCBackend/VLCBackends.swift:91-96) has no seeking state. MXRTimeLabel reads only app.clock.displayTime (Sources/MXRUI/Player/PlayerControls.swift:83-87); the drag target is private @State inside MXRSeekBar (line 315), so the label cannot show it. In onEnded (lines 365-371) dragPosition is cleared at once, and the display link (lines 387-391) repaints from the stale running point: the handle jumps back to the old position, then forward when the seek lands.
findings.fix: In the bridge, set a seeking flag on on_seek(value) and clear it on on_seek(NULL); drop on_update points while it is set. Move the scrub state into the model (for example PlaybackClock.scrubTime or PlayerModel.pendingSeek). The seek bar sets it during drag and keeps it until the first post-seek point arrives. The current-time label shows scrubTime ?? displayTime, and the playhead uses it until the clock confirms.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed, with one nuance. The elapsed label does track the drag indirectly: each vlc_player_SeekByPos calls vlc_player_UpdateTimerSeekState (src/player/timer.c:320-364), which sends on_seek(point) with ts set to the target and system_date VLC_TICK_MAX. The bridge forwards it as a timer point with hostTime 0 (MXRPlayerBridge.m:48-54, 193-198). Stale pre-seek on_update points are still delivered while seeking (timer.c:429-437, and the vlc_player.h:3518-3521 note), and the bridge applies them. So the label and isRunning flip between the target (not running) and the old running point, and the display link starts and stops on every flip. After onEnded clears dragPosition, a stale running point can snap the handle back. MXRTimeLabel reads only clock.displayTime and has no access to the private drag @State. The fix (bridge seeking flag, model-level scrubTime) is correct.

findings.title: Waveform is on by default and drawn on the seek bar of normal videos (the dense tick marks in the owner's screenshot) instead of the solid thick bar
findings.designEvidence: Figma default bar 491:1779 and Player-6.png: solid 28 pt BG/B2 track, BG/Accent Bright fill, 8x24 Accent capsule. The waveform appears only in Controls variants 'waveform' 2139:8124 and 'music' 4778:26181. The final Figma Playback tab (Controls 5187:24308) has no waveform toggle. Video 09:17.5: 'Show Waveform on Seekbar' is OFF. Transcript 12:00: 'you have the waveform seekbar if you want' (music, optional). VIDEO_BREAKDOWN §09 MUST: draw the waveform only 'when Show Waveform on Seekbar is on'.
findings.actual: InterfaceModel.swift:161 sets showWaveform = true. MXRSeekBar requests a waveform for every media item (Sources/MXRUI/Player/PlayerControls.swift:420-426) and draws it whenever samples exist (lines 326 and 335), switching to the 4 pt music thumb (line 327). The bridge accepts any local file URL (module/bridge/MXRAudioServices.m:348-366), and readWaveform (line 264+) decodes the whole audio track of MP4/MOV videos with AVAssetReader. Result: tick marks on video, plus a full-length audio decode (tens of CPU-seconds for a feature film) at every open, competing with playback. The gallery shows the same bug: S13.Player/osd and S05.Player/fullscreen draw a waveform on The_Wand_S01E04.mp4.
findings.fix: Default showWaveform to false and persist the setting. Draw the waveform only for the music layout (app.player.isAudioOnly), or for video only after explicit opt-in. Request a waveform only when it will be drawn, and send cancelWaveform when the media changes or the task is cancelled. Keep the 8x24 capsule for video.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed. InterfaceModel.swift:161 sets showWaveform = true. The bridge advertises supportsWaveform=YES (MXRAudioServices.m:135) and accepts any file URL (lines 348-366). MXRSeekBar draws WaveformShape whenever samples exist, and renders S13/S05/S12 show tick marks on The_Wand_S01E04.mp4. The video at 09:17.5 shows 'Show Waveform on Seekbar' OFF, and 12:56.6 shows it on music only. Two corrections or additions. (1) Decoded waveforms are cached in memory per URL, mtime and bins (_waveCache), so the full AVAssetReader decode runs on the first open per session, not on every open. Swift task cancellation does not send cancelWaveform, so a decode keeps running after the view goes away. (2) showWaveform is a plain stored var with no persistence, so a user who switches it off gets tick marks back on the next launch. Keep: the solid-bar geometry matches Figma 491:1779 almost pixel for pixel (S01.ControlBar/default check), and the music bar (S34.ControlBar/music, mean Δ 1.7/255) is excellent. Don't break either.

findings.title: Clicking or dragging the volume cone (and the seek bar) gives it keyboard focus, and macOS draws its system-colored focus ring
findings.designEvidence: Figma 'audio value' 2245:9805: fill #0E0E0E at 95%, radius 6, background blur 50, drop shadow, no strokes. Volume set 244:184 has no outline. No design surface has a system focus ring, and VIDEO_BREAKDOWN principle 11 reserves accent outlines and colors for active state only.
findings.actual: MXRVolumeCone has .focusable() (Sources/MXRUI/Player/PlayerControls.swift:179), as does MXRSeekBar (line 413); .focusEffectDisabled() appears nowhere in Sources. On macOS a .focusable() view with key handlers takes focus on click, and AppKit draws the keyboard-focus ring in the system accent (purple or blue, not the app's orange). It appears exactly when the user drags the cone and the '78 %' chip is visible (overlay at lines 172-178), and it stays until focus moves. The focusability is redundant: arrow and volume keys are already handled by the window key monitor (Sources/MXRPlugin/MXRAppController.swift:102-114) before SwiftUI sees them. A secondary risk on macOS 26+: the 121x37 chip sits on a live NSVisualEffectView .hudWindow backdrop (PlayerControls.swift:261; Sources/MXRDesign/Materials/MXRBackdropSurface.swift), whose AppKit material is not guaranteed to respect SwiftUI's rounded clip.
findings.fix: Add .focusEffectDisabled() to the cone and the seek bar, or remove .focusable() and keep the accessibilityAdjustableAction. If keyboard focus is wanted, use .focusable(interactions: .edit) with @FocusState and draw a token-colored ring only for keyboard focus. Render the tooltip with a plain bgB1Transparent fill and the outside shadow; blur is invisible at this size. Verify in the real app with a bright or colorful video.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed by experiment, not just plausible. A scratch SwiftUI app (scratchpad/shadowtest/focus.swift) reproduces the cone: frame 88x28, .contentShape(.rect), DragGesture(minimumDistance:0), .focusable(), .onKeyPress.
