One synthesized click makes it first responder (SwiftUI.KeyViewProxy). AppKit then draws the system-accent focus ring, purple on this Mac, as a rounded square around the 88x28 cone (focus.png). Adding .focusEffectDisabled() removes it (focus_disabled.png). This is C1. The ring surrounds the cone, not the '78 %' chip, and it stays after the drag until focus moves. MXRSeekBar (.focusable() at line 413) gets the same ring after any click. The onKeyPress handlers are dead code: the window key monitor handles arrows first, and MXRKeyRouting.shouldHandle only yields to NSTextView or NSControl, not KeyViewProxy. The NSVisualEffectView-corner theory is secondary and unproven. Fix: .focusEffectDisabled(), or drop .focusable() and keep accessibilityAdjustableAction.

findings.title: Two OSD systems: VLC's vout OSD (top right, e.g. 'Volume: 48%') and the app's SwiftUI OSD (top left, only 'Pressed X') are never paired or deduplicated
findings.designEvidence: VIDEO_BREAKDOWN §13 MUST: OSD feedback for shortcuts shows two lines, the action ('Crop: 2.35:1') then 'Pressed C'. Frames 15:25 and 15:27.1: one VLC-style white OSD block at the top right of the video (the window frame is visible on the right), two left-aligned lines, the second slightly smaller. Design principle 6: one place per function, no duplicates. spec-part2 §13B: controlled by 'Show feedback for shortcuts' and the duration slider.
findings.actual: The engine OSD is never suppressed. Every volume change calls vlc_player_osd_Volume (src/player/aout.c:94 and 103), which draws 'Volume: %ld%%' at the top right and, in fullscreen, also a vertical slider (src/player/osd.c:167-169); the hotkeys module draws the action text in the vout. The SwiftUI MXRPlayerOSD sits at the top left (Sources/MXRUI/Player/PlayerView.swift:91-95, 208-223). In the real app it only ever shows 'Pressed X': VLCOSDBackend listens for an 'osd' service (Sources/MXRVLCBackend/VLCServiceBackends.swift:232) that nothing in module/ emits. For volume keys, MXRAppController.swift:109-112 shows 'Pressed Up' (SwiftUI, top left) while VLC shows 'Volume: 48%' (top right). The two differ in font, corner, timing (osd-duration vs VLC's fixed 1 s) and refresh path (the main-thread snapshot vs the vout thread), which is the desync the owner sees. The cone tooltip is a third volume indicator. VLCOSDBackend.showMessage (line 233) sends each message to both the engine and SwiftUI. The mock backend pairs action and key (Sources/MXRMockBackend/MockServices.swift:188-251), so gallery S13 looks right while the app does not. The OSD typography is welcomeTitle and bodyLarge (2:1) instead of VLC's OSD look (about 1:0.85).
findings.fix: Use one OSD renderer. At interface start, turn off the engine OSD for this player only: var_Create(player, "osd", VLC_VAR_BOOL) plus var_SetBool false (vouts inherit through the dummy vout and player, so the engine is not modified). The bridge then emits an 'osd' event carrying the action text after 'trigger' (the key-action variable callback is synchronous, so the new state is readable) and for volume, rate, delay and track changes that come from keys, scroll or media keys. Render one two-line block at the top right of the video area in VLC-OSD style (white, soft shadow, size relative to video height, second line about 85%), honoring 'Show feedback for' for every message. Show no OSD for volume changes made on the cone itself, where the tooltip is the indicator. Remove the double send in VLCOSDBackend.showMessage.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed. Each volume change runs vlc_player_osd_Volume from the aout var callback (src/player/aout.c:88-104). It draws 'Volume: N%' at the top right, and in fullscreen also a vertical slider (osd.c:156-173). That includes every cone drag event, so there are three volume indicators at once. Nothing in module/ creates or clears the 'osd' variable, and nothing emits the 'osd' service that VLCOSDBackend listens for. In the real app, MXRPlayerOSD therefore only shows 'Pressed X' (top left), while VLC shows the action text (top right). VLCOSDBackend.showMessage sends to both. One caveat on design evidence: spec-part2 §13B says the two lines sit at the top left, while the zoomed video frames (15:25-15:27) suggest the right side of the video. Placement needs a decision, but the duplication bug is the same either way. The existing 'Show feedback for shortcuts' toggle writes VLC's global 'osd' option, which kills both systems at once, more evidence that one renderer is needed. The see-also missed finding CB-M1 covers the same root cause for seek, play and rate.

findings.title: Track popover opened from the audio or subtitle button is vertically centred in the video instead of anchored just above the bar at the bottom right
findings.designEvidence: VIDEO_BREAKDOWN §04 MUST: each button opens a floating track popover anchored at the bottom right above the bar. spec-part1 Appendix A and §0.4: floating panels sit about 10-12 px from the right edge and 12-22 px above the control bar. Tokens: sidePanels.placementGapAboveControlBar = 20, placementRightInset = 20. Native key frame 04-track-popover__subtitles-tab-external-tracks-native__06m21.7s: popover bottom about 22 px above the bar.
findings.actual: MXRAppView puts the popover in .overlay(alignment: .trailing) (Sources/MXRUI/MXRAppView.swift:52-58 and 84-90). That alignment centres the 524 pt card vertically, so it floats mid-right: in the render its bottom is about 230 pt above the bar.
findings.fix: Use .overlay(alignment: .bottomTrailing) with .padding(.bottom, Theme.Metric.SidePanels.placementGapAboveControlBar) and .padding(.trailing, placementRightInset), and cap the height so it never goes under the top bar.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed. MXRAppView.swift:52-58 and 84-90 use .overlay(alignment: .trailing), which centres the 524 pt card vertically. The S14 render shows it floating mid-right. The native key frames 06:21.7 (subtitles) and 04:54.8 (video tab) show the popover anchored at the bottom right, about 20 px above the bar and about 12-20 px from the right edge. The fix (.bottomTrailing plus the placementGapAboveControlBar and placementRightInset tokens) is correct. This answers C2's placement question.

findings.title: Bottom-right popovers and panels appear by swapping the whole view tree, with no transition, no reliable Esc and no click-outside dismissal; the top '⋯' menu is an NSPopover that animates
findings.designEvidence: VIDEO_BREAKDOWN §04 SHOULD: clicking outside or pressing Esc closes the popover; a short fade or slide is fine. §03 and spec §03: about 120-150 ms reveal timing. Principle 2: panels appear on request and go away cleanly. MUST: the bar icon is orange while its popover is open (toggle).
findings.actual: InterfaceModel.toggle sets rightPanel without animation. MXRAppView then switches from the MXRPlayerView root branch (Sources/MXRUI/MXRAppView.swift:39-41) to a different VStack/HStack branch (lines 42-98). This hard cut recreates the control bar (MXRSeekBar @State, display link, waveform task, hover state) and re-hosts the video view. The '⋯' menu uses .popover (Sources/MXRUI/Player/PlayerBars.swift:212-213), which animates, hence the inconsistency. Esc is handled only through .onExitCommand inside TrackPopover (Sources/MXRUI/Panels/TrackPopover.swift:19), which needs focus inside the popover; after a mouse click it has none. There is no click-on-video dismissal; the only way to close is to click the same icon again.
findings.fix: Keep one persistent MXRPlayerView and control bar and lay panels over it in a stable overlay layer, instead of branching the root. Insert and remove panels with .transition(.opacity.combined(with: .offset(y: 8))) inside withAnimation(.easeOut(duration: MXRPlayerMetrics.revealDuration)), fading only under Reduce Motion, and use the same motion for the '⋯' menu. Add window-level Esc (in the key monitor, before VLC's leave-fullscreen) and a click on the video to close the open panel.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed, and the Esc cause is different from what the finding says. Opening a track popover with the library hidden switches MXRAppView from the MXRPlayerView root (lines 39-41) to the VStack/HStack branch (64-102). That is a hard cut that rebuilds the bar (@State, display link, waveform task) and re-hosts the video NSView. The '⋯' menu is an animated NSPopover (PlayerBars.swift:212-213), hence C4's inconsistency. Esc: the window key monitor (MXRAppController.swift:102-114) runs before SwiftUI. VLC binds Esc to key-leave-fullscreen by default (libvlc-module.c:2318/2590), so ShortcutsModel.handle consumes Esc, shows 'Pressed Esc' and runs leave-fullscreen. .onExitCommand (TrackPopover.swift:19) never fires, whatever has focus. The key monitor must close an open panel on Esc before shortcut dispatch. For a 'click on video dismisses' fix: MXRVideoHostView already turns a single click into play/pause after the double-click interval (MXRAppController.swift:205-211). The dismissing click must be consumed, or it will also pause the video.

findings.title: Subtitle-timeline mode in the real bar keeps the normal elapsed and duration labels instead of the '00:06:00*' / '00:07:00*' window bounds; cue blocks are rounded
findings.designEvidence: spec-part1 §07 (subtitle timeline): time labels become range bounds with an asterisk, '00:06:00*' … '00:07:00*'. Native key frame 07-sidebar__subtitle-timeline-native__07m04.2s. Figma Controls sub-timeline variant 3744:12361 (labels 00:01:50* and 00:02:40*, square cue blocks 3744:12372). Video: square-cornered cue blocks.
findings.actual: PlayerBars.swift:223-225 creates MXRSubtitleTimelineView(showsRangeLabels: false), while the separate .currentTime and .duration items keep showing playback time. Only the isolated S21.Timeline gallery entry shows the asterisk labels, so the gallery looks right and the bar does not. Cue blocks use RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: Theme.Radius.md) (Sources/MXRUI/Panels/SubtitleTimeline.swift:77) while Figma's are square. The nudge and arrow glyphs are visibly thinner than Figma's (cmp_L.png and cmp_R.png). TimelineView(.animation) rebuilds every cue segment each frame (line 48).
findings.fix: When showSubtitleTimeline is active, have MXRTimeLabel(.current/.duration) show the window start and end with '*' (expose the viewport from a model, not view @State), or hide those items and turn on showsRangeLabels. Make cue blocks square (radius 0) and use the Figma glyph weight. Drive only the playhead per frame.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed. The Figma sub-timeline variant 3744:12361 reuses the normal Current Time and Duration instances (3744:12370 and 3744:12376) with the texts '00:01:50*' and '00:02:40*'. spec-part1:432 says the labels 'become range bounds with an asterisk'. PlayerBars.swift:223-225 passes showsRangeLabels:false while .currentTime and .duration keep showing playback time beside a 50 s window, which is misleading. The real bridge enables this mode (MXRSubtitleCueServices supportsSubtitleTimeline). Correction on cues: Figma cue blocks (3749:12473…) have radius 1 and fill white at 14%, drawn over the played fill so played cues read orange-brown. The app uses Theme.Radius.md, so 'square' should be 'radius 1'. TimelineView(.animation) rebuilding all segments every frame is real but minor.

findings.title: Continue-watching toast first shows '-00:00:00' (permanently when the media library has no record); the bold time falls back to a smaller system font; the resume hint looks like already-played progress
findings.designEvidence: spec-part2 §12: toast text plus bold time, Continue Watching (Accent, dark label 600), ✕ button; the seek bar shows a faint dark-orange span (#150900) and a faint marker (#322212). Figma hidden layer 1919:9580 (552x52, radius 16, #191919 at 95%): text 1922:9584 is Inter 16 with the time (characters 25-32) in Inter SemiBold 600 at the same size; close button 6309:14029 is 44x32 with fill #222222 (BG/A1). Native key frame 12-continue-watching__resume-toast-native__14m09.8s. Transcript 14:00: 'I have like five seconds to respond'.
findings.actual: applyRestoreQueryForURL publishes _restorePrompt=@{@"time":@(-1)} immediately (module/bridge/MXRServicesBridge.m:388). VLCPlayerBackend.restorePrompt (Sources/MXRVLCBackend/VLCPlayerBackend.swift:67-70) turns -1 µs into a prompt, and MediaTime formats it as '-00:00:00' (Sources/MXRCore/Foundation/MediaTime.swift:91-100), so the toast says 'You already watched till -00:00:00' until the library replies, or for its whole 5 s life when the ML has no entry. PlayerView.swift:179 builds the time as Text(...) + Text(time).bold() on a custom CTFont, so .bold() falls back to SF at about 13 pt and the time is smaller and in another typeface (r2_S12_toast.png vs v_S12_toast.png). The close button background is bgA4 (line 187), invisible on the toast. The resume span uses bgAccentBright, the same color as the played fill (Sources/MXRUI/Player/PlayerControls.swift:349-351), so the bar reads as if 45 minutes were already watched. The timeout does not pause on hover (PlayerModel.swift:221-235), and .transition(.opacity) has no animation transaction, so the toast pops in and out (PlayerView.swift:84-89).
findings.fix: Publish the prompt only when a valid time (≥ a few seconds) is known, otherwise do not show it. Give the time an explicit Inter SemiBold 16 font token. Use bgA1 for the close-button background. Color the resume span BG/Accent Dark (or accent at about 8% alpha) and the marker BG/Accent Bright. Pause the 5 s timer while the toast is hovered. Show and hide inside withAnimation(.easeOut(0.15)).
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed. applyRestoreQueryForURL publishes @{time:-1} before the library replies. MediaTime(-1 µs).formatted gives '-' + 00:00:00, so the toast reads '-00:00:00', and for the whole 5 s when the ML has no record. The bar marker is then drawn at 0. The bold time is visibly smaller and in a different face in r2_S12_toast vs the video frame. Only Inter Light, Regular, Medium and SemiBold are bundled, so .bold() on the concatenated Text cannot resolve to Inter. Use an explicit Inter SemiBold 16 token. The close button uses bgA4 where Figma 6309:14029 uses #222222 (BG/A1). The resume span is filled bgAccentBright, the played-fill color, so the S12 render reads as 45 minutes already played, while the video shows a near-black span with a faint marker. The hover-pause suggestion is not design-backed; keep it optional.

findings.title: Pressing Play (button or Space) with an empty queue produces a raw error card, 'The play queue is empty or cannot start.', with a system-styled 'Retry Playback' button
findings.designEvidence: Figma Player-6 idle state: title 'VLC Media Player', quiet bars. PHILOSOPHY §4 and design principle 1: reuse Figma components (Button.png); never invent a visual language. Principle 2: quiet by default. The owner's screenshot shows this card.
findings.actual: MXRPlayPauseButton is always enabled (Sources/MXRUI/Player/PlayerControls.swift:48). PlayerModel.togglePlayPause calls backend.play() when stopped (Sources/MXRCore/Models/PlayerModel.swift:90-92). The bridge returns Fail("The play queue is empty or cannot start.") (module/bridge/MXRServicesBridge.m:599), which VLCPlayerBackend stores as commandError (VLCPlayerBackend.swift:147) and exposes as errorMessage. PlayerView then shows a card with a system .buttonStyle(.bordered) button (Sources/MXRUI/Player/PlayerView.swift:156-162). 'Retry' repeats the same failing command, and commandError stays until the media or state changes.
findings.fix: With an empty queue, make Play (button and Space) open the Open Files panel (the empty canvas already offers 'Open a media file'), or disable it with help text; never turn a command refusal into a playback error card. Keep the error card for real input errors (vlc_player_GetError), build it from the Figma Button and secondary tokens, and offer actions that make sense ('Open File…', 'Skip').
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed (MXRServicesBridge.m:590-599 → commandError → errorMessage → card in PlayerView.swift videoSurface with .buttonStyle(.bordered)). Worse than described: the card sits in the same ZStack as the 'Open a media file' button, so with no media both appear centred on top of each other. Design evidence correction: Player-6 is not an idle state; it shows a playing cat video titled 'VLC Media Player'. The finding rests on principles 1-2 and the owner's screenshot. The fix is right: Play with an empty queue should open Open Files, or be disabled.

findings.title: Time labels use proportional digits, so the centred label shifts sideways every second; single clicks are delayed by a double-click recognizer
findings.designEvidence: VIDEO_BREAKDOWN §02 SHOULD: hh:mm:ss with tabular digits. spec-part1 §0.2: 'tabular figures ("00:00:00", 64px wide)'. Figma Current Time 1904:7238 (Default/hover/click with orange caret) and Duration 1905:7312 (Default/click = remaining).
findings.actual: Theme.Font.time is Inter Regular 15 and monospacedDigit/tnum is used nowhere. Measured in the bundled Inter-Regular.otf: '1' advances 0.46 em and '4' advances 0.64 em, so the centred 76 pt label moves as digits change. MXRTimeLabel attaches both .onTapGesture(count: 2) and .onTapGesture (Sources/MXRUI/Player/PlayerControls.swift:105-108), so the single-click actions (edit current time, toggle remaining) wait out the double-click interval. Double-clicking Duration opens an edit mode the design does not have, pre-filled with the current time (line 127).
findings.fix: Apply .monospacedDigit() (Inter has tnum) to the bar labels, the preview-card time and the toast time. Use one single-tap gesture per label (current: edit; duration: toggle remaining) and drop the invented double-click edit on Duration.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed. There is no monospacedDigit or tnum anywhere in Sources, and Theme.Font.time is Inter Regular 15 (Tokens.swift:389). .onTapGesture(count:2) placed before .onTapGesture delays every single click by the double-click interval. The Duration double-click edit, and its help text 'double-click to seek', are invented. VIDEO_BREAKDOWN §02 SHOULD and spec §0.2 ask for tabular figures.

findings.title: A single click on the seek bar sends two seeks, fast then precise, so the frame visibly jumps twice
findings.designEvidence: VIDEO_BREAKDOWN §02: a thick, easy-to-hit seek bar; clicking should land where the pointer is.
findings.actual: DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0) calls onChanged with .fast and then onEnded with .precise (Sources/MXRUI/Player/PlayerControls.swift:363-367). A click first decodes the nearest keyframe and then the exact frame: two decoder flushes and a visible double jump.
findings.fix: Send fast seeks only after the drag moves more than about 3 pt; a click sends one precise seek in onEnded.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed. DragGesture(minimumDistance:0) fires onChanged(.fast) on mouse-down, then onEnded(.precise), so a click causes two seeks and decoder flushes. Fold this into the BB-02 throttle work: one precise seek per click.

findings.title: The display link re-evaluates the whole seek bar body (and both waveform paths) on every frame while playing
findings.designEvidence: PHILOSOPHY §2.4: idle player under 1% CPU. PlaybackClock.swift's own header comment says only the playhead should be driven per frame.
findings.actual: PlayerDisplayLink writes @State position every frame (Sources/MXRUI/Player/PlayerControls.swift:387-391). That re-runs the whole MXRSeekBar body: GeometryReader, ZStack, resume marker, and two WaveformShape paths of up to 244 rounded rectangles each (lines 336-340). This happens at 60-120 Hz, while for a 25-minute video the playhead moves about 1 px per second.
findings.fix: Put the playhead in its own small view (or a CALayer) driven by the display link, and update it only when it moves at least 0.5 px. Cache the waveform path keyed by (samples, width).
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed. The display link writes @State position every frame (PlayerControls.swift:387-391), which re-runs the whole MXRSeekBar body, including two WaveformShape paths. That is the opposite of PlaybackClock's own header contract. Keep the good part: labels change once per second (displaySecond), and the link stops when bars are hidden or playback is paused.

findings.title: Compact bar: the overflow '⋯' is accent-colored at rest, and the layout collapses all at once instead of progressively
findings.designEvidence: Principle 11: a resting clickable icon is FG/A2 gray, and orange means active. Figma iconButton 177:97 has FG/A2 icons. VIDEO_BREAKDOWN §02: the seek bar fills the free width and must stay easy to hit.
findings.actual: The overflow Menu uses .menuStyle(.borderlessButton) (Sources/MXRUI/Player/PlayerBars.swift:104-113), which tints its template label with the app accent, so the '⋯' renders orange at rest (r3_compact_bar.png). PlayerRowLayout counts the seek bar at the play-button width, 54 pt (line 135), so the full row is kept down to about 736 pt with a useless 54 pt seek bar. Below that, ViewThatFits drops prev/next, both time labels and the audio and subtitle buttons together.
findings.fix: Draw the icon with MXRIcon(.more, tint: fgA2) in a plain button that shows the menu, or apply .tint(fgA2) to that Menu. Collapse progressively (duration, then prev/next, then track buttons) and keep a minimum seek width of about 160 pt.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed visually (r3_compact_bar.png and r_S01.Player_compact.png: orange '⋯' at rest). Root cause: mxrAccent applies a global .tint(Theme.Color.accentMain) (ThemeEnvironment.swift:31-34), and the .borderlessButton Menu label inherits it. PlayerRowLayout measures the seek bar at the 54 pt play-button width (line 135), and compactItems drops everything except play, seek, volume and queue at once.

findings.title: Hovering the seek bar shows no time at all when thumbnails are unavailable (music, streams, preview preference off, no thumbnailer)
findings.designEvidence: VIDEO_BREAKDOWN §02 MUST: hovering anywhere on the seek bar shows a floating card with a frame thumbnail plus a timestamp. Figma thumbnail 2151:9673 and the 'audio value' chip 2245:9805 show the style for a small value chip.
findings.actual: previewsEnabled requires showsSeekThumbnails && hasThumbnails && !isAudioOnly (Sources/MXRUI/Player/PlayerControls.swift:319-321), and the overlay is shown only when previewsEnabled is true (line 379). With music (the waveform layout) there is no hover feedback.
findings.fix: When no thumbnail can be produced, show a time-only chip (bgB1Transparent, Inter 15, styled like the 121x37 audio-value chip) centred above the pointer.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed (previewsEnabled requires hasThumbnails && !isAudioOnly, and the overlay is gated on it). There is no hover feedback for music, for a disabled preference or for a missing thumbnailer. The design does not draw a time-only chip, so this is an improvement suggestion grounded in the §02 MUST ('preview card … plus timestamp'). Minor is right.

findings.title: VLC's own OSD duplicates every control-bar action: a time readout (and in fullscreen the classic VLC slider) on each seek event, a play/pause icon and 'Speed: x'
findings.designEvidence: Design principles 2 (quiet by default) and 6 (one place per function). Video 03:29.3 and 20:07: scrubbing shows only the preview card and the bar, with no engine text over the video. VIDEO_BREAKDOWN §02: the bar plus preview card is the seek feedback. §13: OSD is for shortcut feedback, with the key named.
findings.actual: The bridge never disables the engine OSD (no var_Create or var_SetBool of 'osd' in module/; video_text.c:99 and video_widgets.c:289 gate only on var_InheritBool(vout,"osd"), default true). Every SeekByPos or SeekByTime the bar sends (PlayerControls.swift:363-367 → MXRServicesBridge.m seekPosition) calls vlc_player_osd_Position (src/player/input.c:153 and 179). That flushes and redraws 'hh:mm:ss / hh:mm:ss' at the top right on every drag event, so the text flickers during a scrub. When the app has told the engine it is fullscreen, it also draws VLC's old horizontal OSD slider over the video (src/player/osd.c:150-151). Play/pause from the bar shows the engine play/pause icon (src/player/player.c:1292 and 1349), and rate changes from the speed slider show 'Speed: %.2fx' (player.c:1430). The redesigned bar, preview card and SwiftUI OSD then compete with legacy VLC overlays.
findings.fix: Same mechanism as BB-06. At interface start, var_Create(player,"osd",VLC_VAR_BOOL) and var_SetBool(player,"osd",false). This is per-player and inherited by vouts, with no engine edit. Route only the design's shortcut feedback (action plus 'Pressed X') through one SwiftUI OSD. Re-wire 'Show feedback for shortcuts' to the app OSD instead of VLC's global 'osd' option.

findings.title: The outside-shadow mask hard-clips the y+8 shadow under the volume chip (and menus), leaving a straight cut line
findings.designEvidence: Figma 'audio value' 2245:9805: drop shadow (Effect menuShadow: y 8, blur 15, #000 at 46%) with a soft falloff and no visible edge.
findings.actual: PlayerOutsideShadow (Sources/MXRUI/Player/PlayerMenus.swift:156-169) masks the shadow with Rectangle().padding(-blur), which extends only 15 pt around the shape. The shadow is offset 8 pt down with a 15 pt blur, so its lower part is cut at a hard horizontal edge 15 pt below the chip. A scratch reproduction rendered with ImageRenderer (scratchpad/shadowtest/shadow.png) shows the straight cut line on a light background. Over bright video it reads as a faint rectangular frame edge.
findings.fix: Pad the mask by blur + |y| + spread on each side (for example padding(-(blur + abs(y) + spread))), or draw the shadow with .compositingGroup().shadow() on the shape and cut out the interior with an even-odd mask that has no outer bound.

findings.title: The seek-preview thumbnail is scaledToFill, so non-16:9 video (2.39:1 films, 4:3 TV) is center-cropped in the card
findings.designEvidence: Figma thumbnail 2151:9673: a 252x142 image well on a placeholder background. VIDEO_BREAKDOWN §02: the card exists to recognise the frame you are seeking to (transcript 3:00).
findings.actual: MXRSeekPreview draws Image(...).resizable().scaledToFill() inside the 252x142 box (Sources/MXRUI/Player/PlayerControls.swift:291-299). For a 2.39:1 film about 26% of the width is cut off, and 4:3 content loses its top and bottom. The preview then shows a zoomed partial frame that does not match the video above it.
findings.fix: Use scaledToFit inside the existing thumbPlaceholder well (letterbox or pillarbox), keeping the 252x142 box and its radius. Request the thumbnail at the well's aspect only for 16:9 media.

refuted.note: Refuted. The design specifies these values. spec-part2:422 (Settings, Audio, Volume) reads: Maximum volume slider at 200%; Startup volume selector with 'Remember last volume' selected and 'Always starts at: [200%]'; Volume step [input 1]. MXRAppOptions.inc (max 200, startup 200 used only in the 'Always starts at' mode, step 1) and the default remember-volume behavior match Figma. VLC's AOUT_VOLUME_STEP does not override an explicit Figma value. The mute glyph and muted state are listed as OPEN in VIDEO_BREAKDOWN §02 and spec-part1:215, and orange-when-muted is a defensible 'active' state. At most this is a product question (1% per key press is slow), not a defect.

grades.justification: Completeness 42: there is a gallery state for almost every screen, but the VLC bridge doesn't implement the library model the design depends on. Folder hierarchy, the multi-crumb breadcrumb, the current-folder chip, the Music split, Home sections and chevrons, default streams, m3u expansion, playlist thumbnails and launch-to-Home are missing or fake in the real app. Fidelity 55: the gallery renders are near-identical to Figma (mostly PASS/REVIEW), but in the real app the menus sit inside NSPopover bubbles with arrows, the Figma hover states are missing (rows, mini player), system buttons, spinners and alerts leak in, and real data (no artist, -1 progress, first-frame thumbnails) breaks the designed row states. Code quality 48: the Swift models are clean (generation tokens, paging, debounce), but the mock and the VLC bridge implement two different domain models, gallery fixtures are tuned to Figma pixels, and the bridge does full-list counts and reloads on every media-library event. There are also hover-anchored popovers, gesture conflicts, ForEach keyed by offset and duplicated drop code.

doneWell: Gallery renders of nearly every library state match Figma closely. Checked by eye: S28 compact S01 list (378pt panel, 42pt pitch, watched dimming, ▶ now-playing overlay), S33 Music root, S35 Network, S38 Playlists, S40/S43 Home, S44 grid, S45 four-column list with the '+' only in list mode, S46 mini player with expanded queue, S36 Open Network Stream and S39 New Playlist (including the per-edge dashed drop outline). Keep the geometry and tokens when fixing behavior.

Menu contents follow the Figma lists exactly: file 2404:13340, folder 2139:8935, playlist 2459:9389, the 16 sorts with music-only filtering, Grid/List view options, and two-tone icons. Only the presentation (popover chrome) is wrong.

LibraryModel is well structured: back/forward stacks, generation tokens that drop stale results, cancellable load-more with tokens, a 250 ms search debounce, per-category sort, and a keepingLoaded reload that avoids losing scrolled pages.

The bridge runs all media-library work on a serial background queue with atomic shutdown handling, and network collections are persisted as real ML playlists so they survive restarts. That is a good basis once they are filtered out of Playlists.
Drag from library rows provides file URLs, and queue rows show a 2pt orange insertion line on drop, matching the spec's inferred indicator.
The music now-playing composition (738×737 art, glow, 73pt title gap, centered on the window) matches Player - Music, and the layout switches automatically to the music control bar for audio.
The mini player snaps to the nearest corner with an animation that respects Reduce Motion, and fits short windows by shrinking the video before dropping the queue.
Dialogs keep Save disabled until the input is valid (URL parsing, playlist name) and surface parse errors inline instead of failing silently.

findings.title: Real backend flattens the library: no folders, a single generic breadcrumb, and the top-bar folder chip always says 'Videos'
findings.designEvidence: VIDEO_BREAKDOWN §08 MUST: the top bar shows a folder icon plus the current folder name ('S01'), and clicking it opens the compact library at the current folder. The breadcrumb is a clickable address line ('… ▸ The Wand ▸ S01'). Transcript 9:30: she criticizes VLC because files 'just all show up next to each other regardless of the folder they are in'. Transcript 10:00: 'an address line that you can click on to go up and down in folders'. Figma Player-1/3/4 (970:3308/2703/4028): breadcrumb 'Videos ▸ Shows ▸ The Wand ▸ S01'. Key frame 08-library__compact-library-plus-queue-native__11m57.0s: the chip reads 'S01'.
findings.actual: MXRLibraryServices.m:111 maps Videos to vlc_ml_list_video_media, a flat list of every video, which is exactly the VLC 3 behavior she criticized. Line 115 can list a folder, but nothing in the bridge ever emits {type:'folder'} entries, so folders are unreachable. The breadcrumb request (lines 298-304) returns one crumb whose title is [kind capitalizedString], so navigating into an album, artist, genre or show shows the literal word 'Album'/'Artist'/'Genre'/'Show', and the root crumb ('Videos ▸') is never present. LMedia (lines 17-29) never sends 'folder', so MediaItem.folder is always nil. As a result PlayerBars.swift:280-292 always shows 'Videos' (or 'Songs'), and clicking it opens the flat Videos list. The mini player folder chip (MXRMiniPlayerView.swift:60) never appears, and the per-folder preset key (MediaItem.presetKey) never resolves. InterfaceModel.toggleCompactLibrary opens at whatever location was last shown, initially Home. MockData.swift:284-351 implements the full hierarchy, so every gallery check passes.
findings.fix: 1) Videos root: vlc_ml_list_entry_points / VLC_ML_LIST_FOLDERS_BY_TYPE(video), returned as type 'folder' entries. Folder location: VLC_ML_LIST_SUBFOLDERS (as folder entries) followed by vlc_ml_list_folder_media. 2) Breadcrumb: walk ancestors (match the folder MRL against the parent-path chain using vlc_ml_get_folder_by_mrl, or subfolder parent ids), prefix the category root, and resolve album/artist/genre/show names with vlc_ml_get_album/artist/genre/show. 3) In LMedia, add folder {id,name} by resolving the main file MRL's directory with vlc_ml_get_folder_by_mrl. 4) Make the sidebar toggle and the chip navigate to .folder(current) before showing the panel. 5) Add a contract test that runs the same LibraryModel scenario against the mock and the bridge.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed in code. MXRLibraryServices.m:111 maps Videos to vlc_ml_list_video_media. No bridge path emits a {type:'folder'} entry. The breadcrumb at :298-304 returns one crumb whose title is [kind capitalizedString]. LMedia (:17-29) sends neither 'folder' nor 'episode'. PlayerBars.swift:280-292 falls back to 'Videos'/'Songs', and InterfaceModel.toggleCompactLibrary (:224) never navigates. Key frame 11m57.0s shows the 'S01' chip and '… ▸ The Wand ▸ S01'. Correction to the fix: this VLC 4 header has no vlc_ml_get_folder_by_mrl, and vlc_ml_folder_t has no parent id. Ancestors therefore have to be built by walking vlc_ml_list_entry_points plus VLC_ML_LIST_SUBFOLDERS and matching MRL prefixes, or from an app-side parent map. vlc_ml_list_folders_by_type, VLC_ML_LIST_SUBFOLDERS, vlc_ml_count_folder_media and vlc_ml_get_album/artist do exist. The chip name can also come from the file URL's parent directory, which works even for files outside the library. Another consequence: because folder and episode are always nil, MediaItem.presetKey is always nil, so per-show and per-folder presets (§07) never work with VLC. Do not break: the mock hierarchy and the compact breadcrumb collapse already match Figma 848:1995 almost pixel for pixel.

findings.title: The Music category is a flat file list: Songs/Albums/Artists/Genres are unreachable and songs show file names instead of 'title - artist'
findings.designEvidence: VIDEO_BREAKDOWN §09 MUST: the Music root lists '+ Add · Songs · Albums · Artists · Genres', and folder views show square art with 'title - artist'. Transcript 12:00: 'the actual music section gets divided into songs, albums, artists, and genres'. Figma sidebar.png music variant 858:5001, Player - Music-1 4778:25123 ('untangle - juxtopposed'). Key frame 09-music__music-root-songs-albums-artists-genres__12m12.4s.
findings.actual: MXRLibraryServices.m:112 maps both music and songs to vlc_ml_list_audio_media, a flat list. No 'link' entries and no addAction 'add' are returned (line 275 sets addAction only for network), so the albums, artists and genres pages (lines 249-264) can never be reached from the UI. LMedia (lines 22-25) sends no artist, album, genre or trackNumber. MediaItem.listTitle therefore falls back to the file name ('01 untangle.mp3'). Listen Again cards lose their artist line (LibrarySupport.swift mxrSubtitle returns media.artist, which is nil). Sorting by artist/album/track number has no visible data. The gallery passes because MockData.swift:328-336 returns the four links plus Add.
findings.fix: At kind 'music', return '+ Add' (addAction 'add') and four {type:'link'} entries (songs/albums/artists/genres, with icon names). Make 'songs' list audio entry-point folders, as Figma's 'Songs ▸ My Songs' does. In LMedia, add artist (from album_track.i_artist_id via vlc_ml_get_artist, or the media's artist name), album, genre, track and disc numbers, and psz_filename. Use album thumbnails for the album grid and add a 200pt square grid for Albums and Artists (§09 OPEN).
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed. :112 returns a flat audio list for both 'music' and 'songs'. addAction is set only for network (:275), and no 'link' entries are returned, so the albums/artists/genres pages (:249-264) cannot be reached. LMedia sends no artist, so listTitle falls back to fileName (MediaItem.swift:182-185) and mxrSubtitle is nil. The design evidence holds: transcript 12:00, the §09 MUST, and key frame 09-music now-playing showing '+ Add' plus 'title - juxtopposed' rows. The fix is small, because the bridge already has the album, artist and genre queries. vlc_ml_media_t.album_track has i_artist_id, i_album_id, i_genre_id, i_track_nb and i_disc_nb.

findings.title: Launch shows the blank-cone start screen she explicitly replaced; pressing Play then shows a raw engine error with a system 'Retry Playback' button
findings.designEvidence: VIDEO_BREAKDOWN §11 MUST: when there is nothing to resume, launching VLC opens the full-window library on Home, never a blank cone screen. Transcript 13:30: 'Instead of this blank cone, now you come back to VLC and see a full media library ready to continue wherever you left off.' Figma Player-5 (6261:15078). Key frame 11-playlists-home__home-full-window-native__13m57.3s.
findings.actual: InterfaceModel.swift:143 sets library = .hidden by default, and nothing in MXRPlugin switches to .full at launch. PlayerView.swift:147-153 draws the VLC cone with 'Open a media file', the old start screen. Pressing Space or Play with an empty queue reaches MXRServicesBridge.m:599, which fails with 'The play queue is empty or cannot start.' PlayerView.swift:155-160 then shows that string in a translucent card with Button('Retry Playback').buttonStyle(.bordered), the owner's screenshot. The 'Retry' does the same thing again.
findings.fix: On launch, if there is no resume prompt or opened file, set interface.library = .full and navigate to .home. Treat play with an empty queue as a no-op or open the library or file picker, not as an error. Reserve the error card for real input errors and style it with the Figma Button component (500:3063) and in-design copy.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed. The default is in InterfaceModel.swift:142 (not :143). Nothing in MXRPlugin sets .full at launch: the only references are AppModel.swift:148 (→ .hidden) and the showFullLibrary command. With an empty queue, vlc_player_Start returns VLC_EGENERIC (src/player/player.c:1257-1269). That reaches Fail at MXRServicesBridge.m:599, then commandError, then PlayerView.swift:155-160, which shows the raw string with a .bordered system 'Retry Playback' that fails the same way. This is the owner's screenshot, and it contradicts the §11 MUST and transcript 13:30.

findings.title: Gallery fidelity comes from a mock that implements a different domain model plus Figma-tuned fixtures, so pixel checks hide every real-data gap
findings.designEvidence: PHILOSOPHY §2.5: every screen also runs against a mock backend for previews, which implies the same contract. AGENTS: every UI change is verified visually. The owner reports the app 'looks right at first glance but behaves differently'.
findings.actual: MockData.swift:284-351 provides multi-level breadcrumbs, folder, link and addAction rows, five Home sections with destinations, and progress=1 for watched items (MockLibrary.swift setWatched). The VLC bridge provides none of these (see L01, L02, L09-L11, L17). Gallery entries also apply pixel hacks: MockLibrary.swift:14-23 usesFigmaHomeProgress, usesFigmaCompactHomeProgress and usesFigmaGridProgress hard-code bar lengths. LibraryGallery.swift:42/69 sets fixtureFileNameOverrides to reproduce Figma's typo 'The_Wand_S01E13mp4', and line 22 sets media.artist = 'S01' on a video so the mini player artist chip matches 970:3070. LibraryEntryView.swift:91 and LibraryModel rely on cachedPage, cachedHomeSections and cachedBreadcrumb, which only the mock implements. So S28/S33/S40/S43/S44/S45/S46 PASS while the shipped app shows something else.
findings.fix: Write the LibraryBackend contract as tests: location → entry kinds, addAction, crumbs, non-empty sections with destinations, progress semantics (nil vs -1). Run them against MockLibrary and against the bridge (module/tests/bridge-smoke.m with a temporary ML and a fixture folder tree). Remove the Figma-pixel fixture flags or confine them to a clearly separate 'Figma replica' scenario that is not used as acceptance evidence. Add gallery entries for hover, empty-real-data and loading states.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed. The MockLibrary flags (:14-23) hard-code Figma bar lengths. LibraryGallery.swift:22 sets artist='S01' on a video, and :42/:69 add the Figma typo override. Only the mock implements cachedPage, cachedHomeSections and cachedBreadcrumb. MockData.entries(at:) returns add/createPlaylist/link rows that the bridge never returns. This is the main reason S28-S47 pass while the shipped app differs. The bridge-contract test proposed in the fix is the right lever.

findings.title: A single click on a library row wipes the queue and replaces it with the whole loaded page; there is no selection model
findings.designEvidence: PHILOSOPHY §3.7: Queue ≠ playlist, the queue is what plays next. Key frame 08-library__drag-library-row-to-queue__11m45.8s: E05 plays from a 15-item folder, the queue holds '1 item - 23m', and she drags E06 in to make '2 items - 47m' (11m57.0s). Transcript 11:30: 'you'd just drag whatever you want from the library to the queue'. Mac convention: click selects, double-click or Return opens.
findings.actual: LibraryEntryView.swift:27 makes the whole row a Button that calls MXRLibraryActions.open (LibrarySupport.swift:55-69). That calls app.play(media, context: app.library.mediaEntries), which runs queue.playNow(context) (AppModel.swift:99-105) and replaces the existing queue with every loaded entry (up to pageSize 100). Because Videos is the flat list from L01, clicking one episode queues up to 100 unrelated videos from the whole library in sort order. There is no hover background, no selection, no multi-select, no keyboard navigation and no Return to play, and dragging always carries a single item.
findings.fix: Click: select (FG/2 label as in Figma hover/selected). Double-click or Return: play that item only (replace the current item, keep the user's queue), or play it and append the folder only when the queue is empty. Keep 'Play folder' and 'Shuffle' in the folder menu. Add Cmd/Shift multi-select, and drag the selection as one payload. Use arrow keys and type-select.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed. The row Button (LibraryEntryView.swift:27) calls MXRLibraryActions.open, which calls app.play(media, context: mediaEntries), which runs queue.playNow and replaces the queue with up to 100 loaded entries. Key frames 11m45.8s and 11m57.0s show E05 playing from a 15-item folder with the queue at '1 item - 23m', then '2 items - 47m' after a drag. That supports 'click plays one item; you build the queue'. The design never states click versus double-click semantics explicitly, so the selection model is Mac convention rather than Figma. The queue wipe contradicts the shown behavior.

findings.title: The row ⋯ menu is anchored to a view that exists only while the row is hovered, so it closes when the pointer moves into it; the Figma hover label state is also missing
findings.designEvidence: VIDEO_BREAKDOWN §08 MUST: on hover, '⋯' appears at the row end and opens the file context menu (Figma 2404:13340). Figma media component 2404:9167: hover-watched 2404:9256 and hover-unwatched 2404:9168 change the label to FG/2 #C6C6C6, versus #969696 normal and #6B6B6B watched. The playlist row component 2459:9352 behaves the same.
findings.actual: LibraryEntryView.swift:52-60: `if hovered { LibraryIconButton(...).popover(isPresented: $popup) {...} }`, with .onHover { hovered = $0 } at line 68. When the popover window opens and the pointer leaves the row to reach it, the row gets mouseExited, hovered becomes false, and the popover's anchor view is removed, so SwiftUI dismisses the popover. Only keyboard use or right-click remains. The label colour (lines 22-24) ignores hover, so the FG/2 brightening never happens. Grid cards have no hover affordance at all.
findings.fix: Keep the anchor alive with `if hovered || popup`, or attach the menu to the row container. Include hover in `color` (fg2 when hovered or selected). Add a gallery entry that renders the hover variant against 2404:9168/9256.
findings.verifyNote: The code is as described: `if hovered { …popover }` at :52-60 with onHover at :68. Dismissal when the pointer moves into the NSPopover window (the anchor view is removed) is highly likely, but I could not confirm it at runtime. The hover label colour is verified from figma_file.json: 2404:9168 and 2404:9256 text is #C6C6C6, unwatched #969696 and watched #6B6B6B, and the code (:22-24) ignores hover. The key frame at 11m45.8s shows the hover '⋯' on row E06.

findings.title: All library menus are rendered inside system NSPopover bubbles (with an arrow and system material) instead of the Figma dropdown cards; some are invented system-styled lists
findings.designEvidence: Figma Sorting Options 856:2215, View Options 858:3290, folder context menu 2139:8935, file context menu 2404:13340, playlist context menu 2459:9389: flat 265pt cards with radius 12, the 'bg blur + shadow' effect, anchored under the trigger, with no arrow. Spec-part1 §08 sort menu. Key frames 08-library__sort-menu-watched-unwatched__10m49.5s and 08-library__more-menu-add-file-folder__10m55.5s.
findings.actual: These menus use SwiftUI .popover: LibraryNavigation.swift:146 (sort), 156 (view), 167 (⋯), 185 (+), 42 (rail +), LibraryEntryView.swift:54 (row ⋯) and MXRMiniPlayerView.swift:164 (queue sort). On macOS that is an NSPopover with an arrow and its own bubble, so the Figma card appears as a card inside a bubble. The gallery renders MXRLibraryPopupView in isolation, so this is never seen. The Network ⋯ menu adds a system-styled 'Browse Devices & Network Sources…' Button above the Figma menu in a bgA3 VStack (LibraryNavigation.swift:168-174). The mini player queue sort popover is plain system Buttons in a VStack, including the raw enum text 'Repeat: all' (MXRMiniPlayerView.swift:164-173).
findings.fix: Build one shared in-window dropdown presenter: an overlay anchored with anchorPreference, or a borderless child NSPanel for overflow. It needs no arrow, a consistent 120-150 ms fade/scale that respects Reduce Motion, Esc and outside-click dismissal, and arrow-key navigation. Use it for every library menu and for the app ⋯ menu so all menus behave the same (also see C4). Make 'Browse Sources' a regular two-tone row in the Figma menu. Use MXRLibraryPopupView rows for the queue sort.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed at all the cited lines. SwiftUI .popover on macOS is an arrowed NSPopover, and MXRLibraryPopupView draws its own blurred card inside it (LibraryPopup.swift:76). The gallery renders the popup view directly (LibraryGallery S29-S32), so the bubble never appears in checks. The queue sort popover is a set of plain system Buttons, with 'Repeat: \(rawValue)' producing 'Repeat: all/off/one' (MXRMiniPlayerView.swift:171). This is a valid root-cause contributor to C4.

findings.title: Root cause of the '0 items' header; fresh installs show orphan Home headings; counts ignore search
findings.designEvidence: Spec-part2 §11 D/E: Home shows '110 items' plus non-empty sections. LibraryValues.swift:403 contract: 'Empty sections are not returned.' VIDEO_BREAKDOWN §08 header: 'N items'.
findings.actual: The Home count comes from LibraryModel.swift:155/175, totalCount = backend.mediaCount. That reads MXRLibraryServices.m:61/79, vlc_ml_count_media(ml, NULL), which is medialibrary mediaFiles() and counts only indexed (internal) media. Continue Watching comes from vlc_ml_list_history (GLOBAL, line 294), which includes external media you opened directly. A user who hasn't added a library folder therefore sees '0 items' above Continue Watching rows (the owner's screenshot). The bridge also always returns both sections even when they are empty (line 296), so a fresh install shows 'Continue Watching ›' and 'Listen Again ›' with nothing under them instead of the empty state (MXRLibraryView.swift:116 checks homeSections.isEmpty). The totals for playlists, albums, artists and genres use NULL params (lines 248, 254, 260, 264), so while searching the header shows the unfiltered count and hasMore keeps paging.
findings.fix: Home count: count what Home represents. Either drop it, as the Figma compact Home could, or use vlc_ml_count_history plus vlc_ml_count_media, or the sum of section lengths. Omit empty sections in the bridge. Pass the same pattern params to the count functions (vlc_ml_count_playlists(&p…)).
findings.verifyNote: Mostly confirmed. totalCount = backend.mediaCount comes from vlc_ml_count_media(NULL), which in medialibrary.cpp:987-997 is m_ml->mediaFiles(). In libmedialibrary that counts only indexed (internal) media; I could not read the libmedialibrary source locally, but this is consistent with the owner's '0 items' above Continue Watching. Always returning both sections (:296) confirmed: on a fresh install, homeSections is non-empty, so MXRLibraryView.swift:116 shows headings with nothing under them instead of the empty state. The search-count part is minor: hasMore triggers one extra empty page, then stops.

findings.title: Network: m3u links are not expanded into a channel list, there are no default Podcasts/Radio streams, saved streams also appear under Playlists, and streams cannot be removed
findings.designEvidence: VIDEO_BREAKDOWN §10 MUST: 'The defaults include Podcasts and Radio' and 'Saving adds the stream, or the expanded m3u playlist, to the Network category'. Transcript 12:20: 'By default there are a bunch of streams saved here'. Transcript 13:00: 'Now it's an automatic playlist with all the videos listed.' Key frames 10-network-open__network-category-default-streams__12m28.4s and 13m18.66 ('Index'). Figma sidebar network variant 858:5294.
findings.actual: saveNetworkURLs (MXRLibraryServices.m:181-216) stores the .m3u URL itself as a single vlc_ml_new_stream media, so itemCount is 1. LibraryValues.swift:275 then gives the row no destination; it can only be played, never browsed. No default entries are seeded. The Playlists page lists VLC_ML_PLAYLIST_TYPE_ALL (lines 244-248), so every saved network collection, which is stored as a real ML playlist, appears again under Playlists. The Network page also lists every network URL ever played from history as if it were a saved stream (lines 158-165). removeNetworkStream, removeFromPlaylist and removeFolder have no UI anywhere in MXRUI.
findings.fix: Expand playlists on save: preparse with subitems via vlc_preparser, append each child MRL to the ML playlist and name it. Keep network collections out of the Playlists query (tag them by name prefix or keep an app-side id set). Seed defaults on first run, for example VLC's podcast and Icecast service-discovery roots or editable starter entries. Add Remove, Rename and Remove from Playlist actions to the stream, playlist and folder row menus.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed. A saved .m3u becomes a 1-item playlist, and LibraryValues.swift:275 needs itemCount > 1 for a destination, so it can only be played. :245 lists TYPE_ALL, so network collections also appear under Playlists. :158-165 turns network history into 'saved' streams. No default Podcasts/Radio rows are seeded (key frame 12m28.4s shows them; the mock does too). There are no UI call sites for removeNetworkStream, removeFromPlaylist or removeFolder (grep over MXRUI, MXRCore/Models and MXRPlugin).

findings.title: The real Home has two sections and inert chevrons; Frequently Visited Folders is missing
findings.designEvidence: VIDEO_BREAKDOWN §11 MUST: sections Continue Watching ›, Listen Again › and Frequently Visited Folders ›, and 'Section titles with › open the full list'. Figma Player-5 6261:15078 and sidebar home 1106:5633 (which also has Frequently Visited Playlists and Frequently Listened Artists).
findings.actual: The bridge homeSections request (MXRLibraryServices.m:292-297) returns only continueWatching and listenAgain, with no 'destination'. MXRLibraryView.swift:167-177 renders the chevron button `.disabled(section.destination == nil)`, so the › chevrons do nothing in the real app. Continue Watching also includes audio with partial progress, shown as 16:9 video cards. The mock returns five sections with destinations, so the gallery looks complete.
findings.fix: Add a destination for each section: Recent filtered to in-progress items, and audio history. Add frequentFolders (group recent history by parent folder, ordered by count), frequentPlaylists and frequentArtists. Filter Continue Watching to video.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed. The bridge returns 2 sections with no 'destination' (:292-297), so the chevrons are .disabled (MXRLibraryView.swift:177). Figma S40 (1106:5633) has 5 sections, verified in the check side-by-side. Audio items with partial progress fall into Continue Watching and get 16:9 cards (`square = kind != .continueWatching`).

findings.title: Watched items very likely lose their orange progress line in the real app (progress -1 wins over displayProgress)
findings.designEvidence: VIDEO_BREAKDOWN §08 MUST, item states: 'watched: dimmed name and an orange progress line along the thumbnail bottom'. Figma media 2404:9166 (Rectangle 12, #D37918). Key frame 11-playlists-home__folder-grid-unwatched-first__20m14.8s: E01-E04 have full bars.
findings.actual: LibrarySupport.swift:248 uses `entry.media?.progress ?? entry.media?.displayProgress`. The bridge sends f_progress unchanged (MXRLibraryServices.m:24). VLC medialibrary reports lastPosition -1 when no position is stored and resets it to -1 when playback passes about 95% and the play count is incremented. A watched item therefore has progress -1, which is non-nil, so it beats displayProgress = 1, and the bar width clamps to 0: dimmed text, no line. The mock sets progress = 1 for watched items, so the gallery hides this. I could not run the app; confirm with one finished file.
findings.fix: Bridge: send 'progress' only when 0 < f_progress < 1. UI: draw `media.displayProgress` (1 when watched, otherwise partial) instead of the raw progress.
findings.verifyNote: The code path is confirmed: entities.cpp:257 copies lastPosition() into f_progress, the bridge sends it as-is, VLCWire maps it to a non-nil progress, and LibrarySupport.swift:248 prefers it over displayProgress. medialibrary resets the position to -1 after roughly 95% and on never-played items, so a watched item draws a 0-width bar. This needs runtime confirmation, but it is likely. A second case: marking a half-watched item as watched keeps the partial bar. The mock sets progress=1 (MockLibrary.swift:108/120), which hides this.

findings.title: The Home page flickers to a system 'Loading library…' spinner on every media-library event; navigation always flashes a system ProgressView
findings.designEvidence: PHILOSOPHY §3.2 'The UI gets out of the way'. Figma has no spinner state. A premium Mac app keeps stale content during a refresh.
findings.actual: VLCLibraryBackend.swift:12 sends .contentChanged for every ML event (MXRLibraryServices.m:38-43, 74-85: any event triggers a count and serviceChanged('library')). LibraryModel.handle then calls reload(keepingLoaded:). reload sets `isLoading = !haveCachedContent` (LibraryModel.swift:162), which is always true for VLC because it has no cache. MXRLibraryView.swift:108 shows ProgressView('Loading library…') whenever `isLoading && entries.isEmpty`, and Home never has entries. So during indexing, thumbnail generation or media start/stop, the Home (and any empty category) is replaced by a system spinner. show() (LibraryModel.swift:262-275) also clears entries on every navigation, which gives a spinner flash.
findings.fix: Show a placeholder only on the very first load and keep the current content during refreshes. Debounce or coalesce ML events (about 250 ms) and react only to relevant event types. Replace ProgressView with an in-design skeleton or nothing.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed. Every ML event goes through engineChanged to serviceChanged('library') and then .contentChanged → reload(keepingLoaded:). For VLC, haveCachedContent is always false, so isLoading becomes true. On Home, entries is always [] (LibraryModel.swift:156), so the ProgressView replaces the Home sections on every event, during indexing and on every play start or stop. Worse than stated: MXRServicesBridge.m:403 also refreshes player and queue on each 'library' change.

findings.title: Right-click 'Add to Playlist' never lists existing playlists in the real app, and the right-click menu diverges from the Figma file context menu
findings.designEvidence: VIDEO_BREAKDOWN §11 MUST: 'Add to Playlist' is available from the file context menu everywhere. §08 MUST: the file context menu follows Figma 2404:13340 (Play, Mark as Watched, Favorite, Stream, Convert, Add to Queue, Add to Playlist, Show in Finder, Go to Source, Add Subtitle/Audio Tracks, Properties). Design principle 6: one place per function.
findings.actual: LibraryEntryView.swift:91-95 builds the submenu from `app.backends.library.cachedPage(at: .playlists)`. VLCLibraryBackend doesn't implement cachedPage (protocol default nil, QueueAndLibraryBackends.swift:122), so the submenu only ever contains 'New Playlist…'. The right-click list (lines 97-148) is a different set from the ⋯ popover: it adds Play Next, Pin and Rename/Delete Playlist, and drops Stream, Convert, Go to Source and Add Subtitle/Audio Tracks. Users get two inconsistent menus for one item.
findings.fix: Keep an observable `playlists` list in LibraryModel, loaded once and refreshed on .playlistsChanged. Generate both the native right-click NSMenu and the ⋯ card from one action table (the Figma order), and keep Pin and Play Next as extras appended to both.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed. VLCLibraryBackend has no cachedPage (protocol default nil, QueueAndLibraryBackends.swift:122), so the right-click submenu only offers 'New Playlist…'. The ⋯ popover path (LibraryPopup.loadPlaylists) loads asynchronously and works, which is a partial workaround. The two menus contain different action sets, as described.

findings.title: The waveform seek bar is drawn for every medium, including normal video: the 'dense tick marks' in the owner's screenshot
findings.designEvidence: VIDEO_BREAKDOWN §09: the waveform is part of the music layout ('you have the waveform seekbar if you want', transcript 12:00). Figma Controls default 491:1779 has a solid thick bar for video, and the music variant 4778:26181 has the waveform. PHILOSOPHY §3.3: 'The seek bar is thick and easy to hit'.
findings.actual: PlayerControls.swift:420-426 requests a waveform for any app.player.media whenever capabilities.supportsWaveform is true. Lines 326/335 draw it whenever `app.interface.showWaveform`, which defaults to true (InterfaceModel.swift:161). Nothing gates on isAudioOnly or layoutKind, so videos with an audio track get the waveform instead of the solid bar, and an extra audio decode pass runs for every video.
findings.fix: Compute and draw the waveform only when app.layoutKind == .music, or when the user explicitly enabled it for video (separate default false). Keep the solid track for video.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed, but this is the control-bar area. supportsWaveform=YES comes from MXRAudioServices.m:135, overriding @NO in MXRServicesBridge.m:407. showWaveform defaults to true at InterfaceModel.swift:160 (not 161). PlayerControls.swift:420-426 has no isAudioOnly or layout gate, so every video with an audio track gets a waveform and runs an extra analysis pass. Figma video controls (491:1779) show a solid bar. This explains the owner's 'dense tick marks'.

findings.title: Mini player: the hover state doesn't follow Figma, there is no close or ended state, scrubbing the bar drags the whole card, and audio shows a black box
findings.designEvidence: Figma Miniplayer 970:3091 hover variants: darkened video, ✕ close at top left, ↗ open-in-player at top right, large white ⏮ ▶ ⏭ centered with no pill, an orange playhead knob on the progress bar, and an ended variant with a replay icon. VIDEO_BREAKDOWN §08 MUST: the card is draggable to any corner. Key frames 08-library__full-window-list-mini-player__11m48.3s and 08-library__mini-player-queue-expanded__11m54.3s.
findings.actual: MXRMiniPlayerView.swift:30-46 shows small FG/A2 LibraryIconButtons inside a bgB1Transparent rounded pill, with no scrim, no ✕, no playhead and no ended or replay state, and no gallery entry for hover. MXRMiniPlayerDock (line 330) puts .simultaneousGesture(DragGesture) on the whole card. That fires together with MiniSeekBar's DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0) at line 287 and with the queue rows' onDrag, so scrubbing or reordering moves the card. For audio the video box is an empty bgB2 rectangle with no cover art (lines 27-29). The folder chip never appears with real data (L01).
findings.fix: Implement the hover variant from 970:3091 (scrim with Theme tokens, ✕ stops playback and hides the dock, ↗ returns to the player, 3 white icons, playhead knob on hover, replay when ended). Start the card drag only from the info strip or a non-interactive area, for example .gesture on the info block, or give the seek bar a highPriorityGesture. Show MXRMediaArtwork when isAudioOnly.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed against Miniplayer.png (970:3091). The hover variant has a dark scrim, ✕ at top left, ↗ at top right, large white ⏮ ▶ ⏭ with no pill, an orange playhead knob, and an ended variant with a replay icon. The code (:30-46) uses small FG/A2 icons in a bgB1Transparent pill, with no ✕, knob or replay. The parent .simultaneousGesture(DragGesture) at :330 runs alongside the seek bar's DragGesture (:287), so scrubbing drags the card. For audio, the box is an empty bgB2 rectangle. The folder and artist chips never appear with real data (Figma shows both, 'S01').

findings.title: Thumbnails are first-frame, unpersisted and serialized; the media-library thumbnailer is never used
findings.designEvidence: VIDEO_BREAKDOWN §08 SHOULD: thumbnails come from VLC's media-library thumbnailer. Figma shows representative frames (Player-3/4 grids).
findings.actual: MXRThumbnailServices.m:35 uses a preparser with max_thumbnailer_threads=1 and an 8 s timeout. Line 67 seeks to args.time, which is 0 for artwork, so most thumbnails are the first frame (often black or a title card). Results live only in VLCThumbnailBackend's in-memory dictionary, which is wiped entirely when it passes 200 entries (VLCServiceBackends.swift:134), so scrolling a large folder makes everything reload and flicker. Cancelled SwiftUI tasks don't cancel the preparser request, so stale decodes queue up serially. vlc_ml_media_generate_thumbnail is never called, and LMedia only uses an already-available SMALL thumbnail.
findings.fix: For ML media, call vlc_ml_media_generate_thumbnail(ml, id, VLC_ML_THUMBNAIL_SMALL, w, h, 0.3), listen for VLC_ML_EVENT_MEDIA_THUMBNAIL_GENERATED and emit .thumbnailReady(id). Use an LRU cache keyed by id and size, and cancel preparser requests when rows disappear. Keep the preparser path for non-library URLs, with a non-zero seek position.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed. There is one thumbnailer thread with an 8 s timeout (MXRThumbnailServices.m:35). The seek time is 0 for artwork. The in-memory dictionary is wiped at more than 200 entries. vlc_ml_media_generate_thumbnail and VLC_ML_EVENT_MEDIA_THUMBNAIL_GENERATED both exist in the header and are unused. Audio files without artworkURL are also sent to the video thumbnailer, where they block the serial queue until they fail. The cache also ignores the requested size; see missed finding LM3.

findings.title: The bridge materializes entire collections just to count them and re-queries on every media-library event
findings.designEvidence: PHILOSOPHY §2.4: as fast as stock VLC, 'we measure, we don't guess'.
findings.actual: MXRLibraryServices.m:269-271 runs listAt a second time with nbResults=0 (the whole unpaged list, converting every vlc_ml_media_t) to read i_nb_items, on every page request and every load-more. networkEntries (lines 148-157) lists the media of every playlist on each Network page load (N+1 queries). Together with L12 (a reload per ML event), a 10k-item library re-lists everything repeatedly during indexing.
findings.fix: Use the count functions: vlc_ml_count_video_media, vlc_ml_count_audio_media, vlc_ml_count_folder_media, vlc_ml_count_history and vlc_ml_count_playlist_media. Cache the network-collection classification and invalidate it on playlist events. Coalesce events.
findings.verifyNote: Real (:269-271 re-lists unpaged to count; networkEntries is N+1), but it runs on the background serial queue and was not measured. Responsiveness impact is stale or lagging results rather than a frozen UI, so this is downgraded to minor. The proposed count functions exist (vlc_ml_count_video_media, vlc_ml_count_history, vlc_ml_count_playlist_media, vlc_ml_count_folder_media). Fix together with L12's event coalescing.

findings.title: The New Playlist thumbnail picker silently discards the chosen image
findings.designEvidence: VIDEO_BREAKDOWN §11 MUST: the New Playlist dialog has a name field and a square thumbnail picker, and 'The playlist will be saved and displayed with this title and thumbnail' (Figma new playlist 6259:14954). SCREENS.md: unsupported operations must show that they are unavailable rather than pretend to succeed.
findings.actual: LibraryDialogs.swift:71-81 lets the user pick an image, and line 162-163 passes artworkURL. VLCLibraryBackend.swift:61-64 forwards it, but the bridge createPlaylist (MXRLibraryServices.m:333-342) never uses artworkURL. The playlist is saved without the thumbnail and the playlist row shows the generic icon.
findings.fix: Persist the playlist artwork app-side (JSON keyed by ML playlist id, copied into Application Support) and return it as Playlist.artworkURL. Otherwise disable the picker with an explanation.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed. artworkURL is forwarded by VLCLibraryBackend.swift:61-64 and ignored by the bridge createPlaylist (:333-342). The dialog copy itself promises 'saved and displayed with this title and thumbnail'.

findings.title: Searching from Home only searches playback history
findings.designEvidence: Figma Player-5 (6261:15078): the full-window Home has the 325pt search field. A user expects library-wide search. S47 (search results) is design-silent, which calls for the macOS convention.
findings.actual: With location == .home and non-empty searchText, LibraryModel requests a page at .home. MXRLibraryServices.m:113 maps home to vlc_ml_list_history with psz_pattern, so only previously played items can be found. Results reuse the 'Home' crumb with no 'Results for …' label. Mixed results render audio as 317×317 squares next to 16:9 cards, and the caption repeats the artist ('untangle - juxtopposed' / 'juxtopposed', S47 render; LibraryEntryView.swift:32-37, MXRLibraryView.swift:156-157).
findings.fix: At Home and category roots, search with VLC_ML media search (vlc_ml_list_media with pattern, plus playlists, folders and artists), grouped into sections. Show 'Results for “x”' in the crumb area. Use 200pt squares for audio, as in Listen Again. Use media.title for the caption when the subtitle is the artist.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed. With searchText set, Home goes to the page path, and :113 sends it to vlc_ml_list_history with a pattern. The S47 render shows the 'Home' crumb, a roughly 317pt square audio card, and the caption 'untangle - juxtopposed / juxtopposed' (title plus a repeated artist line).

findings.title: Music now-playing backdrop has a fixed 1952pt size and no darkening
findings.designEvidence: VIDEO_BREAKDOWN §09 MUST: 'The background is the same art scaled up, blurred and darkened.' Figma Player - Music 4767:23726: a 1952×1952 image with layer blur 20 under Frame 312 with background blur 50, in a 1920 frame.
findings.actual: PlayerView.swift:271-279 (MXRMusicBackdrop) uses a constant MXRPlayerMetrics.backdropSize = 1952 (PlayerMetrics.swift:10) with no dim layer. In fullscreen or windows wider than 1952pt (any 2560-wide 'looks like' display), the blurred art doesn't cover the window and its soft edges and bgA3 background show. A bright cover yields a bright backdrop behind the FG/A1 title, so the text is hard to read. The gallery passes only because the fixture art is nearly black.
findings.fix: Size the backdrop to max(width, height) × 1.02 with aspect fill, using the geometry already available in PlayerView. Add a dim layer (bgB2 at about 40-60%) or a brightness reduction so arbitrary covers read like the Figma example.
findings.verifyNote: Partly refuted, and it belongs to the music-player area. Figma 4767:23726 has no darkening layer: only the 1952² image with LAYER_BLUR 20 (4777:24034) and Frame 312 with BACKGROUND_BLUR 50 and no fill. The 'darkened' wording comes from the breakdown, and the source art is near-black. Keep only the sizing bug: the fixed 1952pt backdrop does not cover windows wider than 1952pt, such as fullscreen on a 2560pt display. A dim layer is optional and not Figma-backed.

findings.title: Library empty, error, info and rename states use default AppKit controls instead of the design system
findings.designEvidence: PHILOSOPHY §4: reuse the closest Figma component and never invent a new visual language. Figma Button 500:3063 (primary #301B00 with orange text, secondary #181818). Dialog chrome as in Open network stream 6216:13614.
findings.actual: The empty state (MXRLibraryView.swift:213-224) is Button('Add Folder…') rendered as a default gray push button (S43.Library/empty render). Fresh-install users see it first, together with the Home '0 items'. The error state (lines 110-114) uses a system 'Try Again' button and raw `String(describing: error)` text. The loading state (109) is a system ProgressView with a label. The folder or playlist 'Info' (LibraryPopup.swift:160-173) is a bare sheet with a system 'Done'. Rename and Delete Playlist (LibraryEntryView.swift:73-85) are system .alert dialogs. Every failure shows an alert titled 'Library action failed'.
findings.fix: Build an MXREmptyState (icon, FG/A1 title, FG/A3 hint, Figma primary Button) with copy such as 'Add a folder to start your library'. Render info and rename with DialogShell (Cancel/Save). Map errors to human messages per §9 'Use your words'.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed by the S43.Library/empty render, which shows a default gray push button 'Add Folder…' under '0 items'. Also confirmed: the system 'Try Again' plus String(describing: error), a ProgressView with a label, a bare Info sheet with a system Done, system .alert rename/delete dialogs, and the generic 'Library action failed' alerts.

findings.title: Folder ⋯ menu: 'Add File' adds to the play queue, and two of six items are always disabled in the real app
findings.designEvidence: Figma folder context menu 2139:8935: Add File, Add Folder, Edit Subtitle Tracks, Edit Audio Tracks, Resync, Info. Transcript 10:50: 'adding a file or folder here … my folder was added'.
findings.actual: LibraryPopup.swift:84 maps 'Add File' to .addFilesToQueue, which adds to the play queue, not the library. 'Edit Subtitle Tracks' is enabled only when the location is .folder (lines 86-91), which never happens with the real bridge (L01). 'Edit Audio Tracks' is hard-coded enabled:false (line 92), as is the playlist menu's 'Add Audio Tracks' (line 121).
findings.fix: Make Add File import into the library (vlc_ml_new_external_media, shown in the current category) or add to the current playlist when inside one. Enable subtitle editing for any media list. Implement or hide Edit Audio Tracks with an ⓘ explanation.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed at LibraryPopup.swift:84 (.addFilesToQueue), :86-91 (enabled only for a .folder location, which never happens with VLC), :92 and :121 (hard-coded enabled:false).

findings.title: Small token and colour deviations: compact Home and Network rows, header icons, search placeholder, sort dot
findings.designEvidence: Figma sidebar home 1106:5633 and network 858:5294: compact Home rows and saved-stream rows use FG/A3 #6B6B6B, and the Network header ⋯ and ↗ are #6B6B6B. Player-4 / Player-5: the search placeholder is FG/A4, and there is no orange dot on the sort icon in Music, Network, Home or the full-window grid.
findings.actual: Sampled from my renders: compact Home rows #969696 vs Figma #6B6B6B, Network 'Podcasts' #969696 vs #6B6B6B, ⋯/↗ #8F8F8F vs #6B6B6B. The search placeholder uses the system placeholder colour because macOS ignores `prompt: Text(...).foregroundStyle` (MXRLibraryView.swift:93-94), so it renders noticeably brighter than FG/A4 (S44 header crop). LibrarySortMenu shows the orange dot whenever sort != .titleAscending (LibraryNavigation.swift:145), adding it in Music, Network, Home and the full grid where Figma has none. Sort and view controls are shown on Home but do nothing there.
findings.fix: Use per-context row colours from the nodes. Draw the placeholder as an overlay Text, as DialogField does. Show the dot only when the sort differs from the category default, and hide or disable sort and view on Home.
findings.verifyNote: Verified with check runs. S35 and S40 rows render #8F8F8F/#969696 against Figma #6B6B6B. The search placeholder renders about #7A7A7A against Figma #404040 (FG/A4, node 6261:15138). The orange sort dot appears in S35 and S40 renders where Figma has none, but Figma S28 does show the dot for the folder's Unwatched First sort, so the rule should be 'sort differs from the category default'. Correction to the fix: Figma S40 shows sort and view icons on Home, so don't hide them; make them act on Home or dim them.

findings.title: Narrow layouts: the breadcrumb clips mid-glyph and the full-library nav card never collapses
findings.designEvidence: Spec-part1 §08 open question: the compact breadcrumb collapses ancestors to '…'. D019: product windows must adapt.
findings.actual: With compactWidth = min(427, width × 0.45 or 0.32) (MXRAppView.swift:178-180), opening the queue on a 1000-1280pt window gives about 307-409pt. The S28.Library/narrow render shows the breadcrumb as '… ▸ T ▸ S(', with letters cut off and no ellipsis (LibraryNavigation.swift:102-133: no layoutPriority or truncation strategy). The S44.Library/narrow render keeps the 202pt nav card at 480pt width, leaving about 250pt for content.
findings.fix: Give the current crumb the highest layoutPriority and tail truncation, and fold more ancestors into the '…' menu when space runs out. Below about 900pt, switch the full library nav to the 50pt icon rail.
findings.verifyNote: Verified. The S28.Library/narrow render shows '… ▸ T| ▸ S(' with glyphs clipped and no ellipsis. The S44.Library/narrow render keeps the roughly 202pt nav card at a 480pt width (the full breadcrumb truncates correctly there with 'Th...').

findings.title: Rail pins: extra divider and spacing, small radius, no reordering
findings.designEvidence: Key frame 11-playlists-home__rail-pins-recent-add__13m41.2s: pins continue directly after the categories at the same 46pt pitch, pinned media is a thumbnail in a rounded square (radius about 6), and '+' follows. Spec-part2 §11 C.
findings.actual: LibraryNavigation.swift:19-20 inserts LibraryDivider with vertical padding before the pins. Pinned media uses LibraryArtwork with radius Theme.Radius.xs (line 87). PinStore.move exists but there is no drag-to-reorder. The rail '+' offers 'Pin Home' or 'Pin Videos' for category roots, which duplicates rail items (LibraryPopup.swift:51-53).
findings.fix: Remove the divider, use the pin radius from the node, add onMove or drag reordering, and hide 'Pin' for category roots.
findings.verifyNote: The divider and padding are verified against key frame 13m41.2s, where pins follow the categories at the same pitch with no separator. The radius claim is marginal: Theme.Radius.xs is 2pt against roughly 3pt in the zoomed frame. Pin reordering is not shown in the design (§11 OPEN), so it is optional. Pinning category roots duplicates rail items: confirmed.

findings.title: No transitions for the library panel, mini player or folder navigation, while menus animate as NSPopovers (the same inconsistency as C4)
findings.designEvidence: PHILOSOPHY §3.2: panels appear on request and go away cleanly. macOS convention: sidebars slide, and Reduce Motion is respected. Owner complaint C4: the ⋯ menu animates but the bottom popovers don't.
findings.actual: MXRAppView.swift:43-103 swaps the compact library, full library and mini-player overlays with plain `if` branches and no .transition or withAnimation, so they pop in. The library menus are NSPopovers (L07) with the system animation. In the same file the tracks panel is `.overlay(alignment: .trailing)` (lines 52-59, 84-91) with no transition. That is the root cause of C2's vertically centred 'floating card mid-right' and C4's missing animation for the bottom popovers.
findings.fix: Use one motion spec: a 180-220 ms slide plus fade for side panels, Reduce Motion falling back to fade, a scale-fade for menus, and a spring snap for the mini player (already present). Anchor the tracks panel at bottom-trailing above the control bar.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed: no .transition or withAnimation for the compact library, full library or mini dock. The C2 root cause is confirmed: the tracks panel is `.overlay(alignment: .trailing)`, so it is vertically centred, while §04 MUST says 'anchored at the bottom right above the bar' and a short fade/slide is fine. That part is major for the tracks reviewer. The deeper cause is that the view tree itself swaps (see missed finding LM2).

findings.title: Saving a network stream or playlist from the app menu gives no visible result
findings.designEvidence: Transcript 13:00: after pasting a link, 'Now it's an automatic playlist with all the videos listed', shown in the library. Principle 3: feedback near where the user is looking.
findings.actual: LibraryDialogs.swift:41-43 and 162-165 call app.library.select(.network or .playlists) and dismiss the sheet, but they don't open the library. When the dialog was opened from the ⋯ app menu while watching, the sheet closes and nothing appears to happen.
findings.fix: After a save, set interface.library = .compact (if hidden), navigate to the new item and briefly highlight it.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed. Both save paths call library.select() and dismiss the sheet without presenting the library, so nothing visible happens when the dialog was opened from the app ⋯ menu during playback.

findings.title: Library view and bridge hygiene: offset identity, O(n²) current-item checks, duplicated drop code, literal paints, identity loss on drop
findings.designEvidence: AGENTS: no literal colors or sizes in views. Principle 16: everything follows the accent and theme.
findings.actual: ForEach is keyed by `id: \.offset` (MXRLibraryView.swift:135, 145, 155), so hover, popover and artwork state stays with positions when the list re-sorts or reloads. isCurrentMedia (LibrarySupport.swift:40-53) compares the whole entries and queue id arrays for every row, which is O(n²) per render. There are two drop decoders, LibraryQueueDrop (MXRMiniPlayerView.swift:233-271) and QueuePanel.acceptDrop (QueuePanel.swift:178-195). LibraryPaint (LibrarySupport.swift:32-36) hard-codes sRGB colours that ignore accent and theme, and LibraryGeometry holds literal sizes.
