Library drags carry only a URL, so dropped items become MediaItem(url:) and lose ML id, duration, thumbnail and progress. Recents are stored twice (RecentsStore recents.json and ML history).
findings.fix: Key rows by entry.id plus an occurrence index. Compute the current-media index once in LibraryModel. Share one drop payload type ('mxr-library:<id>' resolved through backend.media(id:)). Move paints and sizes to generated tokens. Choose one recent-history source.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed: `id: \.offset` at :135/:145/:155, isCurrentMedia maps both id arrays for every row, there are two drop decoders, LibraryPaint uses sRGB literals, URL-only drag payloads, and recents are stored twice. Do not break: LibraryModel's generation and moreToken cancellation, keepingLoaded reloads, and the rowIndex handling for repeated playlist occurrences are solid.

findings.title: Light-theme compact library panel paint differs from Figma
findings.designEvidence: Figma Player - Light 2425:13624 (described as a partially light-styled frame): panel #C2C2C1.
findings.actual: S72.App/light check FAILs: 24.96% of solid pixels differ (render #D5D5D5 light bgA3 vs Figma #C2C2C1). The mock also marks E04 as now playing, while Figma doesn't highlight it.
findings.fix: Confirm the intended light panel token with the owner, since Figma is partial here. If Figma wins, use the measured BG/A3 light value for the compact panel and rail and align the fixture state.
findings.verifyNote: The check FAIL (render #D5D5D5 against Figma #C2C2C1) is real, but it covers the whole chrome (top and control bars too), not only the library panel. colors.json meta says the Light frame 2425:13624 is only partially styled, so this needs an owner decision. The mock's highlight on E04 versus none in Figma was confirmed in side-by-side.png. Low priority.

findings.title: The '+ Create playlist' (Playlists) and '+ Add' (Videos/Music/Songs/folder roots) rows never appear with the real VLC backend
findings.designEvidence: VIDEO_BREAKDOWN §11 MUST: 'The Playlists category shows "+ Create playlist" first'. Figma Player.png (compact library on Playlists) shows '+ Create playlist · Cool Songs · Anime to Watch'. Key frame 11-playlists-home__playlists-category__13m24.7s. §09 MUST: Music root and folder views start with '+ Add'. Key frame 09-music__now-playing-cover-art-native__12m18.4s shows '+ Add' in My Songs.
findings.actual: MXRLibraryServices.m:274-275 sets result[@"addAction"] only when kind == 'network'. MockData.entries(at:) (MockData.swift ~322-343) returns .add for videos, music and songs and .createPlaylist for playlists, so every gallery check shows the rows while the shipped app has no create row on Playlists and no add row in any media category.
findings.fix: Return addAction from the bridge for each kind: playlists → 'createPlaylist'; videos, music, songs and entry-point folders → 'add'. Add this to the bridge/mock contract test proposed in L04.

findings.title: Opening the compact library or the track popover swaps the whole window view tree (player, top bar, control bar and video host are rebuilt)
findings.designEvidence: PHILOSOPHY §3.2: panels appear on request and go away cleanly. §08: the library opens beside the video ('never leave the video'). §04 SHOULD: a short fade/slide. Owner complaints C2 and C4 (inconsistent or missing animation).
findings.actual: MXRAppView.swift:37-41 renders MXRPlayerView (with its own top and control bars) only when library == .hidden && rightPanel == nil. Any other state switches to a different branch (:42-100) that builds new MXRTopBar and MXRControlBar instances plus a second MXRPlayerView (playerCanvas, :160-166) and re-parents videoView. Each library or track-popover toggle destroys and recreates the chrome. Hover and open-menu state reset, the seek bar's `.task(id:)` waveform load restarts, and SwiftUI cannot animate between two unrelated subtrees. That is why nothing slides. The video host is likely to flash during re-parenting; this was not observed at runtime.
findings.fix: Use one stable layout: MXRPlayerView, the top bar and the control bar are always present with stable identity. The library rail and panel, the right panels and the track popover are sibling columns or overlays shown by state with .transition(.move+.opacity) under withAnimation, falling back to a fade under Reduce Motion. Never re-parent the video host.

findings.title: The thumbnail cache ignores the requested size, so full-library grid and Home cards show tiny list thumbnails upscaled (blurry)
findings.designEvidence: Figma Player-3/Player-4 grid tiles 316×178 (970:4081) and Home cards (6272:13899) show sharp art. PHILOSOPHY: premium visual quality.
findings.actual: VLCThumbnailBackend (VLCServiceBackends.swift ~126-134) keys `cache` by media.id only. cachedArtwork and artwork return any cached image regardless of maxPixelSize. The bridge renders at the requested width (MXRThumbnailServices.m: width from args). A compact-list row asks for about 114×64 px (LibrarySupport.swift:217-225 for a 32pt thumb), so after browsing the compact library, opening the full library or Home reuses those images for 316pt (632 px) cards. Each gallery entry builds a fresh AppModel with mock thumbnails, so this never shows in checks.
findings.fix: Key the cache by (id, size bucket), for example the next power of two of the max dimension. Serve a smaller cached image only as a placeholder and request the larger one. Use an LRU (see L16).

findings.title: The row ⋯ menu for network streams, albums, artists, genres and links shows the folder header menu (Add File, Add Folder, Resync…)
findings.designEvidence: Figma has a dedicated menu per entity: file 2404:13340, folder 2139:8935, playlist 2459:9389. A saved stream collection is playlist-like (§10: 'saved streams', expanded m3u playlist).
findings.actual: LibraryEntryView.swift:55-58 handles media, playlist and folder, and every other entry falls back to MXRLibraryPopupView(kind: .folder). Hovering ⋯ on 'Podcasts' or 'Radio' or an album therefore offers Add File, Add Folder, Edit Subtitle Tracks, Edit Audio Tracks (disabled), Resync and Info. There is no Play, Shuffle, Rename or Remove for streams (also see L09).
findings.fix: Give streams a playlist-style menu: Play, Shuffle, Add to Queue, Rename, Remove (removeNetworkStream). Give albums, artists and genres Play, Shuffle, Add to Queue, Add to Playlist and Pin. Never show folder-management actions on non-folder rows.

findings.title: File menu 'Go to Source' does nothing for local files and opens network streams in the web browser
findings.designEvidence: Figma file context menu 2404:13340 'Go to Source', meaning go to where the item lives in the library. VIDEO_BREAKDOWN §08 file context menu MUST.
findings.actual: LibraryPopup.swift:106: local files need media.folder, which is always nil with VLC (L01), so the item silently does nothing. Non-file URLs go to NSWorkspace.shared.open(url), which hands an http/rtsp stream URL to Safari.
findings.fix: For local files, navigate the library to the containing folder (or the parent directory derived from the file URL, as with the chip fix in L01). For streams, navigate to the Network collection that contains the URL. Never open media URLs in the browser.

findings.title: Adding a library folder gives no feedback: the indexing state is tracked but never shown
findings.designEvidence: Transcript 10:50-11:00: 'Alright, my folder was added and I can finally watch the next episode.' Design principle: feedback near where the user is looking.
findings.actual: MXRLibraryServices tracks _indexing, and LibraryBackend.isIndexing and LibraryEvent.indexingChanged exist, but no file in MXRUI reads isIndexing. VLCLibraryBackend never emits .indexingChanged, and LibraryModel ignores it (LibraryModel.swift:315). After 'Add Folder…' the page keeps saying 'Your library is empty' with the Add Folder button (alternating with the L12 spinner) until the first items arrive.
findings.fix: Emit .indexingChanged from the backend. Show an in-design status in the header ('Adding S01… 12 items') or a progress row, and hide or disable the empty-state CTA while indexing.

findings.title: The empty state is the same for every location ('Your library is empty' plus 'Add Folder…'), including empty playlists, Recent and Network
findings.designEvidence: PHILOSOPHY §9 'Use your words'. The empty state is OPEN in §08, so macOS convention applies: context-specific copy and action.
findings.actual: MXRLibraryView.swift:213-224 shows the same title and 'Add Folder…' button for any empty location. An empty playlist, a Recent tab with no history and an empty folder all tell the user their library is empty and offer to add a folder.
findings.fix: Use per-location copy and actions: an empty playlist offers 'Drag files here' and Add Files, Recent says 'Nothing played yet', Network offers Add Network Stream, a folder says 'No media in this folder', and search keeps Clear Search. Render it with the MXREmptyState component proposed in L21.

findings.title: No native Mac navigation in the library: no ⌘[ / ⌘], ⌘F, Esc-to-close, swipe or mouse back/forward
findings.designEvidence: AGENTS hard rule: native macOS behavior with the Figma look. §08 Back/forward buttons plus a clickable address line, which Mac users also expect from the keyboard and trackpad as in Finder and Music.
findings.actual: Back and forward are only reachable through the 24pt icon buttons (MXRLibraryView.swift:54-55). Search focuses only from the icon toggle (:81-83). A grep over MXRUI and MXRPlugin finds no keyboardShortcut or menu command for library back/forward/search and no swipe or other-mouse-button handling. The compact library cannot be closed with Esc.
findings.fix: Add Go-menu commands (Back ⌘[, Forward ⌘], Find ⌘F focusing the search field) through MXRNativeMenus and AppCommand. Handle trackpad swipe and mouse buttons 4/5 in the library. Close the compact library with Esc when search is not focused.

grades.justification: Completeness 55: every runtime surface exists and basic playback works: play/pause, auto-advance, tracks, volume, fullscreen, quit. But several behaviours the design specifies are missing or wrong: bars do not reveal independently, the popover is not bottom-anchored and cannot be closed with Esc or a click outside, the elapsed label does not follow a drag, External Tracks is always empty, and there are two OSD systems. Fidelity 38: the main screen deviates on first sight. There are two top rows instead of one 40-pt bar, the cone is indented, a waveform replaces the solid seek bar on video, a purple system focus ring appears around the seek bar and the cone, and the side panels sit in their own column instead of overlaying the video. Code quality 40: protocols and models are cleanly layered. But every display frame re-evaluates the whole seek-bar body and bridges the full VLC config dictionary. Every engine event or volume tick rebuilds the whole player snapshot. One NSView instance is reused across SwiftUI representables, which mis-places the video. Benign command failures show as two error UIs at once.

doneWell: Engine integration is solid. VideoToolbox + samplebufferdisplay + AUHAL are selected, the sidecar .srt autoloads and renders, and auto-advance E01→E02 works. Precise seek on release lands on the target (pointer 32 s → frame 32.433).
Quit is clean and fast: Quit from the menu went to process gone in <0.5 s, exit 0, 'macosx_redesign interface closed', no leftover vlc-preparser.
Stopped or idle cost is fine: 0.0% CPU, 84 MB footprint (262 MB peak). Fullscreen with bars auto-hidden ~7% CPU; Hide UI 3.5%.
Native fullscreen works (button, then Esc). Bars overlay the letterbox without moving the video (b2/fs-compare.png). Reveal in ≤60 ms with a 130 ms fade; hide after the 0.5 s Figma-default delay.
The seek preview card is good: correct frame and time under the pointer during hover and drag, debounced 80 ms and quantized (b2/seek-strip.png). Keep it when fixing R3.

The track popover follows the design semantics: picking a row does not close it, the selected row gets an orange ✓, the active tab has orange icon and underline, and the bar icon turns filled orange. Track switching None ↔ Track 1 takes effect immediately.
The volume cone mapping (nonlinear, boost above 100%) and the hover tooltip chip itself match Figma 'audio value'. The outline problem is only the focus ring (R4).
The play/pause button state (orange ▶ when paused, gray ⏸ when playing) and the queue panel content ('2 items - 2m', repeat/shuffle/±, current row orange) match the design.
The user's own state is isolated by bundle id (org.example.vlc-redesign.codex), and smoke-native.py refuses to launch a stock bundle. Keep these guards.

findings.title: Top bar is pushed below the titlebar safe area: traffic lights get their own 32-pt row and the cone is indented by an empty 76-pt reserve (also in fullscreen)
findings.designEvidence: VIDEO_BREAKDOWN 03 MUST 'One thin top row'; Figma Player-6 (247:445) topBar 247:447 = 1920x40 at y=0 with the cone at x≈20; video key frame 06m24.4s and 06m21.7s show one 36-40 px row with the cone at the far left. D007/D019 allow native traffic lights, but in the same 40-pt row.
findings.actual: Runtime AX: 'Player title bar' group at window y=32..72 while the traffic lights sit at y=8..24 in an otherwise empty 32-pt strip (shots/01-launch.png, 01-top.png). Total chrome is 72 pt. In fullscreen there are no traffic lights, but the cone is still at x≈100 (shots/b2/13-topleft.png). Root cause 1: MXRAppController.swift:64-80 builds a .titled + .fullSizeContentView window with an NSHostingView root, and nothing in MXRUI or MXRPlugin calls .ignoresSafeArea, so SwiftUI lays the whole scene out under the titlebar safe-area inset. Root cause 2: PlayerBars.swift:18 always inserts Color.clear of MXRPlayerMetrics.trafficLightReserve (PlayerMetrics.swift:38, which reuses the 76-pt timeLabel token) before the cone, even though the lights are not in that row and are absent in fullscreen.
findings.fix: In MXRAppView (or the NSHostingView root in MXRAppController.start) apply .ignoresSafeArea(.container, edges: .top) so the top bar occupies y=0..40. Centre the standard window buttons vertically in the 40-pt bar: re-layout standardWindowButton(.closeButton)?.superview on windowDidResize/didEnterFullScreen, or use an empty NSToolbar with toolbarStyle .unifiedCompact and tune it. Derive the reserve from standardWindowButton(.zoomButton).frame.maxX + Figma gap, apply it only when !window.styleMask.contains(.fullScreen), and stop reusing the timeLabel token. Then verify that the cone, ⋯ and title are on one row with the traffic lights.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed. 01-launch/01-top show the traffic lights in their own empty strip with the cone at about 107 pt. In fullscreen (b2/13-topleft) the cone is still indented with no lights present. MXRAppController.swift:64-80 builds a .titled + .fullSizeContentView window with an NSHostingView root. grep finds no ignoresSafeArea, safeAreaRegions or standardWindowButton anywhere in Sources, so SwiftUI insets the whole scene below the titlebar. PlayerBars.swift:18 always inserts Color.clear(width: trafficLightReserve), and PlayerMetrics.swift:38 sets that to ControlBar.timeLabel.width (76), which is unrelated to the lights. Design evidence checked: Figma Player-6 has the cone at x≈20 in a single 40-px row, and VIDEO_BREAKDOWN 03 says 'One thin top row'. Fix as proposed. Also hide or move the standard buttons in Hide UI (see M1) and add a drag region (see M3); after the safe-area fix the top bar covers the titlebar strip that the window is currently dragged by.

findings.title: Visible control bar costs ~22-30% CPU continuously during playback (scrubbing 50-57%); whole seek bar re-evaluated every display frame
findings.designEvidence: PHILOSOPHY §2.4 'Our controls are an overlay and must not cost frames. Budgets: idle player under 1% CPU'. ARCHITECTURE §8 cited in PlaybackClock.swift: only the playhead should refresh per frame.
findings.actual: Measured on the same 1080p30 VideoToolbox clip, top -pid at 1 s intervals: windowed with bars visible (the default in a window, since bars never hide) 25-34%; Hide UI 3.4-3.6%; fullscreen with bars auto-hidden ~7%; seek-bar drag 50-57% (logs/burst2-top.txt). Main thread is busy ~43% of samples (logs/sample-playing.txt). PlayerControls.swift:387-391 PlayerDisplayLink writes @State position on every CADisplayLink tick (120 Hz ProMotion). That invalidates the entire MXRSeekBar GeometryReader body: two WaveformShape paths with hundreds of rounded rects (335-340), overlays, onChange chains, and an AppKit layout pass. Each evaluation also calls previewsEnabled (319-321) → MXRPlayerPreferences.showsSeekThumbnails → VLCSettingsBackend.value(for:) (VLCSettingsBackend.swift:19), which bridges the full VLC config NSDictionary via values.dictionary("values") on every call. That is ~13% of main-thread samples by itself.
findings.fix: Isolate the playhead: drive only a small view or CALayer, ideally a CALayer position animation computed from the timer point and rate, so there is zero per-frame Swift work. Or use TimelineView(.animation(minimumInterval: 1/30)) around just the head and fill. Set preferredFrameRateRange to 30-60. Cache the waveform as an image or drawingGroup keyed by width and samples, and move the progress mask to a cheap clip. Cache settings as [String: SettingValue] rebuilt once per settings revision, and hoist previewsEnabled out of the per-frame path. Re-measure: target <2% over Hide UI with bars visible.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed in code and in the sample. Line 389 of PlayerDisplayLink writes @State position on every tick. The display link has no preferredFrameRateRange, so it runs at the full display rate, and it is always active in a window because autohide defaults to 'fullscreen only'. Each write re-evaluates the whole MXRSeekBar GeometryReader. In sample-playing.txt the main thread is idle in 438 of 774 samples (about 43% busy). PlayerControls.swift:403, onChange(of: previewsEnabled), alone accounts for 71+30 = 101 samples (13%): it calls VLCSettingsBackend.value(for:) → values.dictionary("values"), which bridges the whole config dictionary on every call. The comment at line 469, 'Only the playhead is refreshed', is false, and ARCHITECTURE §8 explicitly forbids body re-evaluation on ticks. Caveat: load average was 12-18 while measuring, because other reviewers were running, so the absolute top % values (18-38% windowed, 50-57% while dragging) are noisy. The sample evidence holds on its own. SubtitleTimeline.swift:48 has the same issue: TimelineView(.animation) gives a per-frame body whenever the timeline is shown. Fix as proposed.

findings.title: Scrubbing sends keyframe-only FAST seeks on every drag event; picture jumps by GOP, elapsed label lags behind the pointer, playback keeps running while the button is held
findings.designEvidence: VIDEO_BREAKDOWN 02 MUST 'Hovering anywhere on the seek bar shows a floating preview card ... While dragging, the elapsed label follows.' PHILOSOPHY §3.3: thick seek bar with thumbnails while seeking.
findings.actual: Real drag across 15→20→26→32 s (shots/b2/seek-strip.png). Burned-in video frame: 8.333, 16.667, 25.000, 25.000 (keyframes only; the test GOP is 8.33 s). Elapsed label: 00:00:08, 00:00:16, 00:00:24, 00:00:24. Holding still at 32 s for 0.9 s: the video plays on from 25 → 26.133 while the pointer says 32. Only release lands correctly (32.433). Code: PlayerControls.swift:363-371 calls app.player.seek(toPosition:, precision: .fast) on every onChanged, which maps to VLC_PLAYER_SEEK_FAST (MXRServicesBridge.m:631-634). MXRTimeLabel (PlayerControls.swift:82-87) shows clock.displayTime from the engine, not the drag target. Each seek also triggers a full player-snapshot rebuild on the main thread (MXRServicesBridge.m:686).
findings.fix: While dragging, show dragPosition × length in the elapsed label: pass a scrub time through the model, e.g. app.seekPreview.time or a new clock.scrubTime. Rely on the existing preview card for the frame. Throttle engine seeks to ~10 Hz, at most one in flight, using PRECISE (or FAST, then PRECISE on idle >150 ms). Pause output during the drag and restore the previous state on release, like QuickTime. Release keeps the PRECISE seek.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed. seek-strip.png shows burned-in frames 8.333 → 16.667 → 25.000 → 25.000 (keyframes only), elapsed label 08 → 16 → 24 → 24, and the video playing on to 26.133 while held at 32. Meanwhile the preview card shows the correct 15/20/26/32. Code: PlayerControls.swift:364 sends .fast on every onChanged → VLC_PLAYER_SEEK_FAST (MXRServicesBridge.m:631-634). MXRTimeLabel:84 reads clock.displayTime. Each seek rebuilds the snapshot at least twice: the synchronous changed:@"player" at MXRServicesBridge.m:686, plus VLCPlayerBackend.send() calling reload(). This breaks the VIDEO_BREAKDOWN 02 MUST 'While dragging, the elapsed label follows'. Fix as proposed. Show the drag time in the label; throttle seeks with one in flight; optionally pause during the scrub.

findings.title: System focus ring (owner's purple accent) drawn around volume cone + tooltip and around the seek bar; persists after the pointer leaves
findings.designEvidence: Figma 'audio value' (2245:9805, renders/audio value.png): dark chip, no stroke, soft shadow. No element in Figma has an accent outline. VIDEO_BREAKDOWN 01: active state is orange; no focus rectangles.
findings.actual: Reproduced: drag on the cone produced a square purple ring enclosing the '104 %' / '72 %' tooltip and the cone. It stays as an empty purple box over the video after the pointer moves away (shots/b1/vol-strip.png, b1/05-volume-away.png, b1/06-cmd-up.png). The seek bar shows the same ring at launch and after any click (shots/01-seek.png, b2 drag frames). The owner's AppleAccentColor=5 (purple) explains the colour. Root cause: .focusable() on MXRVolumeCone (PlayerControls.swift:179) and MXRSeekBar (PlayerControls.swift:413) with the default focus effect. SwiftUI draws the macOS focus ring around the full modified view, including the tooltip overlay at 172-178. The seek bar also becomes the window's initial key view.
findings.fix: Add .focusEffectDisabled() to both. Draw a token-based focus indicator only when keyboard focus is real (FocusState + NSApp.isFullKeyboardAccessEnabled), or drop .focusable() and keep arrow handling in the app key monitor or accessibilityAdjustableAction. Move the tooltip into a separate overlay outside the focusable view so it never enlarges the hit or focus rect.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed visually. b1/vol-strip.png shows a square purple ring around the cone plus tooltip, and it stays as an empty box after the pointer leaves. 01-launch shows the same ring around the seek bar at launch. Cause: .focusable() at PlayerControls.swift:179 and :413 with the default focus effect, with the tooltip overlay at 172-178 placed before .focusable(). Figma 'audio value' (2245:9805) is a borderless chip with a shadow. More .focusable() sites will show the same ring: SettingsEqualizerView.swift:68, SettingsControls.swift:301, MXRCustomizationView.swift:73. Fix as proposed (.focusEffectDisabled, or drop focusable in favour of accessibilityAdjustableAction plus the key monitor).

findings.title: Track popover is vertically centred on the right edge of the video instead of anchored bottom-right 20 pt above the control bar
findings.designEvidence: Figma Controls variant 'subtitles' 491:2216: popup 491:2243 = 400x524 at (1500,-544) relative to the 54-pt bar, so the bottom edge is 20 pt above the bar and the right inset is 20 (crop shots/figma-controls-subtitles.png). Video 06m21.7s key frame shows the same. VIDEO_BREAKDOWN 04 MUST 'anchored at the bottom right above the bar'.
findings.actual: Runtime: the popover floats mid-right (window y≈290-815 of 1084) in windowed mode and fullscreen (shots/04-subs-popover.png, b2/08-subs.png, b3/08-fs-hidden-small.png). Root cause: MXRAppView.swift:52-59 and 84-92 use .overlay(alignment: .trailing), which centres vertically, with only trailing padding.
findings.fix: Use .overlay(alignment: .bottomTrailing) with .padding(.bottom, 20).padding(.trailing, 20) from tokens, inside the video frame, so the panel's bottom sits 20 pt above the bar in all layouts including fullscreen. Use the same anchor for the sidebar and queue (see R7).
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed. In Figma, 491:2216 places 491:2243 (400x524) at (1500,-544) relative to the 54-pt bar, giving bottom 20 pt above the bar and right inset 20. The 06m21.7 frame matches. MXRAppView.swift:52-59 and 84-92 use .overlay(alignment: .trailing) with only trailing padding, which centres the panel vertically. The gallery entry S14.App/subtitle-tracks reproduces the mid-right placement (rendered to review/native-runtime-verify/s14-app.png). It has no Figma node, so mxr-snapshot check never caught it (see M4). Fix as proposed.

findings.title: Inconsistent panel presentation: ⋯ menu is an animated NSPopover with an arrow, bottom panels appear with no transition and cannot be dismissed by Esc or click-outside; clicking the video pauses instead
findings.designEvidence: VIDEO_BREAKDOWN 04 SHOULD 'Clicking outside or pressing Esc closes the popover. A short fade/slide is fine'. Figma menu.png (6062:13354) is a flat rounded panel with no arrow.
findings.actual: ⋯ uses SwiftUI .popover (PlayerBars.swift:212-213), so it gets the system NSPopover scale/fade (60-ms capture is half-transparent, shots/b2/menu-strip.png), an arrow and the popover material (10-menu-top.png). Track, sidebar and queue panels are a plain branch or overlay swap with no .transition. With the popover open: Esc left it open; the AX tree still had 'Embedded Tracks' after keyg 53 (b3/07). The key went to the shortcut monitor (MXRAppController.swift:102-115), which only shows a 'Pressed esc' OSD (b2/10-crop.png). The only Esc hook is .onExitCommand on MXRRightPanelView (TrackPopover.swift:19), which needs focus inside the panel, and it never has focus. Clicking the video left the popover open and toggled pause through MXRVideoHost.mouseDown → onSingleClick (MXRVideoHost.swift:33-45; MXRAppController.swift:205-211), with VLC's own ⏸ icon OSD drawn (b2/09-crop.png). The panel only closes by clicking the same bar icon (InterfaceModel.toggle).
findings.fix: Pick one presentation system: custom overlay surfaces for ⋯ and all right panels, with one shared transition, e.g. .transition(.opacity.combined(with: .offset(y: 8))) and withAnimation(.easeOut(duration: 0.14)) in InterfaceModel open/close, honouring reduce motion. Add a transparent full-window dismiss layer under an open panel that consumes the click (closeRightPanel without pausing). Handle Esc in the key monitor first when rightPanel != nil or the ⋯ menu is open. Drop the NSPopover arrow and material for the ⋯ menu.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed. The ⋯ menu is a SwiftUI .popover (PlayerBars.swift:212-213): system scale/fade and an arrow, visible in b2/menu-strip.png. The Figma menu.png panel has no arrow. A grep for .transition/withAnimation in MXRAppView, Panels/* and InterfaceModel finds none, so the right panels pop in and out. The only Esc hook is .onExitCommand in TrackPopover.swift:19. The local key monitor (MXRAppController.swift:102-115) sees Esc first and runs VLC's leave-fullscreen hotkey, a no-op in a window, which only draws 'Pressed esc' (b2/10-crop). A video click goes MXRVideoHost.mouseDown → onSingleClick → playPause (MXRAppController.swift:205-211); the engine pause icon appears and the popover stays (b2/09-crop). Breakdown 04 SHOULD (click outside or Esc closes; short fade) is unmet, and the inconsistency complaint (C4) is valid. Fix as proposed.

findings.title: Settings sidebar and queue panel are laid out as a separate HStack column that shrinks the video, producing a 'window inside a window'
findings.designEvidence: Figma Controls 'playback' variant 2238:9432: sidebar 5187:24308 = 400x946 at (1500,-966), i.e. it overlays the video 20 pt below the top bar, 20 pt above the control bar and 20 pt from the right (shots/figma-controls-playback.png). Video 15m16.7s key frame shows the panel floating over the full-width video frame. VIDEO_BREAKDOWN 07 SHOULD 'The sidebar overlays the right side of the video ... It does not push or shrink the video.'
findings.actual: Opening the gear or Queue shrinks the rounded video frame to x≤1300 pt. The panel sits in its own gutter column with its own inset and window-colour background (shots/08-sidebar.png, 16-queue-panel.png, 09-library-plus-sidebar.png). Root cause: MXRAppView.swift:93-98 'if reservesPanelSpace { MXRRightPanelView().frame(width: panelWidth(...)).padding(.vertical/.trailing, panelInset) }' as an HStack sibling of playerCanvas (reservesPanelSpace 169-174 is true for .sidebar and .queue). Toggling it also switches the whole SwiftUI branch (37-103), which contributes to R10.
findings.fix: Render sidebar and queue in the same bottomTrailing overlay of the video frame as the tracks popover: 400 pt wide, top inset 20 below the top bar, bottom 20 above the bar, using the translucent PanelSurface over the video. Keep the video frame full width. If D019's responsive yield is wanted, apply it only when the window is narrower than ~2× panel width. Keep a single composition branch so the video host is not re-parented.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed. MXRAppView.swift:93-98 adds MXRRightPanelView as an HStack sibling of playerCanvas for .sidebar/.queue, so the video frame shrinks (08-sidebar.png, 09-library-plus-sidebar.png). In Figma, 2238:9432 places 5187:24308 (400x946) at (1500,-966): it floats over the video 20 pt below the top bar, 20 pt above the bar, inset 20 from the right. Key frame 15m16.7 shows the full-width rounded video frame with the panel inside it. VIDEO_BREAKDOWN:347 SHOULD says it 'does not push or shrink the video'. ARCHITECTURE §3.3 also says the sidebar overlays the video. D019's 'yield space' covers panel widths at small sizes, not a separate column. Fix as proposed. Use one stable composition, which also removes a branch switch behind R10.

findings.title: Two unrelated OSD systems: VLC's engine OSD (top-right, freetype) shows volume/pause/track while the redesign OSD (top-left) only shows 'Pressed <key>'
findings.designEvidence: VIDEO_BREAKDOWN 13 MUST 'OSD feedback for shortcuts shows two lines: the action (e.g. Crop: 2.35:1), then Pressed C' as one OSD (key frame 15m27.1s). VIDEO_BREAKDOWN 02: the volume value shown is the Figma 'audio value' chip.
findings.actual: Runtime: AXDecrement on volume drew the engine 'Volume: 118%' in large freetype text top-right (shots/07-volume-ax.png). Cmd+Up drew 'Pressed ⌘↑' top-left from the UI and a separate engine 'Volume: N%' top-right (b1/06-cmd-up.png). Pausing drew VLC's ⏸ icon (b2/09-crop.png). Track change drew 'Subtitle track: N/A' / 'Track 1' (b3/b3-grid.png). The tooltip chip is a third indicator. Root cause: the engine OSD comes from vlc_player itself (src/player/aout.c:94 vlc_player_osd_Volume; osd.c icon/track messages) and is never suppressed. VLCOSDBackend (VLCServiceBackends.swift:229-235) listens for an 'osd' service that the bridge never emits (no @"osd" anywhere in module/), so OSDModel.engineDisplayed never fires. The UI only ever shows the key (ServiceModels.swift keyPressed / show(nil, pressedKey:)). It even shows 'Pressed esc' for an Esc that did nothing.
findings.fix: Disable engine OSD for this interface without touching the engine: at bridge init do var_Create(player, "osd", VLC_VAR_BOOL); var_SetBool(player, "osd", false). vouts inherit it and subtitles are unaffected. Then generate UI OSD text in AppModel from player events (volume/mute, rate, track selection, hotkey seeks, snapshot), paired with the pending key, in one designed surface. Show the volume chip during hover/drag and the OSD for keys and scroll, never both. Only show 'Pressed X' when the action did something.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed. There is no @"osd" emission anywhere in module/bridge, so VLCOSDBackend's listener (VLCServiceBackends.swift:232) never fires. Engine OSD comes from vlc_player_osd_Volume (src/player/aout.c:94/103) and from the icon and track messages, gated only by var_InheritBool(vout,"osd") (video_text.c:99, video_widgets.c:289). b3-grid shows 'Subtitle track: N/A'/'Track 1' in engine freetype at top right. b1/06-cmd-up shows 'Pressed ⌘↑' from the UI at top left, and the clipped engine Volume OSD at top right. Note that the global 'osd' config option is also what the redesign maps to 'Show feedback for shortcuts' (AppModel+Preferences.swift:69). Suppress through a player-object variable (var_Create/var_SetBool on the player), not by changing that config value, so the user's toggle keeps driving the UI OSD. Also VLCOSDBackend.showMessage both draws via vout_OSDText and emits locally, which would double up if anything ever called showEngineMessage. Fix as proposed.

findings.title: Seek bar over normal video renders as a waveform of dense vertical ticks because 'Show Waveform on Seekbar' defaults to ON and its toggle is buried
findings.designEvidence: VIDEO_BREAKDOWN 02 MUST: thick seek bar with black track, dark accent-tinted elapsed fill and orange capsule handle (Figma Player-6, Controls default 491:1779). The waveform is a separate Controls variant (2139:8124) meant for music (09). Video 09m17.5s: 'Show Waveform on Seekbar' is a top-level Playback toggle shown OFF.
findings.actual: Every video with audio shows the tick waveform with an orange-tick 'fill' (shots/01-seek.png, 03-subs-popover.png). Root cause: InterfaceModel.swift:161 'public var showWaveform = true'. PlayerControls.swift:420-426 fetches a waveform for any media, and 326-340 swap the thick bar for WaveformShape. The toggle is hidden in a 'Display' expander (SettingsSidebar.swift:121-126); the Playback tab instead shows 'Show Statistics' and no 'Show Metadata' toggle (shots/08-sidebar.png).
findings.fix: Default showWaveform = false and persist the user's choice. Draw the waveform only when the toggle is on, and optionally default it on for audio-only media per section 09. Put the toggle at top level in the design order: Subtitle Timeline, Waveform, Metadata, (Reverse hidden), Sleep Timer, Visualizer, Speed.
findings.verifyNote: Main claim confirmed. InterfaceModel.swift:161 has showWaveform = true, and PlayerControls.swift:326-340 swaps the solid bar for WaveformShape on every video with audio (01-launch.png). That contradicts the solid thick bar in Figma Player-6 and the 09m17.5 frame, where the toggle is OFF. Correction to the evidence: the Figma Playback variant (2238:9432 / 5187:24308) does show 'Show Statistics' and 'Reverse' and does NOT show Waveform or Metadata. Only the video frame (09m17.5) has Waveform and Metadata. So 'Show Statistics' is Figma-sanctioned and should stay. The fix order should merge both sources: Subtitle Timeline, Waveform, Metadata, Statistics, (Reverse hidden per D014), Sleep Timer, Visualizer, Speed. Moving Waveform out of the 'Display' expander (SettingsSidebar.swift:121-126) to top level is still right (breakdown 07 MUST list).

findings.title: Video picture is displaced after toggling Hide UI (top of picture and engine OSD cut off under the top bar, black band above the control bar) until another layout change
findings.designEvidence: VIDEO_BREAKDOWN 03 MUST: the video must not jump. Figma Player-6 shows the full picture inside the framed area.
findings.actual: Reproduced twice. After Hide UI on → off, the burned-in timestamp at the picture's top-left disappears, the picture is shifted up by ~40 pt, and a black band appears above the control bar. The engine 'Volume' OSD is clipped at the top (shots/b3/03-hideui-off.png vs 01-play.png; b1/06-cmd-up.png and 06-topright.png). Opening the tracks popover, which is another branch switch, restored it (b3/04). Root cause: MXRAppView.swift:37-103 swaps whole view branches (isUIHidden / panels / default), and each creates a new MXRNativeVideoView representable. MXRVideoHost.swift:68-72 returns the same persistent MXRVideoHostView from makeNSView for every instance, so SwiftUI hosts one NSView in two containers during the transition and the surface keeps a stale frame.
findings.fix: Keep exactly one representable for the video. Compose a single stable ZStack where hide-UI, panels and library change only overlay opacity, padding and frames, not the branch. Or host the video NSView outside SwiftUI as a sibling AppKit view behind the NSHostingView, positioned from a reported anchor frame. Also set surface.frame in setFrameSize/viewDidMoveToSuperview, not only in layout().
findings.verifyNote: Visual symptom confirmed. In b3-grid frame 3 (and b3/03-hideui-off.png), after Hide UI off the burned-in timestamp is gone, the picture is shifted up and a black band sits above the bar. Opening the popover restores it. The cited mechanism is plausible but not proven. MXRAppView.swift:37-103 switches the root branch on isUIHidden, panels and library, and each branch creates a new MXRNativeVideoView. MXRVideoHost.swift:70 returns the same persistent host from every makeNSView, so one NSView moves between platform containers and keeps a stale surface frame from the hide-UI layout, where the video fills the whole window inset. Fix direction is correct: one stable representable, or an AppKit sibling video view as ARCHITECTURE §3.3 prescribes. Verify by logging host/surface frames across the toggle.

findings.title: Top and bottom bars reveal and hide together; pointer near the bottom also shows the top bar (fullscreen)
findings.designEvidence: VIDEO_BREAKDOWN 03 MUST 'Bars show and hide independently. The pointer near the top reveals the top bar only (03m51.0), and near the bottom reveals the control bar only (03m53.0).'
findings.actual: Fullscreen, pointer moved to the bottom edge: both bars visible at +60 ms and +400 ms (shots/b2/15-bars.png). Pointer at the top also showed both (b2/19-fs-top.png). Timing otherwise OK: reveal ≤60 ms with a 130 ms fade, hidden by +1000 ms after leaving (0.5 s delay matches the Figma setting default). Root cause: PlayerView.swift:96-106 folds nearTop || nearBottom into one pointerNearControls, and a single app.interface.areBarsVisible drives both bars (30-35, 68-80). MXRAppView.swift:132-151 also uses one barsVisible.
findings.fix: Track topVisible and bottomVisible separately (InterfaceModel.areTopBarVisible / areControlBarVisible), each with its own hide task. Panels and paused state pin both. The display link should run only while the control bar is visible.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed. PlayerView.swift:101-103 folds nearTop || nearBottom into one flag, and a single interface.areBarsVisible drives both bars (30-35, 68-80; MXRAppView.swift:132-151). Key frames 03m51.0 (top only) and 03m53.0 (bottom only) and the breakdown 03 MUST show independent reveal. b2/15-bars shows both bars in fullscreen with the pointer at the bottom. Fix as proposed.

findings.title: Sidecar/added subtitles listed as embedded 'Track 1'; External Tracks section is always empty
findings.designEvidence: Figma 491:2243 / Controls subtitles variant: External Tracks lists 'The_Wand_S01_EN.srt'. Video 06m21.7s shows the same. VIDEO_BREAKDOWN 04/06: after Add Subtitles, files appear under External Tracks.
findings.actual: The .srt was autodetected (run log 'autodetected subtitle ... priority 4') and rendered, but the popover shows it under Embedded Tracks as 'Track 1', with External Tracks empty (shots/06-play-after-end.png, b2/08-subs.png). Root cause: Tracks() in MXRServicesBridge.m:71-82 never sets an 'external' key, so VLCPlayerBackend.swift:40 isExternal is always false and TracksModel.externalTracks filters to nothing. The names also lack language and filename.
findings.fix: Mark tracks whose ES comes from a slave or associated input: str_id prefixed with a source hash, e.g. 'b7216…/spu/0' vs 'spu/1', or keep the URLs added via vlc_player_AddAssociatedMedia and sub-autodetect from input_item slaves. Emit external=YES, url, and a display name of filename [Language].
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed. ffprobe shows the test mp4 contains only h264 and aac streams, and run1.log:602 autodetects the .srt, so the popover's embedded 'Track 1' is the sidecar file. Tracks() at MXRServicesBridge.m:71-82 never sets 'external' or 'url', so VLCPlayerBackend.swift:40 isExternal is always false and TracksModel.swift:58 externalTracks is always empty. Names also lack the language: the 06m21.7 frame shows 'Track 1 - English' and 'The_Wand_S01E04 [English]'. Fix as proposed. In VLC 4, slave ES str_ids carry their source's id prefix, while sub-autodetect slaves and vlc_player_AddAssociatedMedia URLs are known to the bridge.

findings.title: Pressing Play with an empty queue raises a native 'VLC operation failed' alert AND leaves a persistent 'The play queue is empty or cannot start. Retry Playback' card
findings.designEvidence: No such state in Figma. PHILOSOPHY §4: reuse existing components and never invent a new visual language. The empty state is the cone + 'Open a media file'.
findings.actual: Reproduced on launch with no media: AXPress Play → alert sheet plus a card behind it, and after OK the card stays over the empty state with a system .bordered button (shots/b4/empty-pair.png, b4/03-card.png). Root cause: PlayerModel.togglePlayPause → 'play' → vlc_playlist_Start fails when the player has no media (MXRServicesBridge.m:591-599). VLCPlayerBackend.send stores commandError, which becomes errorMessage (VLCPlayerBackend.swift:139-148) and renders the card (PlayerView.swift:156-161). transport.report() also shows the alert (VLCServiceBackends.swift:76-79). 'Retry Playback' calls play() again and fails the same way. The play button stays enabled with an empty queue.
findings.fix: If the queue is empty, make Play or Space open the file panel (interface.request(.openFiles)) or do nothing. If stopped with items but no current media, call vlc_playlist_PlayAt(current >= 0 ? current : 0). Disable or dim Play when there is nothing to play. Reserve the in-video error card for real input errors (on_error_changed), styled with Figma components. Never show both card and alert.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed. b4/empty-pair.png shows the 'VLC operation failed' sheet plus the card behind it. The play path is MXRServicesBridge.m:597 vlc_playlist_Start, which fails and is turned into the 'empty or cannot start' error. VLCPlayerBackend.send stores commandError (exposed as errorMessage at line 33) and also calls transport.report, which shows the alert. PlayerView.swift:156-161 then shows a card with a system .bordered 'Retry Playback' that repeats the same failing call. This is the first thing a new user may press (Space or Play on an empty window). Fix as proposed.

findings.title: Whole player snapshot is rebuilt and diffed on the main thread for every statistics tick (1 Hz), every seek and every volume drag event
findings.designEvidence: PHILOSOPHY §2.4 budgets; ARCHITECTURE §2.3 'copy what it needs'.
findings.actual: on_statistics_changed (MXRServicesBridge.m:212) and the aout volume callback (245) call dispatchChange("player"). Every command (686, 601-607) also calls changed:"player". That fires LiveVLCServiceTransport → VLCPlayerBackend.reload(), which calls playerSnapshot: all tracks, titles, chapters, programs, effects (MXREffectsServices snapshot), statistics, NSDictionary equality over 25 key groups. A single volume drag event therefore rebuilds it twice, and statistics do so every second even when 'Show Statistics' is off (visible in logs/sample-playing.txt as MXRServicesBridge changed:/playerSnapshot/MappedSnapshot). MXRAppController.swift:94-101 also runs remoteControl.refresh and PiP updates on every 250-ms timer tick.
findings.fix: Split the 'player' service into granular keys (transport/volume, tracks, titles, effects, stats). Register for statistics only while the Statistics row is visible. Coalesce dispatchChange per runloop turn. Update volume from the callback value without a full snapshot. Refresh Now Playing only on state, rate or seek changes, since MPNowPlayingInfo interpolates.
findings.verifyNote: Accurate in code but downgraded. on_statistics_changed goes through PLAYER_CB to dispatchChange("player") with no coalescing (MXRServicesBridge.m:164-212, 399-402). A volume command actually triggers three snapshot builds: the synchronous changed: at :606, the reload() in VLCPlayerBackend.send, and the async aout callback at :48. The 250-ms vlc_player timer (MXRPlayerBridge.m:252) runs playerTimeDidChange → remoteControl.refresh. Measured steady-state cost is small: the snapshot/reload path is about 7 of 774 main-thread samples, roughly 1%. The user-visible cost is mostly R2, so treat this as part of the R2 performance work, not a standalone major.

findings.title: Library Home header says '0 items' while listing Continue Watching / Listen Again from recents (with duplicate names and an audio file under Continue Watching)
findings.designEvidence: Figma sidebar 'home' variant (848:1996, renders/sidebar.png): '110 items' header consistent with the listed library.
findings.actual: Runtime: '0 items' above Continue Watching (Test Show S01E02.mp4 ×2 from different folders, audio-control-60s.wav) and Listen Again (the same wav) (shots/09-library-plus-sidebar.png). Root cause: LibraryModel.swift:155 and :175 set totalCount = backend.mediaCount, the media-library count (0, nothing indexed), while homeSections come from recents.
findings.fix: On Home, hide the count when the library is not indexed or show the count of what is listed. Offer 'Add a folder' when the ML is empty. Disambiguate same-name recents with the parent folder. Keep audio out of Continue Watching.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed. LibraryModel.swift:155/175 set totalCount = backend.mediaCount (0, nothing indexed) while homeSections come from recents. 09-library-plus-sidebar.png shows '0 items' with S01E02 twice and the wav under Continue Watching. Minor and partly library-area. Fix as proposed.

findings.title: In fullscreen the revealed control bar covers bottom subtitles
findings.designEvidence: VIDEO_BREAKDOWN 03: bars overlay the video in fullscreen. The design shows bars over the picture; subtitles should stay readable.
findings.actual: Fullscreen, pointer at the bottom: 'Another subtitle cue.' is cut by the bar (shots/b2/15-bars.png). The video correctly does not jump (b2/fs-compare.png).
findings.fix: While the control bar is visible in fullscreen, raise the SPU margin (vout 'sub-margin' var) by the bar height, or render subtitles in a safe area, and restore it on hide.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed in b2/15-bars: the bottom cue is cut by the revealed bar in fullscreen, while the video correctly stays put. The design does not specify this, so it is a polish item. Raising the vout 'sub-margin' variable while the bar is visible needs no engine change.

findings.title: Seek bar and volume cone are exposed to VoiceOver as AXUnknown, not sliders
findings.designEvidence: PHILOSOPHY §2.3 Native first: VoiceOver.
findings.actual: AX dump: 'Playback position' and 'Volume' have role AXUnknown with AXIncrement/AXDecrement actions (logs/ax-02.txt). Elapsed time is also AXUnknown.
findings.fix: Add .accessibilityRepresentation { Slider(...) } or the slider trait/role so they announce as adjustable sliders with value text.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed. ax-02.txt lines 14/15/18 show Elapsed time, Playback position and Volume as AXUnknown with v='' (the value is not exposed either). Fix with .accessibilityRepresentation { Slider } or the adjustable trait plus a value.

findings.title: Network services discovery (SAP, UPnP, Bonjour) starts at launch even when the Network category is never opened
findings.designEvidence: PHILOSOPHY §2.4: cold start no slower than stock; avoid unneeded work.
findings.actual: run3.log line ~75: bonjour discovery starts immediately, and 23 'cannot join multicast group' errors appear per run. The provider is created eagerly in MXRDiscoveryServices.m:255.
findings.fix: Create media-source discovery lazily when the Network category or Open Network UI is shown, and stop it when hidden.
findings.verifyNote: Confirmed. MXRDiscoveryServices.m:255-262 obtains the provider at init, and loadSources (301-321) calls vlc_media_source_provider_GetMediaSource for every listed SD. run3.log:73-78 shows Bonjour starting at launch with 23 'cannot join multicast' lines, and the sample has vlc-sap/vlc-podcast threads. Make it lazy as proposed.

findings.title: Hide UI keeps a 32-pt titlebar band with permanently visible traffic lights above the video
findings.designEvidence: Figma 'Player - hide UI' 3328:11554 (gallery S06.App/hidden; crop runtime/shots/figma-hideui-small.png) shows only the rounded video inside a uniform thin frame. VIDEO_BREAKDOWN 05 MUST: 'Hide UI removes all chrome, leaving only the video.' Breakdown 03 MUST: when bars are hidden in a window, only the rounded video remains inside a thin frame.
findings.actual: runtime/shots/b3/02-hideui-on.png: with Hide UI on, the red/yellow/green buttons stay in an empty dark strip about 32 pt tall above the video frame, so the frame is thick at the top and thin elsewhere. Causes: the same titlebar safe-area inset as R1 (no ignoresSafeArea in MXRAppView or the MXRAppController NSHostingView), and nothing ever hides or fades standardWindowButton(.closeButton/.miniaturizeButton/.zoomButton); grep finds no standardWindowButton in Sources.
findings.fix: Once R1 makes the scene ignore the top safe area, hide the three standard buttons (button.superview alpha 0 / isHidden) while interface.isUIHidden. Reveal them on hover near the top-left like QuickTime's chromeless mode, or keep them hidden until Hide UI is toggled off. Use the same uniform Window.videoArea.padding on all four sides.

findings.title: App shortcuts are bound to the Control key on macOS (⌃O, ⌃P, ⌃\) and spelled 'Ctrl + O' in the ⋯ menu
findings.designEvidence: VIDEO_BREAKDOWN 05 SHOULD (macOS): 'Map Ctrl to ⌘ in displayed shortcuts' and 'Hide UI is ⌘\'. PHILOSOPHY §2.3 Native first ('the manners are macOS'). VLC's own macOS reserved hotkeys are Command-based (src/libvlc-module.c:2290-2300: preferences Command+, · open Command+o · open network Command+n; KEY_TOGGLE_FULLSCREEN Command+f).
findings.actual: ShortcutValues.swift:186-200 defines app actions with key("Ctrl+\\"), key("Ctrl+o"), key("Ctrl+f"), key("Ctrl+n"), key("Ctrl+p") and so on. KeyBinding parses 'ctrl' as .control (ShortcutValues.swift:39). MXRNativeMenus.swift:181-182 mirrors those bindings into the macOS menu bar, which shows ⌃O / ⌃P instead of ⌘O / ⌘,. The ⋯ menu shows 'Ctrl + O … Ctrl + P' (runtime/shots/b2/menu-strip.png). Open Folder on Ctrl+F sits next to the engine's Command+F fullscreen, which is confusing.
findings.fix: On macOS, default the app actions to Command: ⌘O open, ⌘⇧O folder, ⌘N network, ⌘, Settings, ⌘\ Hide UI, and so on. Render them with ⌘⇧⌥⌃ glyphs in the ⋯ and right-click menus and in the shortcuts dialog. Keep the spelled 'Ctrl + X' form only for non-Apple builds. Migrate any stored macosx-redesign-key-* values that still hold the old Ctrl defaults.

findings.title: The top bar is not a window drag or zoom region; after the R1 fix the window would have nothing to drag by
findings.designEvidence: VIDEO_BREAKDOWN 03 SHOULD (macOS): 'The top bar is the window drag region.' spec-part1 §03 open questions: the top bar 'should be the window drag region'.
findings.actual: No isMovableByWindowBackground, WindowDragGesture, mouseDownCanMoveWindow or window.performDrag(with:) anywhere in Sources (grep). MXRTopBar (PlayerBars.swift:33-39) is an opaque SwiftUI Rectangle/backdrop in the content view. Today the window can only be dragged by the empty 32-pt titlebar strip that R1 complains about. Once the scene ignores the safe area, that strip disappears, and double-click-to-zoom on the title area also goes away. Not exercised at runtime; this is based on the code.
findings.fix: Give the top bar's background (not its buttons) a drag behaviour: WindowDragGesture() on macOS 15+, or an NSViewRepresentable background whose mouseDown calls window.performDrag(with:) and whose double-click honours AppleActionOnDoubleClick (zoom or minimize). Apply the same to the empty bar area in the full-library layout. Verify by dragging and double-clicking the title text and the empty space between ⋯ and the title.

findings.title: The visual-check pipeline never runs the runtime composition, so R1/R4/R5/R7 pass in the gallery while the real window is wrong
findings.designEvidence: AGENTS.md: 'Every UI change is checked visually against its Figma render.' Controls variants 491:2216 (subtitles popup at 1500,-544), 2238:9432 (playback sidebar at 1500,-966) and the queue variant give exact placement references.
findings.actual: `mxr-snapshot list` shows no Figma node for S14.App/subtitle-tracks, S20.App/subtitle-settings, S22.App/queue, S28.App/compact or S46.App/mini-player, so `check` cannot compare panel placement. Rendering S14.App/subtitle-tracks (review/native-runtime-verify/s14-app.png) shows the same mid-right popover as the app. AppGallery.swift:105 builds MXRAppView(videoView:mediaBackdrop:) without reservesTrafficLights, a titled window or a safe area, and no focus engine runs during the static render. The 72-pt double chrome, the purple focus rings and the column sidebar therefore never show up in gallery diffs. This explains the owner's 'looks right at first glance but behaves differently'.
findings.fix: Attach the Controls variant nodes to the app-level panel entries, with a bottom-right region crop or a placement assertion: panel maxY = bar minY − 20 and maxX = width − 20. Add a snapshot mode that hosts MXRAppView in a real NSWindow (.titled + .fullSizeContentView, 1920x1080, key window) and captures it with cacheDisplay, so safe-area insets, traffic lights and focus effects appear in renders. Add a cheap geometry unit test that the top bar's frame.minY == 0.
